家庭背景、教育与文化姐妹的教育经历如何通向艺术收藏

Their / the sisters 指 Gwendoline 和 Margaret Davies。这段叙述两人的成长、教育及文化活动；philanthropic 表示与慈善有关。

Their religious upbringing in rural Wales gave them a deep sense of social responsibility and they chose to use their inheritance for cultural and philanthropic* purposes.

While there was no real family history of art collecting, the sisters’ education was rigorously geared toward such pursuits. Their London school focused on cultural rather than academic study, and they travelled extensively with their governess, Jane Blaker, visiting art galleries and making extensive notes on the collections there.
需要时看词汇注释
  • upbringing：成长中的教养与环境
  • geared toward：面向、为某一方向作准备
  • philanthropic：慈善的；帮助他人的

食物消费与贸易糖不只是餐桌上的食物

这是一篇历史著作的书评开头，讨论糖的生产、贸易地位、补贴及影响。

Ulbe Bosma’s The World of Sugar is a genuinely global history. Bosma discusses all the sugar-growing places of the world, beginning with Cuba and Java, the largest exporters of the early 20th century. But this is a history not just of cane sugar but also of beet sugar, an equally important form of traded sugar over the last hundred years. Beet sugar is grown mainly in Europe and the United States. It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.
需要时看词汇注释
  • cane sugar / beet sugar：甘蔗糖／甜菜糖
  • subsidised：获得补贴的
  • livelihood：生计、维持生活的收入来源

科技、工作与公共服务有算法之外，还需要什么

本段分析公共部门采用 AI 所需的条件：技术、数据管理、组织协作与人员能力。注意 typically 的限定作用。

AI systems need a lot of data to function, but the public sector typically does not have the appropriate data infrastructure to support advanced machine learning. Most of the data remains stored in offline archives. The few digitised sources of data that exist tend to be buried in bureaucracy. More often than not, data is spread across different government departments that each require special permissions to be accessed. Above all, the public sector typically lacks the human talent with the right technological capabilities to fully reap the benefits of machine intelligence.
需要时看词汇注释
  • data infrastructure：支撑数据存储、管理和使用的基础设施
  • the public sector：公共部门
  • reap the benefits of：获得……带来的益处

环境与资源保护一种动物，也保护它所在的生态系统

本段介绍一项保护项目及其在 2022 年的进展，涉及生态系统修复、生物多样性与跨组织合作。

Recent efforts to save the saiga have been spearheaded by the Altyn Dala Conservation Initiative, a project led by the Association for the Conservation of Biodiversity of Kazakhstan, working in partnership with the Kazakh government’s Committee for Forestry and Wildlife, Frankfurt Zoological Society and Fauna and Flora, an international conservation charity. Its purpose is to protect and restore Kazakhstan’s steppe, semi-desert and desert ecosystems and the many species they support, including the critically endangered saiga. In 2022 the United Nations recognised the initiative as a World Restoration Flagship project, an accolade reserved for the ten best examples of large-scale ecosystem restoration around the globe.
需要时看词汇注释
  • spearheaded by：由……牵头推动
  • working in partnership with：与……合作开展工作
  • ecosystem restoration：生态系统修复

城市、交通与日常服务从买票到上车：交通设施中的可达性

开头 It 指达累斯萨拉姆；DART 是文中讨论的快速公交系统。关注上车流程、无障碍设计与携婴出行。

It has chosen a less exciting but cheaper and more achievable method: the bus.

The DART bus rapid transit (BRT) system runs on bus lanes separated from other traffic, mostly in the middle of the road to reduce stoppages. Ticket purchase and control takes place at stations prior to boarding and the buses are step-free, which means the entire route is accessible to people using wheelchairs or who are travelling with baby buggies.

考古、文化遗产与研究发现遗物之后，还要解释什么

考古结合了发现、分析、想象、解释和遗产保护。注意作者如何组织并列概念。

Archaeology is partly the discovery of the treasures of the past, partly the careful work of the scientific analyst, partly the exercise of the creative imagination. It is toiling in the sun on an excavation in the Middle East, it is working with living Inuit and Yupik people in the snows of Alaska, and it is investigating the sewers of Roman Britain. But it is also the painstaking task of interpretation, so that we come to understand what these things mean for the human story. And it is the conservation of the world’s cultural heritage against looting and careless harm.
需要时看词汇注释
  • excavation：考古发掘；发掘现场
  • painstaking：细致而费心的
  • looting：劫掠、盗取文物

语言与教育一本词典是怎样开始的

Johnson 指 Samuel Johnson。这段介绍词典编写者的工作与做法，可练习人物经历和大型任务的描述。

Johnson was a poet and critic who raised common sense to the heights of genius. His approach to the problems that had worried writers throughout the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries was intensely practical. Up until his time, the task of producing a dictionary on such a large scale had seemed impossible without the establishment of an academy to make decisions about right and wrong usage. Johnson decided he did not need an academy to settle arguments about language; he would write a dictionary himself; and he would do it single-handed.
需要时看词汇注释
  • on such a large scale：以如此大的规模
  • settle arguments：解决争论
  • single-handed：独自地；凭一人之力

体育、技能与训练条件运动成绩背后的训练支持

They play hard, they play often, and they play to win. Australian sports teams win more than their fair share of titles, demolishing rivals with seeming ease. How do they do it? A big part of the secret is an extensive and expensive network of sporting academies underpinned by science and medicine. At the Australian Institute of Sport (AIS), hundreds of youngsters and pros live and train under the eyes of coaches. Another body, the Australian Sports Commission (ASC), finances programmes of excellence in a total of 96 sports for thousands of sportsmen and women. Both provide intensive coaching, training facilities and nutritional advice.

XREADING X READING PASSAGE 1 You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below. AUSTRALIA’S SPORTING SUCCESS A They play hard, they play often, and they play to win. Australian sports teams win more than their fair share of titles, demolishing rivals with seeming ease. How do they do it? A big part of the secret is an extensive and expensive network of sporting academies underpinned by science and medicine. At the Australian Institute of Sport (AIS), hundreds of youngsters and pros live and train under the eyes of coaches. Another body, the Australian Sports Commission (ASC), ﬁnances programmes of excellence in a total of 96 sports for thousands of sportsmen and women. Both provide intensive coaching, training facilities and nutritional advice. B Inside the academies, science takes centre stage.The AIS employs more than 100 sports scientists and doctors, and collaborates with scores of others in universities and research centres. AIS scientists work across a number of sports, applying skills learned in one – such as building muscle strength in golfers – to others, such as swimming and squash.They are backed up by technicians who design instruments to collect data from athletes.They all focus on one aim: winning.‘We can’t waste our time looking at ethereal scientiﬁc questions that don’t help the coach work with an athlete and improve performance,’ says Peter Fricker, chief of science at AIS. C A lot of their work comes down to measurement – everything from the exact angle of a swimmer’s dive to the second-by-second power output of a cyclist.This data is used to wring improvements out of athletes.The focus is on individuals, tweaking performances to squeeze an extra hundredth of a second here, an extra millimetre there. No gain is too slight to bother with. It’s the tiny, gradual improvements that add up to world-beating results.T o demonstrate how the system works, Bruce Mason at AIS shows off the prototype of a 3D analysis tool for studying swimmers. A wire-frame model of a champion swimmer slices through the water, her arms moving in slow motion. Looking side-on, Mason measures the distance between strokes. From above, he analyses how her spine swivels.When fully developed, this system will enable him to build a biomechanical proﬁle for coaches to use to help budding swimmers. Mason’s contribution to sport also includes the development of the SWAN (SWimming ANalysis) system now used in Australian national competitions. It collects images from digital cameras Test 1 18 © Cambridge University Press www.cambridge.org Cambridge University Press 978-0-521-69307-3 - Cambridge IELTS 6 Cambridge ESOL Excerpt More information

running at 50 frames a second and breaks down each part of a swimmer’s performance into factors that can be analysed individually – stroke length, stroke frequency, average duration of each stroke, velocity, start, lap and ﬁnish times, and so on. At the end of each race, SWAN spits out data on each swimmer. D ‘Take a look,’ says Mason, pulling out a sheet of data. He points out the data on the swimmers in second and third place, which shows that the one who ﬁnished third actually swam faster. So why did he ﬁnish 35 hundredths of a second down? ‘His turn times were 44 hundredths of a second behind the other guy,’ says Mason.‘If he can improve on his turns, he can do much better.’This is the kind of accuracy that AIS scientists’ research is bringing to a range of sports. With the Cooperative Research Centre for Micro Technology in Melbourne, they are developing unobtrusive sensors that will be embedded in an athlete’s clothes or running shoes to monitor heart rate, sweating, heat production or any other factor that might have an impact on an athlete’s ability to run.There’s more to it than simply measuring performance. Fricker gives the example of athletes who may be down with coughs and colds 11 or 12 times a year. After years of experimentation, AIS and the University of Newcastle in New South Wales developed a test that measures how much of the immune-system protein immunoglobulin A is present in athletes’ saliva. If IgA levels suddenly fall below a certain level, training is eased or dropped altogether. Soon, IgA levels start rising again, and the danger passes. Since the tests were introduced, AIS athletes in all sports have been remarkably successful at staying healthy. E Using data is a complex business.Well before a championship, sports scientists and coaches start to prepare the athlete by developing a ‘competition model’, based on what they expect will be the winning times.‘Y ou design the model to make that time,’ says Mason.‘A start of this much, each free-swimming period has to be this fast, with a certain stroke frequency and stroke length, with turns done in these times.’ All the training is then geared towards making the athlete hit those targets, both overall and for each segment of the race.Techniques like these have transformed Australia into arguably the world’s most successful sporting nation. F Of course, there’s nothing to stop other countries copying – and many have tried. Some years ago, the AIS unveiled coolant-lined jackets for endurance athletes. At the Atlanta Olympic Games in 1996, these sliced as much as two per cent off cyclists’ and rowers’ times. Now everyone uses them.The same has happened to the ‘altitude tent’, developed by AIS to replicate the effect of altitude training at sea level. But Australia’s success story is about more than easily copied technological ﬁxes, and up to now no nation has replicated its all-encompassing system. 日常工具、技术与自然条件计时工具为什么会受到天气限制

temporal hours 把白昼或黑夜分别分成十二段，段长随季节变化。本段介绍两类古代计时工具及其使用限制。

In order to track temporal hours during the day, inventors created sundials, which indicate time by the length or direction of the sun’s shadow. The sundial’s counterpart, the water clock, was designed to measure temporal hours at night. One of the first water clocks was a basin with a small hole near the bottom through which the water dripped out. The falling water level denoted the passing hour as it dipped below hour lines inscribed on the inner surface. Although these devices performed satisfactorily around the Mediterranean, they could not always be depended on in the cloudy and often freezing weather of northern Europe.

下面提供完整阅读语境与导读答案。此公开样本的摘录没有提供这篇全部原题和答案，本补充作为背景阅读，教师问题明确另行标识。

Test 1 18 READING READING PASSAGE 1 You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below. A Chronicle of Timekeeping Our conception of time depends on the way we measure it A According to archaeological evidence, at least 5,000 years ago, and long before the advent of the Roman Empire, the Babylonians began to measure time, introducing calendars to co- ordinate communal activities, to plan the shipment of goods and, in particular, to regulate planting and harvesting. They based their calendars on three natural cycles: the solar day, marked by the successive periods of light and darkness as the earth rotates on its axis; the lunar month, following the phases of the moon as it orbits the earth; and the solar year, deﬁ ned by the changing seasons that accompany our planet’s revolution around the sun. B Before the invention of artiﬁ cial light, the moon had greater social impact. And, for those living near the equator in particular, its waxing and waning was more conspicuous than the passing of the seasons. Hence, the calendars that were developed at the lower latitudes were inﬂ uenced more by the lunar cycle than by the solar year. In more northern climes, however, where seasonal agriculture was practised, the solar year became more crucial. As the Roman Empire expanded northward, it organised its activity chart for the most part around the solar year. C Centuries before the Roman Empire, the Egyptians had formulated a municipal calendar having 12 months of 30 days, with ﬁ ve days added to approximate the solar year. Each period of ten days was marked by the appearance of special groups of stars called decans. At the rise of the star Sirius just before sunrise, which occurred around the all- important annual ﬂ ooding of the Nile, 12 decans could be seen spanning the heavens. The cosmic signiﬁ cance the Egyptians placed in the 12 decans led them to develop a system in which each interval of darkness (and later, each interval of daylight) was divided into a dozen equal parts. These periods became known as temporal hours because their duration varied according to the changing length of days and nights with the passing of the seasons. Summer hours were long, winter ones short; only at the spring and autumn equinoxes www.cambridge.org© in this web service Cambridge University Press Cambridge University Press 978-0-521-17378-0 - Cambridge IELTS 8 Cambridge ESOL Excerpt More information

Reading 19 were the hours of daylight and darkness equal. Temporal hours, which were ﬁ rst adopted by the Greeks and then the Romans, who disseminated them through Europe, remained in use for more than 2,500 years. D In order to track temporal hours during the day, inventors created sundials, which indicate time by the length or direction of the sun’s shadow. The sundial’s counterpart, the water clock, was designed to measure temporal hours at night. One of the ﬁ rst water clocks was a basin with a small hole near the bottom through which the water dripped out. The falling water level denoted the passing hour as it dipped below hour lines inscribed on the inner surface. Although these devices performed satisfactorily around the Mediterranean, they could not always be depended on in the cloudy and often freezing weather of northern Europe. E The advent of the mechanical clock meant that although it could be adjusted to maintain temporal hours, it was naturally suited to keeping equal ones. With these, however, arose the question of when to begin counting, and so, in the early 14th century, a number of systems evolved. The schemes that divided the day into 24 equal parts varied according to the start of the count: Italian hours began at sunset, Babylonian hours at sunrise, astronomical hours at midday and ‘great clock’ hours, used for some large public clocks in Germany, at midnight. Eventually these were superseded by ‘small clock’, or French, hours, which split the day into two 12- hour periods commencing at midnight. F The earliest recorded weight - driven mechanical clock was built in 1283 in Bedfordshire in England. The revolutionary aspect of this new timekeeper was neither the descending weight that provided its motive force nor the gear wheels (which had been around for at least 1,300 years) that transferred the power; it was the part called the escapement. In the early 1400s came the invention of the coiled spring or fusee which maintained constant force to the gear wheels of the timekeeper despite the changing tension of its mainspring. By the 16th century, a pendulum clock had been devised, but the pendulum swung in a large arc and thus was not very efﬁ cient. G To address this, a variation on the original escapement was invented in 1670, in England. It was called the anchor escapement, which was a lever- based device shaped like a ship’s anchor. The motion of a pendulum rocks this device so that it catches and then releases each tooth of the escape wheel, in turn allowing it to turn a precise amount. Unlike the original form used in early pendulum clocks, the anchor escapement permitted the pendulum to travel in a very small arc. Moreover, this invention allowed the use of a long pendulum which could beat once a second and thus led to the development of a new ﬂ oor- standing case design, which became known as the grandfather clock. H Today, highly accurate timekeeping instruments set the beat for most electronic devices. Nearly all computers contain a quartz- crystal clock to regulate their operation. Moreover, not only do time signals beamed down from Global Positioning System satellites calibrate the functions of precision navigation equipment, they do so as well for mobile phones, instant stock- trading systems and nationwide power- distribution grids. So integral have these time- based technologies become to day- to- day existence that our dependency on them is recognised only when they fail to work. www.cambridge.org© in this web service Cambridge University Press Cambridge University Press 978-0-521-17378-0 - Cambridge IELTS 8 Cambridge ESOL Excerpt More information

健康与公共服务一种历史上的健康理解

本段回顾一种主要从身体和医疗理解健康的历史观点，后续段落继续扩展到生活环境与公共条件。

For much of recent Western history, health has been viewed in the physical sense only. That is, good health has been connected to the smooth mechanical operation of the body, while ill health has been attributed to a breakdown in this machine. Health in this sense has been defined as the absence of disease or illness and is seen in medical terms. According to this view, creating health for people means providing medical care to treat or prevent disease and illness. During this period, there was an emphasis on providing clean water, improved sanitation and housing.

Though we might think of film as an essentially visual experience, we really cannot afford to underestimate the importance of film sound. A meaningful sound track is often as complicated as the image on the screen, and is ultimately just as much the responsibility of the director. The entire sound track consists of three essential ingredients: the human voice, sound effects and music. These three tracks must be mixed and balanced so as to produce the necessary emphases which in turn create desired effects. Topics which essentially refer to the three previously mentioned tracks are discussed below. They include dialogue, synchronous and asynchronous sound effects, and music.

电影声音：三个组成部分怎样协同

Though we might think of film as an essentially visual experience, we really cannot afford to underestimate the importance of film sound. A meaningful sound track is often as complicated as the image on the screen, and is ultimately just as much the responsibility of the director. The entire sound track consists of three essential ingredients: the human voice, sound effects and music. These three tracks must be mixed and balanced so as to produce the necessary emphases which in turn create desired effects. Topics which essentially refer to the three previously mentioned tracks are discussed below. They include dialogue, synchronous and asynchronous sound effects, and music.

原题

  1. the director should plan the sound track at an early stage in filming.
  2. it would be wrong to overlook the contribution of sound to the artistry of films.
  3. the music industry can have a beneficial influence on sound in film.
  4. it is important for those working on the sound in a film to have sole responsibility for it.

Appendix5原题Q14–26

TOPIC BACKGROUND

话题背景学习单元

先认识话题中的基本概念，再读生活情境、积累词语和表达。每次可以只学一个情境，新增内容已标红。

共用背景

可供多科使用的知识与材料。具体阅读、写作、听力、口语任务分别进入练习。

TOPIC 04

城市：把住房、交通与公共空间放在一起看

城市生活涉及住在哪里、怎样出行，以及能否方便地使用学校、商店和公共空间。住房、交通与服务不能完全分开讨论：房子离工作地点多远，会影响出行安排；公园即使在附近，入口和开放时间也会影响使用。改善城市不只有新建道路这一种选择，还可讨论公共交通、步行条件和空间用途。不同居民的预算、行动条件与日常目的地可能不同。

先分清三个概念

概念它指什么不要混淆
public transport供公众共同使用的交通服务，例如公共汽车、地铁和有轨电车。有线路经过与服务方便可靠不是一回事；站点位置、班次和不同线路之间的连接都影响使用。
housing affordability住房支出与个人或家庭能够承担的预算之间的关系。价格低不一定对每个人都负担得起；判断时还需考虑收入以及其他必要生活支出。
public space供公众进入或共同使用的空间，例如广场、公园和部分街道空间。公共空间不一定是绿地；有一片绿地也不代表公众能够进入或方便使用。

读一段背景英语

A city is more than a collection of buildings. It also connects people with the places they need to reach. Consider a family looking for a home. The rent matters, but so do the distance to work, the route to school and the shops nearby. A flat outside the centre may suit them if transport fits their daily schedule. A park can be useful too, but its entrances and opening hours affect who can use it. These examples show why planning involves choices about both space and services. Different residents may have different priorities. A useful discussion of city life can describe a particular need and then consider how a change would affect the people who live there.
中文帮助理解

城市不仅是建筑的集合，也把居民与日常需要到达的地方连接起来。一个家庭选择住房时，除了租金，还可能考虑工作地点、上学路线和附近商店。市中心以外的住宅是否合适，要看交通能否配合他们的生活安排。公园能否实际使用，也与入口和开放时间有关。因此，城市规划既涉及空间，也涉及服务；不同居民重视的条件不尽相同。具体讨论某类人的需要，再解释一项变化会怎样影响他们，比笼统说城市应更方便更清楚。

阅读例句

Vehicles can be flowing freely along, at a density still well below what the road can handle, and then suddenly gel into a slow-moving ooze.

原文讨论车流的变化。交通容量、交通流量和实际通行速度不是同一指标。

The Physics of Traffic Behavior

这部分怎样放进每天的学习

每次只选一段：先用 8–12 分钟读懂背景，再花 3–5 分钟看两三组表达。时间计入当天学习，不在原计划之外加量。熟悉的段落直接跳过；累时读懂一段即可。

听读时，关注同一意思怎样换说法、句间关系与证据；写作时，重新核对题目问了什么、理由适用于什么条件；口语时，选自己的具体经历，练习把人、地点、变化和结果说清楚。阅读记录与写作稿继续分别保存。

隔天只抽两组表达：遮住英语，换一个真实场景说或写一句；能独立用且意思合适，再减少复习。用新语境中的独立表达检查掌握情况，例句记忆与实际运用分别记录。

TOPIC 01

教育：谁能学到，学什么，怎样学

教育讨论常围绕三个问题：谁有机会接受教育，课程应包含什么，以及怎样判断学习成果。能进入学校，不等于能获得适合自己的帮助；考试成绩也只是学习表现的一部分。学术知识、实际技能和独立思考可以相互支持，不必选一个就放弃另一个。讨论统一课程与个别支持时，还要考虑教师时间、学生起点，以及学校能提供哪些资源。

先分清三个概念

概念它指什么不要混淆
access to education获得教育机会，包括能够入学、参与课程并使用必要的学习资源。有机会进入课程与实际学懂是两件事；提供一个学习名额并不自动解决时间、语言或学习支持问题。
practical skills能够用于具体活动或解决实际问题的技能，例如操作工具、安排任务和处理信息。实际技能不只指手工或职业技术；它也可以用到学科知识，不能简单理解成与理论相反。
equal opportunity让不同背景的学习者有公平参与和发展的机会。公平机会不一定意味着每个人得到完全相同的帮助；起点不同的人可能需要不同程度的支持。

读一段背景英语

A school has several purposes. It can introduce students to knowledge, help them develop useful skills and give them experience of working with others. These purposes do not always require separate lessons. A science project, for example, can involve reading, measuring and explaining a result to a partner. However, students may need different kinds of support to take part. One student may understand the subject but struggle with the language used in class. Another may need more time to practise a skill. A common curriculum can give a class shared goals, while additional support can help students work towards them. When discussing education, it is useful to consider both what schools expect and what learners need.
中文帮助理解

学校可以帮助学生获得知识、发展实用技能，也让他们学习与别人合作。这些目标可以出现在同一项活动里，例如科学项目既需要阅读和测量，也需要向同伴解释结果。但参与同一堂课的学生，困难可能不同：有人懂学科内容，却不熟悉课堂语言；有人需要更多练习时间。因此，共同课程可以提供共同目标，额外支持则帮助不同学生接近这些目标。讨论教育时，可以同时关注学校的要求与学习者的需要。

阅读例句

The campaigners argue that such language, whether spoken or written, should be replaced by clearer forms of expression.

这篇阅读材料讨论清晰语言。它连接教育中的“理解与表达”，并非教育政策效果研究。

Plain English

这个话题通常怎样展开

以下为教学归纳的讨论角度，不是考试频率排名或原题清单。

  • 课程应如何安排学科知识、实际技能与独立思考？（教学概括，非原题）
  • 统一的课程或考试怎样与不同学生的学习需要相配合？（教学概括，非原题）
  • 学校、家庭和个人可以分别提供哪些学习支持？（教学概括，非原题）

可以直接理解和借用的搭配

本组是教学选用搭配与例句，尚未逐组统计真题频率。

搭配与意思放进句子里
provide access to education
提供接受教育的机会		Evening classes can provide access to education for people who work during the day.
develop practical skills
发展实际技能		Students can develop practical skills by planning and completing a group project.
meet learners' needs
满足学习者的需要		A course may need to offer different kinds of support to meet learners' needs.
receive feedback on
获得针对某项表现或作品的反馈		Students receive feedback on their first draft before they revise it.
put knowledge into practice
将知识用于实际活动		A design task gives students a chance to put their knowledge into practice.

读过背景后，需要练习时再进入：阅读章 · 听力章。已读过原句或提示的任务，记为学习后应用。

把教育概念用到具体问题里

先用两个课堂情境检查理解，再看一道正式写作题怎样限定讨论范围。前两题是本册编写的理解练习。

  1. 两名学生都能参加科学项目。甲会测量，但听不懂课堂指令；乙能理解指令，却需要练习测量。给两人同一份作业是否就满足了各自的学习需要？各写一种帮助，并说明帮助解决的困难。
  2. 学校给所有学生安排相同的项目目标，同时为需要的学生提供双语词表和额外练习时间。这属于改变学习目标，还是改变参与方式？用 access to education 和 equal opportunity 解释：已有名额，还缺什么？
完成后核对

① 甲需要理解指令的支持，例如关键术语表或一次演示；乙需要测量练习和反馈。两人都能入学，不代表都已获得适合的支持。② 目标相同，支持方式不同；平等机会可以通过不同帮助实现，不必把“公平”理解成每个人得到完全一样的东西。具体措施还受教师时间与可用资源限制。

正式题：小学课堂的正式学习与游戏

Some people argue that primary schools focus too much on formal learning.
To what extent do you agree with this opinion?
How important do you think it is for children to play as well as learn in the primary school classroom?

原题要求说明理由并举相关例子，完整作文至少 250 词，建议 40 分钟。本次只练审题与一个理由段，不计作完成整篇作文。

  1. 写出题目中的两项要求，并明确讨论对象与场景。
  2. 设计一个课堂活动，说明孩子在其中学什么、怎样参与、为什么需要游戏。再补一句：什么情况下需要额外的学习支持？
完成后核对

两项要求分别是：是否同意小学过于重视正式学习；游戏在小学课堂里有多重要。范围是小学课堂，不能只讨论大学就业或入学机会。

原创示例：A simple shop game can help children practise addition while taking turns as customers and shopkeepers. They use numbers for a clear purpose and learn to cooperate. A child who struggles with the instructions may need a demonstration before joining in. 这里“游戏—计算与合作—示范支持”逐项对应 practical skills 和 learners’ needs；它是理由段示例，没有官方分数。

打开同题考生稿：找出第 2 段支持正式学习的两点，以及第 3 段说明游戏价值的两点。再读评语，修改自己段落里最笼统的一句。

核对：考生稿谈到纪律与尊重、考试检验学习；游戏段谈到社交与创造技能、减少无聊并激发长期学习兴趣。考官认可回应两问和相关展开，同时指出结论笼统、句首连接词过多，以及个别搭配错误。7.5 分属于这份考生原稿，并不说明其中每句话都值得照抄。

完整题面 · 同题考生稿与评语（7.5 分） · 续页评语

本轮新增 136 组语境用法（点击返回完整教学）

这些是按语境选取的用法单位，可能含跨主题复现，不等同新增了同等数量的不同单词。

deter someone from doing something

使某人打消念头或不去做某事

Visible security measures may deter people from stealing bicycles.

结构：deter + 人 + from + -ing

易错：不能说 deter people to steal；may 避免把效果绝对化。

犯罪与惩罚：预防、回应与重新融入 →

hold someone accountable for

让某人为某事承担责任

Offenders should be held accountable for the harm they cause.

结构：hold + 人 + accountable + for + 名词/-ing

易错：responsible 与 accountable 都可涉及责任，不要把 accountable 当动词。

犯罪与惩罚：预防、回应与重新融入 →

serve a sentence

服刑

People who have served a sentence may need support when looking for work.

结构：serve + a prison sentence

易错：sentence 在此是刑期，不是语法中的句子。

犯罪与惩罚：预防、回应与重新融入 →

address the causes of

处理……的成因

Prevention programmes should address the causes of repeated offending.

结构：address + the causes of + 问题

易错：address 作及物动词，不能写 address to the causes。

犯罪与惩罚：预防、回应与重新融入 →

reduce the risk of reoffending

降低再次违法的风险

Training may reduce the risk of reoffending by widening lawful choices.

结构：reduce + the risk of + -ing

易错：risk 降低不等于行为一定消失。

犯罪与惩罚：预防、回应与重新融入 →

reintegrate into society

重新融入社会

Stable work can help former offenders reintegrate into society.

结构：reintegrate into + 群体

易错：帮助结构可用 help someone do，不能写 help someone doing。

犯罪与惩罚：预防、回应与重新融入 →

allocate funds to

向……分配资金

The council could allocate funds to urgent library repairs.

结构：allocate + funds + to + 项目

易错：allocate 是分配；不等于最终资金已有效使用。

政府与公共支出：预算、优先次序与长期成本 →

prioritise essential services

优先保障基本服务

Local authorities may need to prioritise essential services.

结构：prioritise + 名词

易错：不要用 priority 作动词。

政府与公共支出：预算、优先次序与长期成本 →

meet an unmet need

满足尚未得到满足的需求

An evening study room could meet an unmet need among shift workers.

结构：meet + an unmet need

易错：需求不能只用“大家都需要”断言，给具体群体与场景。

政府与公共支出：预算、优先次序与长期成本 →

cover running costs

支付运营成本

Ticket income may not cover running costs.

结构：cover + costs

易错：cover 在此不是遮盖，也不是说把成本降低。

政府与公共支出：预算、优先次序与长期成本 →

divert resources from

把资源从……转走

A large project could divert resources from basic maintenance.

结构：divert + resources + from + 原用途

易错：要给出来源用途，否则代价不具体。

政府与公共支出：预算、优先次序与长期成本 →

be accountable to

对……负有说明责任

Public bodies should be accountable to the communities they serve.

结构：be accountable to + 人/群体

易错：to 接责任对象；for 接需要承担责任的行为或结果。

政府与公共支出：预算、优先次序与长期成本 →

participate in community life

参与社区生活

朋友、聚会与快乐：用互动细节建立记忆点 →

have something to look forward to

clear up

throughout the day

be absorbed in

maintenance costs

expand a scheme

pay a deposit

undergo an inspection

under all conditions

be intended for

draw up a timetable

reserve space for

社区交通：找到例子、限制与纠正信息 →

make an initial attempt

rather than

READING PASSAGE 3

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27-40, which are based on Passage 3 below.

Book review: The World of Sugar by

UlbeBosma

Ulbe Bosma's The World of Sugar is a genuinely global history. Bosma discusses all the sugar­ growing places of the world, beginning with Cuba and Java, the largest exporters of the early 20th century. But this is a history not just of cane sugar but also of beet sugar, an equally important form of traded sugar over the last hundred years. Beet sugar is grown mainly in Europe and the United States. It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

Bosma's discussion of the sugar market in Britain gives a sense of the book's range. The sweet-toothed British first bought cane sugar from their own slavery-dependent colonial plantations. Following the abolition of slavery in the British Empire, cane sugar was imported to Britain from places which retained the practice, such as Cuba and Brazil. Towards the end of the 19th century, the British started to import beet sugar from continental Europe. Only in the 20th century was there a move to develop a national beet sugar industry.

The book provides a global labour history, investigating the wide range of labour regimes associated with growing sugar. Contrary to popular belief, cane sugar production was never just restricted to large, dedicated plantations owned by rich men. For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.

The World of Sugar is also a story of similarity and continuity in sugar cultivation. For example, imported labour has been used for much large-scale production. German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production. Cane cutting, Bosma shows, remains a poorly paid and brutal business to this day in many places in the world. But as well as this, the book is about the continuity of the use of traditional methods on small farms. In the mid 20th-century, this type of sugar production dominated in South Asia and Latin America.

This is also a history of capitalists and sugar dynasties, as well as corporations that in some cases have remained influential over very long periods. Great firms and great interests have had profound influence on the policies of states. In many places - not just the British Caribbean but Cuba and the Philippines too - a powerful sugar bourgeoisie played a major role in politics and their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies. In the battle for control of the industry, it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse. All this is explored by Bosma with wonderful subtlety and control.

原文 · 印刷页26

But sugar production was never just a matter of agriculture. It also involved the extraction, close to the place of harvest, of sucrose from the sugar plant, a process which required machinery powered by humans, animals, wind or steam. Further processes involved boiling (from the 19th century, this often involved vacuum systems) and the separation of sugar from other materials in a process known as refinement. From very early on, sugar production was an energy-intensive industrial process, mostly taking place in the countryside and in refineries in centres of consumption, both small and large. The growth of the industry entailed a very rapid diffusion of ideas and techniques from one country to another. Cuba, for example, developed an extraordinarily dense system of railways to transport workers and cane, as well as steam-powered sugar factories. Particular varieties of cane sugar and beet sugar spread very rapidly across the world, in accordance with local needs and demands.

Where once only tiny quantities of sugar could be produced, now new techniques, varieties, fertilisers, irrigation systems and much more have turned gleaming white sugar into a ubiquitous chemical. Over the same time, there has been a massive increase in consumption. Once regarded as a luxury, sugar came to be promoted as a valuable source of energy. But as the consumption of sugar has increased, so has the harm it does, whether to people's teeth or weight. In the face of appalling obstruction from the sugar industry to attempts to reduce consumption, some countries have been forced to tax sugar in order to bring that about. The sugar industry has a history of attacking its critics and, when it comes to obesity, of trying to blame fats, and lack of exercise and self-control. And the recent past has seen worrying new developments in mass sweetening. High-fructose corn syrup made from maize using an enzymatic process invented in Japan in the 1960s has a similar number of calories to table sugar but is far cheaper to produce. It is now widely consumed, having been adopted in the making of soft drinks and a large number of processed foods, and is regarded as a leading cause of obesity.

This is a wonderfully rich book, a model of global history, the history of production and the history of capitalism. Bosma avoids outbursts of emotion, celebratory or critical, even if they might have made his analysis of the multiple tragedies involving sugar all the more powerful. He shows that we could always have done without sugar and that today we have many alternative sources of sweetness. Yet many of the poorest people in the world still depend on it to make a living.

Q27 B：补贴与人为低价使beet sugar更具国际竞争力；Q28 A：英国进口来源按时间更换；Q29 C：Contrary to popular belief 后纠正甘蔗只来自富人种植园的误解；Q30 A：末段 could always have done without sugar 与 alternative sources of sweetness 支撑有害且非必需的评价。Q31–36 H/E/I/A/G/C，分别是移民劳工、小规模耕作、权势个人和公司、国家政府、金融控制、较贫穷国家。Q37 YES：农业技术带来大量供应；Q38 NOT GIVEN：文章说曾被视为奢侈品，却没说广告最初怎样宣传；Q39 NO：作者把高果糖玉米糖浆称为令人担忧的进展；Q40 YES：大量加工食品含它。这里是书评的作者判断，不把历史文章直接当当前营养建议。

用选中的词造句（可选）

让选中的词进入自己的句子

这 1000 条是按话题整理的词义与搭配索引，例搭配为教学编写。查词时可把词条连同正在阅读的原句收藏到“我的单词表”，再做回忆与拼写。学会拼写后，用下面这一步检查自己是否会用。

  1. 从当前话题选 1–3 个自己需要的词或词组；记录它在当前文章中指什么。没有文章语境时，先看本地词典中的对应义项与搭配。
  2. 合上解释，写一个与自己经历或当前题目有关的句子；再补一句条件、原因或具体例子。
  3. 展开词典核对意思与结构。标记一处修改，隔天换一个情境再用。
完成后核对

以 access 为例：Students need access to reliable internet to join the online class. The school could provide a study room for those without a connection at home. 第一处 access 是名词，结构是 access to + 名词；第二句补了具体支持。把“有机会使用”和“已掌握技能”分开表达。

检查三件事：词义是否符合本意；搭配和词形是否正确；句子是否说出了可理解的具体内容。若仍不确定，留下具体疑点再查来源；不要仅因句子包含目标词就标为已掌握。

精选词义与搭配练习

下面的筛选只作用于原有精选与练习；上方话题词表可独立查词。

44 张卡片

24 个跨话题常见词

同话题的独立阅读题：司法与技术：算法风险的真实阅读语境 →

evidence

证据；通常不可数

strong evidence / evidence of / evidence that…

There is little evidence that the new rule has solved the problem.

很少有证据表明新规定已解决问题。

不把 an evidence 当作一条证据；可说 a piece of evidence。

approach

方法；处理问题的方式

an approach to + 名词或动名词

The school is trying a different approach to teaching reading.

学校正在尝试另一种阅读教学方法。

名词 approach 后的 to 是介词；动词 approach 可直接接对象。

source

来源；信息或资源来自哪里

a reliable source / a source of…

The report does not explain the source of its figures.

报告没有解释数字的来源。

信息来源可靠，不等于某个结论必定成立；还要看证据。

research

研究；通常不可数

conduct research / research into…

Further research is needed before a firm conclusion can be reached.

得出确定结论之前还需要进一步研究。

普通概括多用 research；不要为了显得有证据而捏造研究。

alternative

可供选择的另一种办法；替代的

an alternative to… / an alternative method

For short journeys, cycling may be an alternative to driving.

短途出行时，骑车可能是开车之外的一种选择。

替代方案不等于在所有条件下都更好。

solution

解决办法

a solution to a problem / a practical solution

Lower prices alone may not be a complete solution to the problem.

仅降低价格可能无法完整解决这个问题。

用 a solution to；是否有效需要说明它解决了哪一部分。

require

需要；要求

require something / require someone to do something

The course requires students to explain their answers.

课程要求学生解释自己的答案。

避免 require someone doing；注意“需要资源”和“要求人做事”的结构差别。

offer

提供；给予一个机会或选择

offer someone something / offer something to someone

The library offers free activities to local families.

图书馆向本地家庭提供免费活动。

offer an opportunity 很自然；具体名词是否能和动词搭配，要看意思。

improve

改善；提高

improve a service / improve access to…

More frequent buses could improve access to the town centre.

更频繁的公交班次可能改善前往镇中心的便利程度。

可直接接宾语；不要写 improve to a service。

development

发展；开发；变化的过程

the development of… / economic development

The development of online services has changed how people access information.

线上服务的发展改变了人们获取信息的方式。

先明确发展的是技术、地区还是个人能力，不空写 development is good。

process

过程；一系列步骤

a process of… / a gradual process

Learning to use a new system can be a gradual process.

学会使用新系统可能是一个逐步进行的过程。

描述过程要讲步骤或变化，不只说它很复杂。

ability

能力

the ability to do something / develop an ability

Students need opportunities to develop the ability to solve unfamiliar problems.

学生需要机会培养解决陌生问题的能力。

用 ability to do；具体能力比笼统的“综合能力”更容易解释。

impact

影响；作用

have an impact on… / the impact of…

The impact of the change may differ between large and small businesses.

这一变化对大企业和小企业的影响可能不同。

impact 不自动表示负面；要说对谁、通过什么途径。

effect

效果；影响，名词

have an effect on… / the effect of…

The effect of the policy may take time to become clear.

这项政策的效果可能需要一段时间才会清楚。

与动词 affect 区分；effect on 后接受到影响的对象。

range

范围；种类

a range of… / a wide range of…

The centre provides a range of services for residents.

中心为居民提供多种服务。

wide 表示种类广，原材料未支持时不要随意加强范围。

complex

复杂的；包含相互关联的部分

a complex problem / a complex system

Traffic congestion is a complex problem with several possible causes.

交通拥堵是一个可能有多种原因的复杂问题。

复杂不等于无法解决；后面需要拆出具体因素。

appropriate

适当的；适合情境的

appropriate for… / an appropriate response

A method that works for beginners may not be appropriate for every learner.

适合初学者的方法未必适合所有学习者。

适合是相对于对象、目的和条件而言，不等于普遍最优。

value

价值；重视

cultural value / place value on…

People may value an object for its history rather than its price.

人们可能因为物品的经历而重视它，而非因为价格。

这里 value 可作动词；价格、使用价值与个人意义并非同一概念。

public

公众的；公共的

public transport / public services / the public

Public services need to be accessible to people with different needs.

公共服务需要让具有不同需求的人能够使用。

public 作形容词与 the public 指公众分开；开放给公众不一定免费。

community

社区；有共同联系的一群人

the local community / community facilities

A library can serve as a meeting place for the local community.

图书馆可以成为本地社区的聚会地点。

不只表示住宅区；要看地点或共同兴趣把哪些人联系起来。

technology

技术；技术手段

digital technology / adopt new technology

New technology is useful only if people can learn to use it effectively.

新技术只有在人们能够有效使用时才能发挥作用。

technology 常作概括性不可数名词；具体多种技术才可能用 technologies。

energy

能源；精力

energy use / renewable energy / have the energy to…

The design aims to reduce energy use in the building.

该设计旨在减少建筑中的能源使用。

建筑能源与个人精力是不同语境，不把一个义项套到所有文章。

goods

商品；货物

goods and services / transport goods

Online shopping changes how goods are ordered and delivered.

网购改变了商品的订购和配送方式。

这一义项通常是复数 goods，不用 a goods。

social

社会的；社交的

social responsibility / social interaction

The activity offers opportunities for social interaction.

这项活动提供了社交互动的机会。

social policy 是社会政策；social activities 可指社交活动，意思由名词决定。

没有找到匹配的表达。试试更短的词，或切回“全部”。

            听读

            写作
            完整初稿、具体反馈、修订稿。Task 1 与 Task 2 分开。

            口语
            真实声音、一处时间点、实际影响。文字不能代替发音证据。

            用法
            K 已会用／R 认识少用／N 新学；另记无提示、提示后或合法替代。

            考试要求与反馈标准

            科目 完整任务要求 怎么评价
            Academic 阅读 3 部分、40 题、60 分钟；填写字数按每道原题 每题 1 分；单篇不转换整科 band。
            听力 40 题；播放与检查时间按考试形式和指令 每题 1 分；回放后改对和首听正确分开。
            写作 共 60 分钟；Task 1 至少 150 词，Task 2 至少 250 词；建议约 20／40 分钟 每题看任务完成／回应、连贯衔接、词汇、语法四项，等权；整科 Task 2 权重为 Task 1 的两倍。
            口语 Part 1–3，整体 11–14 分钟；Part 2 有 1 分钟准备，长回答 1–2 分钟 流利连贯、词汇、语法、发音四项等权；声音和互动证据不能用文字补造。

            评分标准：写作评分描述、写作四项标准、口语评分描述、口语四项标准。

            阅读专项技巧

            先按卡点选方法：定位慢、判断不清、标题难分、填空失分，或看图对不上原文。每个单元都有步骤、英文例子和练习解释。

            Reading 图示标注是读文章后给图中部件填标签；Academic Writing Task 1 是根据图表写报告，两者任务不同。

            Task 1 读图与写作 →
            阅读起手判断题专项标题匹配信息与人物匹配填空专项阅读图示标注选择题与限时复盘
            阅读起手：用真实噪声文章建立段落地图

            用剑桥21 Test 1 Passage 2 Why we need silence 练一次“略读—扫读—精读”。先只标功能：A讲身体反应，B讲问题规模，C讲城市措施，D/E讲漂浮舱及实验，F/G讲安静的使用条件。无需先翻译所有句子。

            原题Q14标准答案C：题干问降低公众噪声暴露的策略。C列出quieter buses、reducing noise from roads、controlling noise from aircraft，随后又补道路涂层、绿化及禁令，因此是“多个措施”的完整对应。B虽也出现noise，却主要给40 decibels、1 in 5等数据，应对应Q15，答案B。

            原题Q16标准答案A：physiological changes定位到blood pressure goes up、muscles tense、glands release hormones。精读时记录“题干概括词→原文具体表现”，不要只抄共同词noise。下方三组保持正常真题难度，按原段落顺序答完再精读。

            继续做原题片段：Why we need silence｜噪声风险与城市降噪 · Why we need silence｜漂浮舱的两项实验 · Why we need silence｜主动安静与短时收益

            本单元的学习记录

            判断题：用真题区分反证、未知与观点归属

            判断前先拆主语、动作与限制词。剑桥21 Davies Q10说Hugh Blaker opposed姐妹购买印象派作品；原文称他为champion并说had a hand in the decision。标准答案FALSE：这是支持并参与，与反对矛盾，不是“没有提到”。

            同篇Q11说Bath画展very popular with the public。原文只说作品是首次在英国公共画廊展出的塞尚画作。标准答案NOT GIVEN：“公开展出/首次展出”都不等于受欢迎；完整原篇也没有观众反响。不能把自己的艺术常识补进来。

            观点题再加一步核对说话人：AI Q36称Russell的建议impractical，作者实际上说sensible and realistic，所以NO。Q37声称Brooks遭支持者不公批评，全文仅引用他的部署耗时判断，没有对他的回应，因此NOT GIVEN。F/NO需要直接矛盾，NG需要缺少命题中的关系或限定。

            继续做原题片段：The Davies Sisters｜印象派转向与战时收藏 · Do animals dream?｜章鱼行为与研究边界 · Artificial Intelligence｜部署边界、医疗与司法案例

            本单元的学习记录

            标题匹配：Miles Davis原题中的主旨与干扰项

            British Council官方教辅 Miles Davis 的Q14要求给A段选标题。A段开头说十三岁收到小号并开始上课，随后强调这些课塑造了signature sound：其他演奏者喜用vibrato，他被训练成长而直的音色；末句又说这种声音贯穿职业生涯。首句交代年龄和家人，整段落点却是独特演奏风格。

            标准答案：Q14＝viii，Davis’ unique style of trumpet playing。干扰项v Childhood and family life只覆盖开头背景，无法概括音色训练、与他人对比及终身延续。主旨应覆盖主要论述，而不只是重复第一句里的年龄或父亲。

            再核对Q15＝iii，An education in two parts。B段明确both in the clubs and in the classroom；随后既写退学和对课程的不满，也写后来承认学校在技巧与理论上的价值。因此ii Formal education unhelpful过于绝对，漏掉后半段的肯定。完成原材料的A–F六段后，以“每段讲什么＋作者借此说明什么”各写一句再对答案。

            原题完整九个标题为：i A legacy is established；ii Formal education unhelpful；iii An education in two parts；iv Branching out in new directions；v Childhood and family life；vi Change necessary to stay creative；vii Conflicted opinions over Davis’ earlier work；viii Davis’ unique style of trumpet playing；ix Personal and professional struggles。打开完整原文与原题；答后核对官方反馈。

            继续做原题片段：Miles Davis：早年音色与音乐教育

            本单元的学习记录

            信息与人物匹配：证据功能和说话人同时核对

            信息匹配先判所需信息的类别。Mapungubwe Q18问社群增长规模的估计，答案B，证据是人口高峰around 5,000 people；同段5 hectares是居住面积，虽然也为数字，却不是population。Q16问王室亲属住处，答案C，要找male relatives及outskirts，不能看到B段国王hilltop住处就停下。

            人物匹配先建立姓名与引语的归属。Why we need silence Q22说被迫安静令人不适，答案C，Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan，对应F段When people do not want silence, it can be very distressing。Q25说短暂安静也能有益，答案D，Eric Pfeifer，对应G段a few minutes at a time与make a big difference。

            答案可能重复，所以同一个人说两件不同事情不应被排除。精读时分别圈出引号边界、she/he指代和观点关键词；信息匹配记“在哪段”，人物匹配再多记“谁说”。

            本单元的学习记录

            用原题练这一题型

            Rethinking the Past · 发现怎样改变既有认识Rethinking the Past · 渐进变化与性别预设
            填空：真实表格、摘要中的字数和同义转换

            先分清两种指令。Davies Q1–4要求ONE WORD ONLY from the passage：grandfather’s wealth来自mining与shipping，题干已用transportation改写shipping，所以Q1＝mining。Q3的lengthy对应extensive，take/make notes相互改写，Q3＝notes，复数不能丢。

            Do animals dream? 表格按物种拆行：鸽子的脑区处理visual information，所以Q2＝visual；鲸豚关闭半边脑，另一半清醒，所以Q3＝half；non-REM dreams are less vivid改写为not very ___，因此Q5＝vivid。先检查行标题和词性，别从邻行捞词。

            选词摘要则填字母而非照抄原文。Sugar Q31把在德国工作的波兰人、在美国工作的墨西哥人等概括为H migrant workers；Q35把trade barriers and subsidies归类为G financial controls。精读把“具体实例→上位概念”连起来，不能认为选项没在原文逐字出现就排除。

            继续做原题片段：The Davies Sisters｜成长背景与收藏起点 · Do animals dream?｜跨物种睡眠研究 · The World of Sugar｜劳动组织与行业权力

            本单元的学习记录

            用原题练这一题型

            Water hyacinth · 沼气流程、收益与价格障碍鸟类起源：理论提出、反驳与新证据鸟类起源：两方论点与过渡化石健康观念变化：年份、十年与三大领域
            图示标注：官方蜣螂隧道原图中的深度与形状

            本示范使用IELTS官方图示标注样题的原文和原图，题号Q6–8不改。先看纵轴是距地表的近似深度cm，再看各隧道的深浅和腔室形态。按题目词框选择名称，不能自行写“20 cm”等深度替代物种。

            原文第二段明确：Some large species originating from France excavate tunnels to a depth of approximately 30 cm below the dung pat. 又说Spanish species的隧道最浅；South African beetles dig narrow tunnels of approximately 20 cm below the surface of the pat. 图上Q7最深约30 cm，Q8最浅，Q6约20 cm。因此官方答案为Q6 South African；Q7 French；Q8 Spanish。

            同段还描述South African ball roller在表面切球、滚走并附在植物基部。这是词框中的干扰项：虽然也有South African，但ball roller的动作和图中地下隧道不符。答后把每种名称同时连到“深度＋形状＋位置”，避免只认一个相同地名。打开三段完整原文；核对官方答案页。

            AI Q27问第一段作者在做什么，答案B：describing a public perception。看似列了治病、创新、创造力等好处，但它们被置于sensationalist news、media headlines、you might think的框架中，属于媒体造成的印象；C仅抓到局部词汇，漏了作者表达的归属。

            补充学习单元

            2 个单元 · 选一个替换当天相应训练块。首稿、修订和迁移答案均加入学习记录备份。

            01标题匹配：用整段意思判断 Miles Davis 的人生阶段这一单元练主旨与支撑细节的区别。先学方法，再做六道原题；结果记录为学习后应用，不作未见基线，也不换算雅思分数。约 25 分钟

            标题覆盖的是整段

            标题匹配要求找段落的中心意思。细节信息匹配则是找某条信息出现在哪里，两者不能用同一套判断标准。现行标题匹配规则中，标题有多余项，一个标题不能重复使用；有的段落可能不设题或已作示例，按当前题面填写。

            先读标题，把它们压缩成中文意义：是在说一种风格、两条学习路径、困难，还是转向？再快速读段落，用一句话写出“谁／什么＋发生了什么＋这段主要在说明什么”。开头、转折和结尾往往有帮助，但首句可能只是引入故事，不能只凭首句选题。

            短示范：不要被第一句话吸走

            “Two years ago, the library bought twenty tablets. Staff then discovered that many visitors needed help filling in online forms. They introduced weekly support sessions, and attendance soon grew. The library now sees digital guidance as a central part of its service.”

            给这段选标题：①购买设备的费用；②图书馆服务重点的变化；③平板电脑的技术故障。先写一句段意，再选择。这个示范由本学习册编写，不是真题。

            下面原页提供 Miles Davis 的 A–F 六段和九个标题。每段先写一个不超过 15 个中文字的主旨，再比较两个最接近的标题。问自己：这个标题能解释大部分句子吗？有没有把一件小事当整段主题？有没有把 earlier／later、肯定／批评或“只有一种”读错？

            原第 9 页还提供 A、B、D 的部分主题句作为课堂支架。如果使用了它们，在记录中写“用过提示”。不会的题可以留空并标问号，不必为六道题反复通读整篇。

            Miles Davis · 标题匹配

            Surveying the text

            1 Survey the following reading passage. (20 seconds)

            MILES DAVIS

            Icon and iconoclast¹

            A At the age of thirteen, Miles Davis was given his first trumpet, lessons were arranged with a local trumpet player, and a musical odyssey began. These early lessons, paid for and supported by his father, had a profound effect on shaping Davis’ signature sound. Whereas most trumpeters of the era favoured the use of vibrato (a wobbly quiver in pitch inflected in the instrument’s tone), Davis was taught to play with a long, straight tone, a preference his instructor reportedly drilled into the young trumpeter with a rap on the knuckles every time Davis began using vibrato. This clear, distinctive style never left Davis. He continued playing with it for the rest of his career, once remarking, ‘If I can’t get that sound, I can’t play anything.’

            B Having graduated from high school in 1944, Davis moved to New York City, where he continued his musical education both in the clubs and in the classroom. His enrolment in the prestigious Julliard School of Music was short-lived, however – he soon dropped out, criticising what he perceived as an over-emphasis on the classical European repertoire and a neglect of jazz. Davis did later acknowledge, however, that this time at the school was invaluable in terms of developing his trumpet-playing technique and giving him a solid grounding in music theory. Much of his early training took place in the form of jam sessions and performances in the clubs of 52nd Street, where he played alongside both up-and-coming and established members of the jazz pantheon such as Coleman Hawkins, Eddie ‘Lockjaw’ Davis, and Thelonious Monk.

            C In the late 1940s, Davis collaborated with nine other instrumentalists, including a French horn and a tuba player, to produce The Birth of Cool, an album now renowned for the inchoate sounds of what would later become known as ‘cool’ jazz. In contrast to popular jazz styles of the day, which featured rapid, rollicking beats, shrieking vocals, and short, sharp horn blasts, Davis’ album was the forerunner of a different kind of sound – thin, light horn-playing, hushed drums and a more restrained, formal arrangement. Although it received little acclaim at the time (the liner notes to one of Davis’ later recordings call it a ‘spectacular failure’), in hindsight The Birth of Cool has become recognised as a pivotal moment in jazz history, cementing – alongside his 1958 recording, Kind of Blue – Davis’ legacy as one of the most innovative musicians of his era.

            D Though Davis’ trumpet playing may have sounded effortless and breezy, this ease rarely carried over into the rest of his life. The early 1950s, in particular, were a time of great personal turmoil. After returning from a stint in Paris, Davis suffered from prolonged depression, which he attributed to the unravelling of a number of relationships, including his romance with a French actress and some musical partnerships that ruptured as a result of creative disputes. Davis was also frustrated by his perception that he had been overlooked by the music critics, who were hailing the success of his collaborators and descendants in the ‘cool’ tradition, such as Gerry Mulligan and Dave Brubeck, but who afforded him little credit for introducing the cool sound in the first place.

            E In the latter decades of his career, Davis broke out of exclusive jazz settings and began to diversify his output across a range of musical styles. In the 1960s, he was influenced by early funk performers such as Sly and the Family Stone, which then expanded into the jazz-rock fusion genre – of which he was a frontrunner – in the 1970s. Electronic recording effects and electric instruments were incorporated into his sound. By the 1980s, Davis was pushing the boundaries further, covering pop anthems such as Cyndi Lauper’s Time After Time and Michael Jackson’s Human Nature, dabbling in hip hop, and even appearing in some movies.

            F Not everyone was supportive of Davis’ change of tune. Compared to the recordings of his early career, universally applauded as linchpins of the jazz oeuvre, trumpeter Wynston Marsalis derided his fusion work as being ‘not true jazz’, and pianist Bill Evans denounced the ‘corrupting influence’ of record companies, noting that rock and pop ‘draw wider audiences’. In the face of this criticism Davis remained defiant, commenting that his earlier recordings were part of a moment in time that he had no ‘feel’ for any more. He firmly believed that remaining stylistically inert would have hampered his ability to develop new ways of producing music. From this perspective, Davis’ continual revamping of genre was not merely a rebellion, but an evolution, a necessary path that allowed him to release his full musical potential.

            ¹ An iconoclast is somebody who challenges traditional beliefs or customs

            3. A description of a journey

            下面可以对照完整原文和对应题目学习。

            A At the age of thirteen, Miles Davis was given his first trumpet, lessons were arranged with a local trumpet player, and a musical odyssey began. These early lessons, paid for and supported by his father, had a profound effect on shaping Davis’ signature sound. Whereas most trumpeters of the era favoured the use of vibrato (a wobbly quiver in pitch inflected in the instrument’s tone), Davis was taught to play with a long, straight tone, a preference his instructor reportedly drilled into the young trumpeter with a rap on the knuckles every time Davis began using vibrato. This clear, distinctive style never left Davis. He continued playing with it for the rest of his career, once remarking, ‘If I can’t get that sound, I can’t play anything.’

            B Having graduated from high school in 1944, Davis moved to New York City, where he continued his musical education both in the clubs and in the classroom. His enrolment in the prestigious Julliard School of Music was short-lived, however – he soon dropped out, criticising what he perceived as an over-emphasis on the classical European repertoire and a neglect of jazz. Davis did later acknowledge, however, that this time at the school was invaluable in terms of developing his trumpet-playing technique and giving him a solid grounding in music theory. Much of his early training took place in the form of jam sessions and performances in the clubs of 52nd Street, where he played alongside both up- and-coming and established members of the jazz pantheon such as Coleman Hawkins, Eddie ‘Lockjaw’ Davis, and Thelonious Monk.

            C In the late 1940s, Davis collaborated with nine other instrumentalists, including a French horn and a tuba player, to produce The Birth of Cool, an album now renowned for the inchoate sounds of what would later become known as ‘cool’ jazz. In contrast to popular jazz styles of the day, which featured rapid, rollicking beats, shrieking vocals, and short, sharp horn blasts, Davis’ album was the forerunner of a different kind of sound – thin, light horn-playing, hushed drums and a more restrained, formal arrangement. Although it received little acclaim at the time (the liner notes to one of Davis’ later recordings call it a ‘spectacular failure’), in hindsight The Birth of Cool has become recognised as a pivotal moment in jazz history, cementing – alongside his 1958 recording, Kind of Blue – Davis’ legacy as one of the most innovative musicians of his era.

            原题选项

            i A legacy is established；ii Formal education unhelpful；iii An education in two parts；iv Branching out in new directions；v Childhood and family life；vi Change necessary to stay creative；vii Conflicted opinions over Davis’ earlier work；viii Davis’ unique style of trumpet playing；ix Personal and professional struggles

            These early lessons, paid for and supported by his father, had a profound effect on shaping Davis’ signature sound.

            02单选题：Older workers 中的条件、范围与替换表达用四道单选练习排除“词相同、意思却扩大了”的选项。材料是练习题节选，适合专项练习，不代表一套完整阅读测评。约 22 分钟

            先确定问题问什么

            这组题每题选 A–D 中一个答案。其他选择题可能要求选多个，必须以题面为准。现行说明中，选择题的问题顺序与相关信息在文中出现的顺序一致；这能帮助定位，不能代替证据。

            把题干中的对象和动作圈出来：问公司可以考虑的做法、某计划的用途、某类工作的吸引力，还是研究表明什么？定位后读完整句，以及解释它的相邻句。不要看到一个词就停。

            检查整个选项的条件

            用“对象＋行为＋程度／时间”核对选项。例如有截止年龄的合同，不支持“想工作多久都可以”；部分人的行为，不支持所有人；在某国开展的研究，不等于某事起源于该国。正确选项常用不同词表达原文，错误选项也可能复制原文词语。

            短示范

            “The town introduced a free shuttle bus for hospital visitors. It runs on weekday mornings only, and passengers must book a seat in advance.”

            Which statement is supported? A. The bus runs throughout every day. B. Visitors can use the bus without booking. C. Visitors may take a free bus on weekday mornings after booking. D. The service is limited to hospital staff.

            这是本学习册条件核对示范，不是真题。给正确选项标出它保留的三个条件，再写出一个错误选项改错的地方。

            原题应用

            下方第一张原页是完整提供的样题节选，第二张是四道题。按题目顺序定位，每题写证据段落号，再给一个最有迷惑性的错误选项标注：与文中矛盾／未提及／把范围扩大。不要用你对退休或创业的常识替文本作答。

            Older workers · 单项选择

            [Note: This is an extract from a Part 1 text about older people in the workforce.]

            The general assumption is that older workers are paid more in spite of, rather than because of, their productivity. That might partly explain why, when employers are under pressure to cut costs, they persuade a 55-year old to take early retirement. Take away seniority-based pay scales, and older workers may become a much more attractive employment proposition. But most employers and many workers are uncomfortable with the idea of reducing someone’s pay in later life – although manual workers on piece-rates often earn less as they get older. So retaining the services of older workers may mean employing them in different ways.

            One innovation was devised by IBM Belgium. Faced with the need to cut staff costs, and having decided to concentrate cuts on 55 to 60-year olds, IBM set up a separate company called Skill Team, which re-employed any of the early retired who wanted to go on working up to the age of 60. An employee who joined Skill Team at the age of 55 on a five-year contract would work for 58% of his time, over the full period, for 88% of his last IBM salary. The company offered services to IBM, thus allowing it to retain access to some of the intellectual capital it would otherwise have lost.

            The best way to tempt the old to go on working may be to build on such ‘bridge’ jobs: part-time or temporary employment that creates a more gradual transition from full-time work to retirement. Studies have found that, in the United States, nearly half of all men and women who had been in full-time jobs in middle age moved into such ‘bridge’ jobs at the end of their working lives. In general, it is the best-paid and worst-paid who carry on working. There seem to be two very different types of bridge job-holder – those who continue working because they have to and those who continue working because they want to, even though they could afford to retire.

            If the job market grows more flexible, the old may find more jobs that suit them. Often, they will be self-employed. Sometimes, they may start their own businesses: a study by David Storey of Warwick University found that in Britain 70% of businesses started by people over 55 survived, compared with an overall national average of only 19%. But whatever pattern of employment they choose, in the coming years the skills of these ‘grey workers’ will have to be increasingly acknowledged and rewarded.

            Questions 1–4

            Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

            Write the correct letter in boxes 1-4 on your answer sheet.

            1 In paragraph one, the writer suggests that companies could consider

            1. abolishing pay schemes that are based on age.
            2. avoiding pay that is based on piece-rates.
            3. increasing pay for older workers.
            4. equipping older workers with new skills.

            2 Skill Team is an example of a company which

            1. offers older workers increases in salary.
            2. allows people to continue working for as long as they want.
            3. allows the expertise of older workers to be put to use.
            4. treats older and younger workers equally.

            3 According to the writer, ‘bridge’ jobs

            1. tend to attract people in middle-salary ranges.
            2. are better paid than some full-time jobs.
            3. originated in the United States.
            4. appeal to distinct groups of older workers.

            4 David Storey’s study found that

            1. people demand more from their work as they get older.
            2. older people are good at running their own businesses.
            3. an increasing number of old people are self-employed.
            4. few young people have their own businesses.

            The Davies Sisters · 原文与 1–13 题

            You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.

            The Davies Sisters

            Between 1908 and 1924, Gwendoline and Margaret Davies amassed one of the largest collections of late-nineteenth and early-twentieth-century French paintings in Britain

            Gwendoline (1882-1951) and Margaret (1884-1963) Davies were the granddaughters of David Davies, a Welshman who amassed a fortune in the shipping and mining industries. In 1907, when Gwendoline came into her inheritance (Margaret would follow in 1909), the sisters were said to be the wealthiest unmarried women in Britain. Their religious upbringing in rural Wales gave them a deep sense of social responsibility and they chose to use their inheritance for cultural and philanthropic* purposes.

            While there was no real family history of art collecting, the sisters' education was rigorously geared toward such pursuits. Their London school focused on cultural rather than academic study, and they travelled extensively with their governess, Jane Blaker, visiting art galleries and making extensive notes on the collections there.

            The sisters began to make regular art purchases from 1908, which roughly coincided with the dates of their inheritance. They took advice from various people, including the art dealer Hugh Blaker (the brother of Jane Blaker) and David Croal Thompson, who was also an art dealer. While it was long assumed that these men were largely responsible for the nature of the sisters' collection, it has recently been accepted that Gwendoline and Margaret retained a far more active role in the process.

            The sisters' journals reveal their preference for Old Master** paintings. Yet they initially made very few attempts to secure any such works. While the sisters were wealthy in relative terms, their income was nothing compared to the fortunes of American art collectors of this period, such as J. Pierpont Morgan. Quite simply, high quality Old Master works were, if not beyond their means, then beyond what they were willing to pay for them. Instead, their early purchases were of the fashionable, safe variety, and included, for example, paintings by the French artist Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot.

            However, it was only a few years before their collecting took a new direction and they turned to the work of the French Impressionists***. We know that Hugh Blaker, as a champion of contemporary French art had a hand in the decision, and we know also that they would have seen examples on their various trips to Paris. Whatever the precise reason for this change, their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice by the French artist Claude Monet. Over the next 12 years, the sisters amassed the bulk of their Impressionist collection, including six further works by Monet, two more by Manet, and three by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne.

            The First World War (1914-1918) played a part in the development of the sisters' collection. Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area. Later in the conflict, both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes, in northern France; Gwendoline in 1916, followed by Margaret in 1917.

            It was tedious and distressing work, which would have a permanent effect on Gwendoline's health. Yet on one of numerous trips to nearby Paris, she visited the Bernheim-Jeune Gallery. Here she acquired two works by Cézanne - Provençal Landscape and The François Zola Dam. The paintings were shipped directly to Bath, England, where they became the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain.

            Commentators have often described the sisters as unlikely pioneer collectors. Much is made of their isolation in rural Wales and the fact that they didn't make friends with artists or gallery owners. Yet they didn't feel obliged to follow fashionable tastes and were free to pursue their own preferences. Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.

            By the early 1920s, Gwendoline felt increasingly uncomfortable buying art works when faced with the poverty and social upheaval created by the First World War. Her philanthropic pursuits then became focused almost exclusively on social causes and the development of the sisters' home at Gregynog Hall into a conference center and venue for the Gregynog Festival of Music and Poetry. Gwendoline made her final art purchase in March 1926. Margaret also stopped collecting around this time, but started again in the 1930s acquiring, on a relatively small scale, work by contemporary British artists.

            The sisters collected French Impressionist paintings at a time when such art was routinely ignored by individuals and institutions alike. The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists. In collecting paintings that they loved, the sisters created a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy for the people of Wales and beyond.

            * philanthropic: seeking to promote the welfare of others, often by charitable funding

            ** Old Master: a highly respected artist of great skill who worked in Europe before about 1800

            *** Impressionist: an artist with a style of painting that developed in France in the late 1800s by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne

            原页文字提示：脚注引文保留原页；其后半句涉及 Renoir 作品，属于来源编辑瑕疵，不要把整条脚注当作英语完整定义范例。这里的 Impressionist 指印象派画家。

            be geared toward… 哪件事被设计为服务某种目的？ 表达一个课程以初学者的需要为重点
            play a part in… 战争怎样参与了收藏发展的过程？它等不等于唯一原因？ 表达公共交通可能对减少拥堵发挥作用

            本章先试这 3 项；其中选 1—2 项进入主动输出。philanthropic、艺术流派和画家姓名可只作为读懂文章的背景，不要求全部主动背诵。选词仍取决于你的实际缺口，并非宣称这 3 项已被证明是考试最高频词。

            Unfamiliar vocabulary usage。 gear something toward something 指把某物设计或调整为适合某目的；常见被动形式 be geared toward/towards…。

            1. 表达：这个课程针对初学者的需要设计。
            2. 换到工作情境：培训侧重实际问题解决。
            3. 标记 K（以前会用）/ R（认识但很少用）/ N（本次新学）。再记“按题面提示组织句子 / 额外帮助后成功 / 换一种说法成功”。结构就在本页，照着它写不能记为无提示独立提取；独立提取留到隔日关闭参考后的检查。

            最后合上解释，用自己的话重建两道选定题的判断。记为修复后的表现，不覆盖首次答案。

            词汇与句子中的真实作用

            champion 在本文是支持者，不是冠军。a champion of contemporary French art 与 had a hand in the decision 共同帮助判断态度和参与；不能只孤立背一个中文义项。

            their education was rigorously geared toward such pursuits 中，their education 是被设计安排的对象，such pursuits 回指前文谈及的文化艺术活动。这句话不是说她们必须已经拥有收藏经验。

            played a part in 表示有所作用；本身不等于唯一或决定性原因。阅读因果信息时，不能把“起到作用”自动升级为“完全由此造成”。

            表达参考：

            • The course is geared towards the needs of beginners.
            • The training is geared toward practical problem-solving.
            • She is a strong supporter of public libraries. / She is a champion of public libraries.
            • Public transport can play a part in reducing congestion. / Public transport can help reduce congestion.

            toward 与 towards 都可接受。designed to meet beginners' needs 是合法替代表达；表达任务成功与目标结构的独立提取分别记。

            TOPIC 03

            科技：工具带来什么，又需要什么条件

            科技讨论可以从具体工具怎样改变一件事开始，例如获取资料、观看演出或处理重复任务。线上服务提供了一种渠道，但能连接网络、会使用工具和能够判断信息是不同条件。自动化可以处理部分步骤，责任与判断却需要另外讨论。评价一项技术时，可以比较便利、成本、使用门槛和个人信息的处理方式，也要说明谁受益、谁可能仍需要其他选择。

            先分清三个概念

            概念它指什么不要混淆
            digital access能够使用数字设备、网络及相关服务的条件和机会。拥有设备、能够连接网络与会熟练使用服务并不相同；服务上线也不等于每个人都能使用。
            automation让机器或软件按照设定方式完成原本需要人工处理的部分步骤。一项任务自动完成，不等于整个岗位都能被替代；操作、检查和责任可以由不同角色承担。
            data privacy个人信息怎样被收集、使用和分享，以及个人对此拥有怎样的选择。隐私关注信息应怎样被使用；安全也关注怎样防止未经许可的访问，二者相关但不能完全互换。

            读一段背景英语

            Technology changes the way people carry out particular activities. An online service can let a viewer watch a recorded performance without travelling to a theatre. A shared document can allow colleagues in different places to work on the same report. However, having a tool does not settle every question about its use. People still need a suitable device, a connection and enough knowledge to use the service. They may also want to know what personal information it collects. In some situations, an online option adds a useful choice; in others, people may still prefer direct contact or a physical space. A balanced discussion can explain the specific benefit of a tool while considering the conditions needed to use it.
            中文帮助理解

            科技可以改变完成某项活动的方式：线上服务让人不必前往剧院，也能观看录制的演出；共享文档让不同地点的同事参与同一份报告。不过，有了工具不代表所有使用问题都已经解决。设备、网络和使用知识仍是条件，服务怎样收集个人信息也值得关注。有时线上方式增加了一个有用选择，有时人们仍希望直接接触他人或使用实体空间。讨论可以具体说明工具提供了什么便利，以及这些便利在什么条件下才能实现。

            阅读例句

            It is technically incorrect to talk about bat 'radar', since they do not use radio waves.

            原文区分雷达与蝙蝠的回声定位：讨论科技要分清机制，不能只凭表面相似就当作同一技术。

            Let’s Go Bats

            这个话题通常怎样展开

            以下为教学归纳的讨论角度，不是考试频率排名或原题清单。

            • 线上服务在哪些情况下增加选择，在哪些情况下难以替代实体活动？（教学概括，非原题）
            • 数字工具的便利应怎样与使用门槛和个人信息保护一起考虑？（教学概括，非原题）
            • 哪些步骤适合自动处理，哪些仍需要人的判断与检查？（教学概括，非原题）

            可以直接理解和借用的搭配

            本组是教学选用搭配与例句，尚未逐组统计真题频率。

            搭配与意思放进句子里

            完成常规、重复性的任务            		Software can carry out routine tasks such as putting a list of names in alphabetical order.
            reduce the need to travel

            读过背景后，需要练习时再进入：Task 2 · 口语章。已读过原句或提示的任务，记为学习后应用。

            技术是否可用：条件、风险与人的判断

            先回到下方 Artificial Intelligence 阅读原文，找到数据基础设施和专业人员两个条件。再完成 Q31 与 Q33；答案在原题词表中，不直接照抄整句。

            完成后核对

            Q31 选 G（framework），对应 data infrastructure；Q33 选 C（skills），对应 human talent。能做算法不等于机构已经具备部署条件：整理和使用数据的基础、能实施与维护的人都需要考虑。

            换到一个具体服务（原创理解练习）

            一家社区中心推出网上预约。部分居民没有稳定网络；另一些人有手机却不会操作。系统要求填写身份证号码，并可能受到恶意攻击。请把四件事分别对应 digital access、digital skills、privacy 与 security，再提出一项保留人工帮助的做法。

            完成后核对

            稳定网络属于 access；会不会使用属于 skills；身份证号码为何收集、谁能看到和保留多久涉及 privacy；防止未授权访问与攻击涉及 security。两者相关，但安全措施完善不表示所有个人信息收集都合理。可保留电话或现场预约，并让工作人员解释必要信息。

            原创表达：An online service can make booking easier, provided that users have reliable internet access and know how to use it. Staff should still be available to help people who cannot complete the process online. 用 provided that 写条件，第二句给出需要人工参与的具体环节。

            AI 原文支持的是实施条件、攻击风险与人的判断。这里的社区预约和隐私讨论是迁移情境，不是声称原文证明了这些服务的实际效果。
