            不真实的信息：发现问题与核对

            不真实的信息：发现问题与核对

            本单元使用真实 Part 2 问题。先看完整问题组，再比较参考作答如何逐问落实内容；人物经历为参考作答中的示例，不是原题事实或统一标准答案。

            1. Describe a time when you read or heard something that you thought was not true.
            2. where you read/heard this
            3. what you read/heard
            4. why you thought it was not true
            5. and explain how you felt about reading/hearing this thing that you thought was not true.

            先留下自己的回答

            可以直接开口，也可以先写文字草稿；录音和文字任选一种。参考内容在后面，按需查看。

            下载录音

            录音按题保存在本浏览器；换设备请下载音频，文字备份不包含声音。

            参考作答

            I remember seeing a message in a group chat saying that our university library would close for an entire month. It appeared just before an important assignment was due, so several people were worried. The message looked like a screenshot of an announcement, but it didn't include a date or a link to the original notice.

            I doubted it because I had been in the library that morning and had seen nothing about a long closure. Rather than immediately telling everyone the message was wrong, I checked the library website. The actual notice said that one reading room would close for repairs while the rest of the building remained open.

            At first I felt anxious, because I depended on the library for a quiet place to study. Once I had checked the notice, I felt relieved and a little frustrated that an incomplete message had caused so much confusion. I shared the link with the group and explained the difference. The experience reminded me to check the original context before passing on information that sounds urgent.

            逐项解释与练习

            where=group chat；what=whole library closed one month；why=different recent observation + original notice核对；feelings=anxious→relieved/frustrated。题目是 thought not true，先怀疑再核对比把直觉当证据更清楚。本文事件是原创参考作答，不是新增真题文本。

            练习：保留题目中的对象、时间和问法，换成自己的真实经历。先口头作答，再对照上面的具体内容逐项检查；不需要逐字背诵参考作答。

            公园：从空间细节讲清兴趣

            公园：从空间细节讲清兴趣

            本单元使用真实 Part 2 问题。先看完整问题组，再比较参考作答如何逐问落实内容；人物经历为参考作答中的示例，不是原题事实或统一标准答案。

            1. Describe an interesting garden or park you have seen.
            2. where this garden or park is
            3. how big it is
            4. what you saw in this garden/park
            5. and explain why you think this garden/park is interesting.

            先留下自己的回答

            可以直接开口，也可以先写文字草稿；录音和文字任选一种。参考内容在后面，按需查看。

            下载录音

            录音按题保存在本浏览器；换设备请下载音频，文字备份不包含声音。

            参考作答

            I'd like to talk about a park near the railway station in a city I visited last spring. It wasn't enormous; I could walk from one entrance to the other in about fifteen minutes. Even so, it contained several different areas, and that made it feel larger than it actually was.

            Near the entrance there was an open lawn where families were sitting. Further along, a narrow path led past flower beds to a small pond. I also noticed a section where local residents were growing vegetables. There were simple labels beside the plants, so visitors could see what was being grown.

            What interested me most was the contrast between the busy streets outside and the way people used the park. Some were exercising, while others were just talking or reading. The vegetable plots made it feel like a place that residents helped shape, rather than somewhere people only passed through. I spent longer there than I had planned because there was something different to notice around each corner.

            逐项解释与练习

            题卡 how big 用 walk across in about fifteen minutes 给感知尺度，不虚报面积。what saw 是草坪／池塘／菜地；interesting 由居民参与与外部繁忙街道的对比解释。不要只罗列设施而漏掉为什么有趣。

            练习：保留题目中的对象、时间和问法，换成自己的真实经历。先口头作答，再对照上面的具体内容逐项检查；不需要逐字背诵参考作答。

            景点：免费开放与失望原因

            景点：免费开放与失望原因

            本单元使用真实 Part 3 问题。先看完整问题组，再比较参考作答如何逐问落实内容；人物经历为参考作答中的示例，不是原题事实或统一标准答案。

            1. Do you think tourist attractions such as museums should be free for local people to visit?
            2. What can make a tourist attraction disappointing for visitors?

            先留下自己的回答

            可以直接开口，也可以先写文字草稿；录音和文字任选一种。参考内容在后面，按需查看。

            下载录音

            录音按题保存在本浏览器；换设备请下载音频，文字备份不包含声音。

            参考作答

            Free admission can encourage local people to return regularly, especially families who would otherwise have to pay for several tickets. Museums may still need income for staff and maintenance, though, so one option is to offer free entry to the permanent collection and charge for some temporary exhibitions.

            Visitors can feel disappointed when the experience is very different from what was advertised. A famous view might be hidden by construction, or a small site might feel overcrowded after a long queue. Clear information beforehand can help, because people can decide whether the visit is still worth their time.

            逐项解释与练习

            free for locals 需要兼顾进入机会和维持服务的费用；给出永久展／临展的具体方案，不断言所有博物馆预算相同。失望问题用预期与实际落差串起施工、拥挤两例。

            练习：回应题目的一般判断或社会现象，提出理由、具体例子及适用条件。个人经历可以作例证，但不要用个人故事代替讨论。先独立口头作答，再检查是否回应问法。

            竞争与参与：比较体育观点

            竞争与参与：比较体育观点

            本单元使用真实 Part 3 问题。先看完整问题组，再比较参考作答如何逐问落实内容；人物经历为参考作答中的示例，不是原题事实或统一标准答案。

            1. How important is it to be very competitive at sport?
            2. Why do some people think that taking part in sport is more important than winning?

            先留下自己的回答

            可以直接开口，也可以先写文字草稿；录音和文字任选一种。参考内容在后面，按需查看。

            下载录音

            录音按题保存在本浏览器；换设备请下载音频，文字备份不包含声音。

            参考作答

            It depends on the purpose. For professional athletes, a strong desire to compete may help them keep training when progress is slow. In a casual game with friends, however, enjoying the activity and playing fairly may matter more than the result. Being competitive becomes a problem if it encourages someone to ignore rules or injuries.

            People who value participation often focus on the benefits that continue after a match ends, such as exercise, friendships and learning to work with others. Only one team can win, but both teams can gain those benefits. That is especially relevant when children are just starting a sport.

            逐项解释与练习

            首问用 professional / casual 区分目的；第二问解释 taking part 的评价标准，不是说胜负永远无意义。Only one team can win 对比双方都能得到的长期收益，让观点可见。

            练习：回应题目的一般判断或社会现象，提出理由、具体例子及适用条件。个人经历可以作例证，但不要用个人故事代替讨论。先独立口头作答，再检查是否回应问法。

            真实回答：家乡的四次问答

            完整正式题面

            Part 1 Introduction and interview

            [This part of the test begins with the examiner introducing himself or herself and checking the candidate’s identification. It then continues as an interview.]

            Let’s talk about your home town or village.

            • What kind of place is it? • What’s the most interesting part of your town/village? • What kind of jobs do the people in your town/village do? • Would you say it’s a good place to live? (Why?)

            Let’s move on to talk about accommodation.

            • Tell me about the kind of accommodation you live in? • How long have you lived there? • What do you like about living there? • What sort of accommodation would you most like to live in?

            官方样本节选：家乡四问转写（未附本段官方分数）

            Part 1 Introduction and interview

            [This part of the test begins with the examiner introducing himself or herself and checking the candidate’s identification. It then continues as an interview.]

            Transcript

            Examiner: Now, in this first part, I’d like to ask you some more questions about yourself, OK? Let’s talk about your home town or village. What kind of place is it?

            Candidate: It’s quite a small village, about 20km from Zurich. And it’s very quiet. And we have only little ... two little shops because most of the people work in Zurich or are orientated to the city.

            Examiner: What’s the most interesting part of this place ... village?

            Candidate: On the top of a hill we have a little castle which is very old and quite well known in Switzerland.

            Examiner: What kind of jobs do people in the village do?

            Candidate: We have some farmers in the village as well as people who work in Zurich as bankers or journalists or there are also teachers and some doctors, some medicines.

            Examiner: Would you say it’s a good place to live?

            Candidate: Yes. Although it is very quiet, it is … people are friendly and I would say it is a good place to live there, yes.

            Examiner: Let’s move on to talk about accommodation. Tell me about the kind of accommodation you live in ...

            回答与证据解释

            四问依次问类型、特色、工作、居住评价。原回答用距苏黎世20km、山上城堡、农民／银行职员／记者、安静但友善逐项回应。注意这是公开考生实录，含自我修正和语言瑕疵，并非无误范文：some medicines 应改为 some doctors 或其他人物职业；不要照背。练习：逐题用一个具体事实支持结论，再复述连接关系。

            完整正式题面

            Part 3 – Two-way discussion

            Let’s consider first of all how people’s values have changed.

            • What kind of things give status to people in your country? • Have things changed since your parents’ time?

            Finally, let’s talk about the role of advertising.

            • Do you think advertising influences what people buy?

            官方样本节选：地位象征与未来追问（未附本段官方分数）

            Part 3 – Two-way discussion

            Transcript

            Examiner: We’ve been talking about things we own. I’d like to discuss with you one or two more general questions relating to this topic. First, let’s consider values and the way they can change. In Switzerland, what kind of possessions do you think give status to people?

            Candidate: The first thing which comes in my mind is the car. Yes, because lots of people like to have posh cars or expensive cars to show their status, their place in the society.

            Examiner: Is that a new development?

            Candidate: No, I think it isn’t.

            Examiner: People have thought like that for quite a long time?

            Candidate: Yes. Another thing is probably the clothing. It starts already when you are young. When the children go to school they want to have posh labels on their jumpers or good shoes.

            Examiner: What do you think of this way of thinking, that I need to have a car or certain clothes to show my status?

            Candidate: Probably it’s sometimes a replacement for something you don’t have, so if your wife has left you or your girlfriend, you just buy some new, I don’t know, new watches or new clothes to make you satisfied again.

            Examiner: You don’t think of it as a healthy way of thinking?

            Candidate: It’s probably not honest to yourself. You can understand what I mean?

            Examiner: Yes. And do you think this will change? In the future, will cars and designer clothes be status symbols in the same way?

            Candidate: I’m sure that clothes will be ... that the thing with the clothes will be the same. I’m not so sure about the cars because cars cause lots of environmental problems and probably in some years, a few years, this will change because it’s not reasonable to drive a car anymore.

            Examiner: Can you tell me a little bit more about that? ...

            回答与证据解释

            第一组问答以汽车、服装说明地位象征；追问要求评价和未来判断。回答预测衣服仍重要，但汽车可能因环境问题改变；probably / not so sure 呈现不确定性。示范不是事实调查：应标为考生观点。原表达 first thing which comes in my mind 可改为 first thing that comes to mind；in the society 一般改为 in society。

            重要物品 · 口语 Part 2

            Part 2 – Individual long turn

            Candidate Task Card

            Describe something you own which is very important to you.

            You should say:

            • where you got it from
            • how long you have had it
            • what you use it for

            and explain why it is important to you.

            You will have to talk about the topic for 1 to 2 minutes.

            You have one minute to think about what you’re going to say.

            You can make some notes to help you if you wish.

            Rounding off questions

            • Is it valuable in terms of money?
            • Would it be easy to replace?

            一次只修一处。若需要句型或关键词支持，如实标记；修改稿不替代自己的下一次开口。

            完成后核对 · 答案、讲解与可接受表达
            先说过再听 · Part 2 考生示例

            先保留自己的首答，再看例句和示范。

            一条具体反馈可以怎样给

            首答实际出现的情况 一次可做的修复 怎么判断
            说了物品名称，反复说重要，却没有具体说明 选择一个真实愿意分享的用途、来历或小经历，把它与重要性连起来 重答中听者能指出“为什么”，而不只听到更多形容词
            想说拥有多久，但结构影响意思 先理清得到它的时间和拥有状态是否持续到现在，再选表达 新回答的时间关系清楚；不只检查有没有出现现在完成时
            某个表达想不起来 先用已会的词解释功能或特点，再按需要补一个表达 合法换说法同样算沟通成功；不用为了高级词停在那里
            具体某段声音难懂 定位这一处，先核对你原本想说的意思，再针对实际听见的问题练一小段 要听新录音检查，不通过一份改好的文字稿推断发音已改善

            每次只选一行，不把它们变成四份作业。不确定原因时，可以先请对方复述听到的意思，或保留这一处等待反馈；不要根据口音标签笼统评价能力。

            如果首答暂时组织不出：可选的短讲支架

            仅在首答已经保存、实际需要帮助时使用，替换本章原来的 3–5 分钟修复准备与一次重答，不新增一轮练习。先给自己约两分钟，用几个关键词选定一个用途或经历；随后用约半分钟把这件事说清楚。下次相应口语时段再逐步缩短准备、增加展开，向正式的一分钟准备与一至两分钟回答靠近，不要求当天完成全部阶段。

            先缩短准备与讲话时间，练习把一件事说清楚，再逐步扩展到题卡中的其他要点。

            两个可选结构

            持续拥有：I've had it for three years. / I've had it since I started university.

            for 接一段时间，since 接起点；表达的是拥有状态持续到现在。也可以说 I got it three years ago, and I still use it.，同样把时间与当前关系说清楚。过去得到某物可以用过去时，不要求整段统一用一种时态。

            个人意义：It means a lot to me because my sister made it for me. / It's special to me because it reminds me of our trips together.

            这里表达个人重视程度，不等于市场价格高。来源、使用经验、功能或个人联系都可以支持重要性，不必强写家庭故事或煽情经历。

            选择其中一项，用你自己的物品和意思说一句，再放回短回答中。标 K 以前会用／R 认识但少用／N 本次新学；照着本页说记“有提示”。special to me 等合法替代记任务成功，目标结构的独立提取另记。

            自己说过后，再听真实样例

            这段 Part 2 示例录音回答重要物品题。听听考生怎样交代物品、经历和个人意义。

            示例 MP3 文件 · 文字稿

            听完只回答一个问题：这位考生怎样从物品用途说到对自己的重要性？然后回到自己的物品，决定有没有值得补充的具体信息。若本次时间已用完，示例移到下一次，并替换原定回听活动。

            已核对的文字稿中，考生选择钢琴，提到得到它的经历、弹奏的用途及其个人意义。稿中也保留学习者错误；例如用 I have it for about nine years 表示一直拥有，教学中可以修为 I've had it for about nine years。这只是时间表达的局部修复，不是给原考生重新评分。

            与正式口语评价的关系

            依据本地口语评价说明，完整评价包括流利与连贯、词汇、语法范围与准确性、发音。先处理一个问题是本次教学范围，不意味着其他维度不重要。

            正式口语中，连贯的口头表达可以有自然停顿、简略结构和口语衔接，不按作文标准要求每句话都像书面句。词汇反馈既看范围，也看意思、搭配和必要时的换说法；发音反馈必须依据声音和可理解性。

            题卡要点可帮助组织内容，但不机械转成“一点一分”的评分。完成一个两分钟回答、使用某个句型或减少一次停顿，都不足以单独确定 band。完整表现还需包含其他部分及真实追问。

            可选：换一道题再试

            下次口语时段用约 8—12 分钟完成原物品短回忆、原题卡的同话题追问和折叠区的新追问，分别记录熟内容与新问题。活动情境只在时间允许时做，否则顺延。每项都要实际开口录音；这些局部任务不等同完整口语检查，第 2 周另用未预习的 P1—3 任务替换主任务。

            安排在之后一个口语时段，约 8–12 分钟，替换原定练习。先关闭参考和样例，不预先写好完整答案。本页要求自己开口并录音。

            A. 熟题与同题追问分开记

            先用约半分钟说清原来那件物品为什么重要，保存这次声音。它是熟内容回忆，不是新的 Part 2 限时测试。

            随后看原题卡中的一个真实追问：Would it be easy to replace? 实际口头回答；不用固定句数，只把判断和相关原因说清楚。这是同一话题的追问，不是另一套陌生话题。若上次已经准备过它，标熟问。

            替换问题可能涉及买到功能相同的东西，也可能涉及个人意义是否能替代。可以区分两者，也可以依据自己的物品作其他成立解释；没有统一的 yes 或 no 正确答案。

            B. 一个新追问

            准备好录音后再打开问题。它由工作区编写，不是公开真题或预测题。

            录音准备好后看新问题

            If you could change one thing about this object, what would you change, and why?

            实际说出你会怎样选择；不要求为了回答而必须改变物品，也不强制假设句型。保留你有没有提前见过问题、有没有使用提示。追问可以观察临场调整，但没有校准难度，不能用于换算 band。

            C. 换到另一个语境的短表达

            若还有时间，用英语实际说出你喜欢的一项活动怎样对你有意义，并给一个具体说明。不要只是把原来物品名称机械换成活动名称；内容可以是用途、体验或个人重视的原因。此题是教学迁移，不是另一道Part 2。

            不要求套用上次的 mean a lot to；清楚自然的替代表达同样成功。题目不问拥有时间，就无需硬塞 I've had...。如果这部分导致总用时超出本次安排，移到下次，不补成额外作业。

            完成后看核对原则

            新追问检查是否真的回应“改变什么与为什么”，而不只是重新讲它多重要。活动题检查能否重新组织意义；例如说喜欢画画，还需要说明画画给自己的体验或作用，不能只重复喜欢。

            可以有不同判断，没有固定标准答案。请回听实际录音，记录一条有效表达和一处仍需帮助的问题。仅凭转写文本可看部分内容与用法，不能据此判发音或真实流利度。

            后续完整口语检查

            本章只提供 Part 2 局部与追问证据。后续另安排覆盖 Part 1–3 的未预习完整练习，按当前口语格式控制三个部分与整体 11–14 分钟，并保留完整原音。准备与反馈时间另外计入当天预算，替换当天主任务，不再额外叠加。

            熟悉本页物品题后，它不能再当完整练习中未见的 Part 2。可以从本地训练资料选择确实未准备过的任务组合，避免使用保留材料作反复教学。若由同伴或老师提问，应允许真实追问；若只有自己依次看题录答，明确是自练，尚未检验互动听问和即时应答的全部条件。

            证据类型 本次如何标记
            原物品内容重答 熟内容回忆
            原题卡追加问题 同话题追问，注明是否准备过
            工作区新追问 自编教学题；首次／见过／提示后
            活动语境 换情境表达，内容熟悉程度另记
            后续完整练习 覆盖范围、是否预习、提问形式、完整录音

            熟题说顺与陌生互动可能表现不同；分别保留，不从一次卡顿推断焦虑，也不因同题重答流畅就宣布整科提分。

            按本区各任务实际录答：熟片短回忆、即时追问和活动短答分别注明条件，不统一套用 Part 2 准备时间。点击录音会请求麦克风权限；也可以用自己的录音器。

            完整正式题面

            Part 2 – Individual long turn

            Candidate Task Card

            Describe something you own which is very important to you.

            You should say:

            where you got it from how long you have had it what you use it for

            and explain why it is important to you.

            You will have to talk about the topic for 1 to 2 minutes. You have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes to help you if you wish.

            Rounding off questions

            • Is it valuable in terms of money? • Would it be easy to replace?

            完整回答转写

            Part 2 – Individual long turn

            Transcript

            Examiner: Alright? Remember you have one to two minutes for this, so don’t worry if I stop you. I’ll tell you when the time is up.

            Candidate: OK

            Examiner: Can you start speaking now, please?

            Candidate: Yes. One of the most important things I have is my piano because I like playing the piano. I got it from my parents to my twelve birthday, so I have it for about nine years, and the reason why it is so important for me is that I can go into another world when I’m playing piano. I can forget what’s around me and what ... I can forget my problems and this is sometimes quite good for a few minutes. Or I can play to relax or just, yes to … to relax and to think of something completely different.

            Examiner: Thank you. Would it be easy to replace this, this piano?

            Candidate: Yes, I think it wouldn’t be that big problem but I like my piano as it is because I have it from my parents, it’s some kind unique for me.

            回答与证据解释

            原回答覆盖物品（piano）、来源（parents）、时间（12岁生日、约9年）、重要性（放松、暂时忘掉问题）；追问 replace 区分功能可替代与情感独特。原录音有错误：to my twelve birthday 可改为 for my twelfth birthday；I have it for about nine years 改为 I have had it for about nine years。改写是教学修正，不伪称原录音如此说。

            TOPIC 02

            工作：收入、稳定性与生活安排

            讨论工作时，可以把收入、稳定性、工作内容和时间安排分开看。薪水相同的两份工作，通勤距离、学习机会和照顾家庭的空间可能不同；灵活安排也可能指时间灵活，或地点灵活。远程办公的争论不只是家里与办公室哪个好，还涉及岗位是否适合远程完成、同事怎样协作，以及新人如何获得指导。判断最好联系具体岗位和人的需要。

            先分清三个概念

            概念它指什么不要混淆
            job security对工作能否持续、是否可能失去岗位的稳定预期。工作稳定不等于工作令人满意；一个人可能希望保住岗位，同时不喜欢具体工作内容。
            flexible working arrangements在工作时间、地点或安排方式上提供一定选择。可以调整上下班时间与可以在家工作不是同一件事；灵活程度也不表示没有工作责任。
            work-life balance让工作要求与休息、家庭和其他个人生活需要能够相互协调。它不要求工作与生活各占一半时间；不同阶段、家庭责任和个人偏好会影响具体安排。

            读一段背景英语

            People may value different things in a job. For one person, a steady income may be the main concern. For another, opportunities to learn or time with family may matter more. Working from home is one possible arrangement, but it does not suit every role or every worker. Someone who writes reports may be able to complete many tasks at home, while a mechanic needs access to vehicles and equipment. Even within an office team, some tasks require quiet concentration and others benefit from direct discussion. The useful question is therefore how to organise the work. Clear responsibilities, suitable equipment and opportunities to ask for help are relevant whether employees work at home or in a shared workplace.
            中文帮助理解

            选择工作时，人们重视的条件可能不同：有人最在意稳定收入，有人更看重学习机会或陪伴家人的时间。在家工作只是众多安排中的一种，并不适合所有岗位。写报告的人可能在家完成不少任务，修理汽车的人则需要接触车辆与设备。同一个团队里，也会同时存在需要安静专注和需要直接讨论的任务。因此，讨论重点可以落在工作怎样组织：责任是否清楚、设备是否合适、遇到问题能否获得帮助，而不是笼统判断某个地点永远更好。

            相关练习

            本册就业图比较美国四个行业的岗位数量变化。岗位数、收入、工作稳定性是不同的信息；图里没有的原因，不能自行写成事实。

            这个话题通常怎样展开

            以下为教学归纳的讨论角度，不是考试频率排名或原题清单。

            • 选择工作时，收入、稳定性、兴趣和发展机会应怎样权衡？（教学概括，非原题）
            • 哪些工作安排适合远程完成，哪些需要现场协作？（教学概括，非原题）
            • 雇主可以怎样支持员工学习，同时安排好工作责任？（教学概括，非原题）

            可以直接理解和借用的搭配

            本组是教学选用搭配与例句，尚未逐组统计真题频率。

            搭配与意思放进句子里
            earn a living
            谋生，获得维持生活所需的收入            		Some people earn a living by repairing household equipment.
            gain work experience
            获得工作经验            		A placement can give students a chance to gain work experience.
            balance work and family responsibilities
            协调工作与家庭责任            		Flexible starting times may help some employees balance work and family responsibilities.
            work flexible hours
            在一定范围内灵活安排工作时间            		She works flexible hours but attends the weekly team meeting.
            provide training for employees
            为员工提供培训            		The company provides training for employees who need to use new equipment.

            读过背景后，需要练习时再进入：Task 1 · Task 2。已读过原句或提示的任务，记为学习后应用。

            从工作条件说到生活安排

            下面两个情境为本册编写。先分清“时间、地点、稳定性”，再用正式口语样本观察怎样解释工作与休息的关系。

            1. 甲可以在家工作，但每天必须在线到晚上十点。乙必须到工作场所，但下班时间固定。谁的工作地点更灵活？能否据此断定谁有更好的 work-life balance？还需要哪些信息？
            2. 一份工作薪水较高，但短期合同即将到期；另一份收入较低，长期合同和工时较稳定。说明两者在收入与 job security 上的取舍。为需要接送孩子的人提出一种具体安排，并说明岗位能否支持它。
            完成后核对

            ① 甲的地点选择更多，但长时间在线可能减少休息；还要看总工时、通勤、家庭责任和个人需要。工作地点灵活不自动等于生活更平衡。② 合同期限与稳定预期有关，薪水高低是另一维度；固定提前下班或错峰上班可能有帮助，但需要覆盖岗位职责，不能直接假定所有岗位都能远程完成。

            正式口语样本：Monika 的工作与休闲讨论

            在 IELTS 官方样本页 找到 Band 8 | Monika, Germany，播放工作与休闲部分，或展开转写。本段用来观察理由怎样展开；示例中的社会情况是考生当时的看法。

            中文任务提要：考官顺着她关于工作和休闲失衡的观点，要求进一步解释。她将岗位竞争与保住工作、加班、休闲时间减少和家庭生活联系起来。

            1. 按“压力来源 → 工作行为 → 生活影响”记录她的解释链。
            2. 她关于未来的回答是确定事实还是预测？记录她怎样限制确定程度。
            3. 给自己熟悉的一种岗位提出改善时间安排的办法，用两句说明效果和限制。
            完成后核对

            核对：岗位竞争／保住工作的压力 → 增加加班 → 休闲与家庭时间受到挤压。未来部分带有不确定性，是预测。考官认可长回答的连贯展开、词汇与语音表现，同时指出少数搭配和时态问题；官方 8 分针对该考生表现。

            原创参考：A customer-service team could stagger its shifts so that some staff finish earlier without leaving the service desk unattended. This would require enough staff during busy periods, so a very small team might have less flexibility. 先给安排，再补适用条件；不用把灵活工作说成对所有人都有效。

            延伸阅读：制糖业中的历史劳工

            同话题的独立阅读题：健康与消费：读出作者评价 →

            六段个人生活背景

            社会话题之外，也需要能谈住所、关系、选择和经历。下面每段提供一个具体语境，不需要背成自己的答案；留意怎样用简单词表达可见的细节。

            居住经验：城市的吸引力与取舍

            居住经验：城市的吸引力与取舍

            本单元复用同一正式题卡，练习个人经历组织；不计作另一道新题。

            把题目中的 some people 与自己的喜好分开。先说生活体验，再用交通或安静程度解释，不能把示范中的价值判断当作所有人的看法。

            城市生活：吸引力与不便

            本单元选用真实 Part 1 问题组中的两问。先分别口头作答，再比较参考写法如何回应问题；示例经历由本地编写，不是官方考生作答或统一标准答案。

            1. Do you think cities are exciting places to live?
            2. Why do some people dislike living in a city?

            参考作答

            Yes, they can be. I enjoy having different places to eat and events to choose from, even if I don't go out every evening. Just knowing that I could try something new makes the city feel lively to me.

            I think the noise and crowds put some people off. A journey that looks short on a map can also take a long time during rush hour. If someone values peace and easy access to nature, those everyday frustrations may matter more than the entertainment a city offers.

            逐项解释与练习

            两问视角不同：自己的兴奋感与 some people 的不喜欢。第二答不用 everyone hates，保留人群条件；rush hour 举出具体不便，最后说明不同价值取舍。

            练习：保留题目中的对象、时间和问法，换成自己的真实经历。先口头作答，再对照上面的具体内容逐项检查；不需要逐字背诵参考作答。

            完整原件：Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · Test 2 · 物理页54 / 印刷页53

            认识的人：竞争心如何体现

            认识的人：竞争心如何体现

            本单元复用同一正式题卡，练习个人经历组织；不计作另一道新题。

            用真实人物与可回忆事件替换大学朋友；分别核对认识方式、竞争领域、成功程度和你的解释。成功不必等于冠军，进入决赛同样可以描述。

            有竞争心的人：具体事件支撑性格

            本单元使用真实 Part 2 题卡。先准备 1 分钟，再连续说 1–2 分钟；对照参考写法检查内容是否充分展开。示例经历由本地编写，不是官方考生作答或经考官评分的高分案例。

            1. Describe a person you know who is very competitive.
            2. who this person is
            3. what this person is competitive about
            4. how successful this person is
            5. and explain why you think this person is so competitive.

            参考作答

            I'd like to describe a friend I met at university. We used to play badminton together, and he was much more competitive about it than anyone else in our group. Even during a casual game, he remembered the score carefully and tried to work out why he had lost a point.

            He wasn't the best player when we first met, but he practised regularly and gradually started winning more matches. One year he reached the final of a small competition organised by our club. He didn't win, but he was pleased that the extra practice had made a difference.

            I think his competitiveness comes from wanting to see measurable progress. He likes having a clear target, and a match gives him immediate feedback. He can get frustrated with himself, although he usually congratulates the other player afterwards. That's why I enjoy playing with him: he takes the game seriously without treating his opponent badly. I wouldn't claim to know everything that motivates him, but improvement seems more important to him than showing off.

            逐项解释与练习

            who=university friend；what=badminton；success=club final但未夺冠；why=measurable progress。第三段用 I think / seems 标明动机推断，避免把性格解释写成已核实的心理事实。竞争心用记分、分析失分、练习行动展示，不只重复 competitive。

            练习：保留题目中的对象、时间和问法，换成自己的真实经历。先口头作答，再对照上面的具体内容逐项检查；不需要逐字背诵参考作答。

            完整原件：Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · Test 4 · 物理页97 / 印刷页96

            Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · Test 4 · 物理页97 / 印刷页96

            日常选择：付款与购买教训

            日常选择：付款与购买教训

            本单元复用同一正式题卡，练习个人经历组织；不计作另一道新题。

            保留usually与Have you ever的时态差异；把示例鞋子换成自己确实买过但用得少的东西，明确价格诱因与实际需求不同。

            购物方式与不必要消费

            本单元选用真实 Part 1 问题组中的两问。先分别口头作答，再比较参考写法如何回应问题；示例经历由本地编写，不是官方考生作答或统一标准答案。

            1. When you go shopping, do you usually pay for things by cash or by card?
            2. Have you ever spent money on something you didn't need?

            参考作答

            I usually pay by card because I don't like carrying a lot of cash. It's also easier to check what I've spent afterwards. I still keep a little cash with me in case a shop's card machine isn't working.

            Yes, I once bought a pair of trainers mainly because they were on sale. I already had a similar pair, so I hardly wore the new ones. It wasn't a disaster, but it did make me stop and think before buying something just because the price looks attractive.

            逐项解释与练习

            两题分开回答：usually 对应现在的习惯与一个例外；Have you ever 对应 yes 后的一次经历，主要叙述用过去时。sale 不等于 need，结尾明确反思怎样从经历产生。

            练习：保留题目中的对象、时间和问法，换成自己的真实经历。先口头作答，再对照上面的具体内容逐项检查；不需要逐字背诵参考作答。

            兴趣与地方：观察公园细节

            兴趣与地方：观察公园细节

            本单元复用同一正式题卡，练习个人经历组织；不计作另一道新题。

            先按题卡地点、规模、所见、兴趣完成，再试用两句讲菜地为什么改变你对公园的印象。不要只列设施名字。

            公园：从空间细节讲清兴趣

            本单元使用真实 Part 2 题卡。先准备 1 分钟，再连续说 1–2 分钟；对照参考写法检查内容是否充分展开。示例经历由本地编写，不是官方考生作答或经考官评分的高分案例。

            1. Describe an interesting garden or park you have seen.
            2. where this garden or park is
            3. how big it is
            4. what you saw in this garden/park
            5. and explain why you think this garden/park is interesting.

            参考作答

            I'd like to talk about a park near the railway station in a city I visited last spring. It wasn't enormous; I could walk from one entrance to the other in about fifteen minutes. Even so, it contained several different areas, and that made it feel larger than it actually was.

            Near the entrance there was an open lawn where families were sitting. Further along, a narrow path led past flower beds to a small pond. I also noticed a section where local residents were growing vegetables. There were simple labels beside the plants, so visitors could see what was being grown.

            What interested me most was the contrast between the busy streets outside and the way people used the park. Some were exercising, while others were just talking or reading. The vegetable plots made it feel like a place that residents helped shape, rather than somewhere people only passed through. I spent longer there than I had planned because there was something different to notice around each corner.

            逐项解释与练习

            题卡 how big 用 walk across in about fifteen minutes 给感知尺度，不虚报面积。what saw 是草坪／池塘／菜地；interesting 由居民参与与外部繁忙街道的对比解释。不要只罗列设施而漏掉为什么有趣。

            练习：保留题目中的对象、时间和问法，换成自己的真实经历。先口头作答，再对照上面的具体内容逐项检查；不需要逐字背诵参考作答。

            完整原件：Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · Test 3 · 物理页75 / 印刷页74

            Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · Test 3 · 物理页75 / 印刷页74

            经历与变化：核对一条信息

            经历与变化：核对一条信息

            本单元复用同一正式题卡，练习个人经历组织；不计作另一道新题。

            参考答题情节只是示例；若自己没有图书馆经历，应换真实的不实消息。要解释怀疑根据与核对方法，不需要编造戏剧性诈骗。

            不真实的信息：发现问题与核对

            本单元使用真实 Part 2 题卡。先准备 1 分钟，再连续说 1–2 分钟；对照参考写法检查内容是否充分展开。示例经历由本地编写，不是官方考生作答或经考官评分的高分案例。

            1. Describe a time when you read or heard something that you thought was not true.
            2. where you read/heard this
            3. what you read/heard
            4. why you thought it was not true
            5. and explain how you felt about reading/hearing this thing that you thought was not true.

            参考作答

            I remember seeing a message in a group chat saying that our university library would close for an entire month. It appeared just before an important assignment was due, so several people were worried. The message looked like a screenshot of an announcement, but it didn't include a date or a link to the original notice.

            I doubted it because I had been in the library that morning and had seen nothing about a long closure. Rather than immediately telling everyone the message was wrong, I checked the library website. The actual notice said that one reading room would close for repairs while the rest of the building remained open.

            At first I felt anxious, because I depended on the library for a quiet place to study. Once I had checked the notice, I felt relieved and a little frustrated that an incomplete message had caused so much confusion. I shared the link with the group and explained the difference. The experience reminded me to check the original context before passing on information that sounds urgent.

            逐项解释与练习

            where=group chat；what=whole library closed one month；why=different recent observation + original notice核对；feelings=anxious→relieved/frustrated。题目是 thought not true，先怀疑再核对比把直觉当证据更清楚。本文事件是原创参考作答，不是新增真题文本。

            练习：保留题目中的对象、时间和问法，换成自己的真实经历。先口头作答，再对照上面的具体内容逐项检查；不需要逐字背诵参考作答。

            完整原件：Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · Test 2 · 物理页54 / 印刷页53

            旅行计划：信息怎样帮助行动

            旅行计划：信息怎样帮助行动

            本单元复用同一正式题卡，练习个人经历组织；不计作另一道新题。

            同一旅游信息原题在这里复习个人经历表达。核对来源、地点、内容、作用四点，说明一项具体信息怎样影响你的行动。

            旅游信息：一次具体使用经历

            本单元使用真实 Part 2 题卡。先准备 1 分钟，再连续说 1–2 分钟；对照参考写法检查内容是否充分展开。示例经历由本地编写，不是官方考生作答或经考官评分的高分案例。

            1. Describe a time when you used information for tourists, for example from a guidebook or online.
            2. where you got this information
            3. what place this information was about
            4. what information you got
            5. and explain whether this information was very helpful for you.

            参考作答

            I'd like to talk about some information I found on a museum's website before a weekend trip. I was planning to visit the city with my cousin, and neither of us knew the area well. We only had one afternoon there, so I wanted to find out what we could realistically fit in.

            The website explained how to get from the railway station to the museum. It also showed the opening hours, the ticket prices and the times of the guided tours. The most useful detail was that the last admission was earlier than the closing time. Without that warning, we might have arrived too late.

            I saved the directions on my phone and booked a tour for the middle of the afternoon. The information was helpful because we spent less time making decisions after we arrived. One bus stop had temporarily moved, so we still had to ask someone for help. Even so, having the basic plan meant that this small problem didn't spoil the visit.

            逐项解释与练习

            题卡四点依次落在 museum website（来源）、museum in a city（地点）、交通／开放时间／最后入场时间（内容）、节省决策时间但公交站临时改变（有帮助与局限）。最后一项不是只说 useful：last admission 的具体后果解释了价值。练习核对：来源不应只说 online 而不说明什么网页；也无需编成网页永远准确。

            练习：保留题目中的对象、时间和问法，换成自己的真实经历。先口头作答，再对照上面的具体内容逐项检查；不需要逐字背诵参考作答。

            Task 1 · 折线图

            四行业就业

            选出主要变化，再用成组比较支持概览

            回到原题入口
            查看题面与图表 · 来源
            The graph below gives information about the number of jobs in four sectors of the economy in the US between 1960 and 2020.

            Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 30 页

            参考置信度：高（题面与来源已核对；练习讲解为编写内容）

            回到原题入口
            提纲首稿检查与修订可选 · 再写

            01 / 审题与提纲

            用自己的话概括与比较图示，至少 150 词，建议约 20 分钟。 可直接开始首稿；提纲为可选准备。

            需要提示：看一种审题与展开方法

            先分清净变化与中途峰值：制造业从 15 到 13 million，净减少 2 million；不能把 1980 年峰值 20 到终点 13 的差当作全期净变化。零售和医疗都在 16 million 结束，但分别从 6 与 2 起步。概览突出主导行业改变与农业整体下降，细节段再用数字支持。

            Retail and healthcare both employed sixteen million people in 2020, although healthcare had started from a much lower base.

            这句把共同终点与不同起点放在同一个比较里。它不能替代整篇概览，也不解释图中未给出的社会原因。

            以上为本地教学示范，不是官方范文或评分。

            首稿 · 美国四行业就业：峰值、交叉与最终排名

            Task 1 · 流程图

            砖块制造

            区分顺序与分支，准确描述工序

            回到原题入口
            查看题面与图表 · 来源
            The diagram below shows the process by which bricks are manufactured for the building industry.

            Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

            官方样题 · IELTS Academic Writing Sample Tasks (2023) · PDF 第 5 页

            参考置信度：高（题面与来源已核对；练习讲解为编写内容）

            回到原题入口
            提纲首稿检查与修订可选 · 再写

            01 / 审题与提纲

            用自己的话概括与比较图示，至少 150 词，建议约 20 分钟。 可直接开始首稿；提纲为可选准备。

            需要提示：看一种审题与展开方法

            先沿箭头走一遍：成形有 wire cutter 与 mould 两条路径，随后都进入干燥，并非每块砖先切再压。温度属于两段 kiln，24–48 hours 属于干燥，48–72 hours 属于冷却。总览可以概括从取土到配送的工业过程，不必机械数出可能有歧义的步骤总数。

            The clay mixture is shaped into bricks either with a wire cutter or in moulds before being dried for 24 to 48 hours.

            either ... or ... 表达备选成形路径，before 表达共同后续步骤。被动语态把砖与原料放在信息中心，但不要求每一句都用被动。

            以上为本地教学示范，不是官方范文或评分。

            首稿 · 制砖：并行成形路径与温度阶段

            学院咖啡厅改造

            用空间分组呈现变化，避免逐项罗列

            回到原题入口
            查看题面与图表 · 来源
            The plans below show a college café before it was redesigned and how it looks now.

            Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 52 页

            参考置信度：高（题面与来源已核对；练习讲解为编写内容）

            回到原题入口
            提纲首稿检查与修订可选 · 再写

            01 / 审题与提纲

            用自己的话概括与比较图示，至少 150 词，建议约 20 分钟。 可直接开始首稿；提纲为可选准备。

            需要提示：看一种审题与展开方法

            先在原图核对每个设施的旧位置和新位置，再选择按区域或按功能分段。只有旧设施消失、同处出现新设施，才使用 replaced by；设施仍在但改到别处，用 relocated 或 moved。图未给出方位标时，用 to the left of、near the entrance 等实际可见参照，不自行指定东西南北。

            The seating area has been relocated closer to the entrance.

            这只是“设施搬迁”的表达示范，并非对本题图面的事实断言。写进作文前，必须核对图中是否真的同时显示搬迁与靠近入口。

            以上为本地教学示范，不是官方范文或评分。

            Task 2 · 教育

            小学课堂中的学习与游戏

            回应两个问题，并把游戏的价值写成因果链

            回到原题入口
            查看题面 · 来源
            Some people argue that primary schools focus too much on formal learning. To what extent do you agree with this opinion? How important do you think it is for children to play as well as learn in the primary school classroom?

            Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 96 页

            参考置信度：高（题面与来源已核对；练习讲解为编写内容）

            回到原题入口
            阅读后写作 · 本题可用表达

            写作前置 · 文中表达

            下面的表达来自阅读材料，例句按本题语境编写。选择确实需要的表达即可。

            Multilingualism · 迁移背景与研究目标

            differs from the language used at home

            与家庭语言不同

            适合解释某些儿童理解课堂内容时面临的额外要求，避免把语言差异等同于能力不足。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            When the language of classroom instruction differs from the language used at home, play with pictures and objects may help children understand and express ideas.

            小学正式学习与游戏题关注课堂学习体验；可用来说明具体情境下游戏和实物活动怎样支持理解，不把游戏宣称为所有语言困难的解决方案。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Multilingualism · 教学语言与出人意料的结果

            little room for independent learning

            自主学习机会不足

            用来描述过度由教师控制的课堂，需要说明儿童缺少哪些探索或表达机会。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            A timetable dominated by teacher-led exercises may leave little room for independent learning through play.

            与小学正式教学和课堂游戏的平衡直接吻合，可具体表达过度正式教学的局限。

            回到这份材料的精读

            提纲首稿检查与修订可选 · 再写

            01 / 审题与提纲

            回应题目，用理由与例子支持立场，至少 250 词，建议约 40 分钟。 可直接开始首稿；提纲为可选准备。

            需要提示：看一种审题与展开方法

            “游戏有用”没有直接回答学校是否过分重视正式学习。先写清赞同程度，再解释游戏在课堂里承担什么功能。发展理由时，把抽象结果拆成可观察过程：儿童轮流参与游戏 → 必须倾听同伴并协商规则 → 有机会练习协作。例子应支持这个过程，不必编造调查比例。

            Structured games can complement formal lessons because children have to listen to one another and agree on rules. For example, a small-group shop game gives pupils a reason to practise numbers while taking turns as customers and sellers.

            这是自编假设课堂例子：它连接活动、机制与学习结果，没有把“有趣”直接等同“有效”。完整文章仍需明确回答两问并维持立场。

            以上为本地教学示范，不是官方范文或评分。

            首稿 · 小学正式学习与课堂游戏：两个问题分别回应

            可选 / 下次再写

            写 2–3 句立场与理由，同时回答两问；随后用一句说明什么情况下游戏不能替代直接讲授。

            展开参考与核对方法

            一种可行方向：部分学校过度依赖正式训练；有结构的游戏对语言与合作练习重要，但新概念仍需要清楚讲授。核对你的句子是否明确包含程度、重要性和边界，而不只说 play is useful。

            参考为编写内容；有其他准确且满足要求的表达。

            换到高层住宅题，先圈定 best，再用一句比较性立场回应；不要只说高层有优点。 打开下一题 →

            同题修订属于熟题练习；新题是否真的未见，请按自己的接触情况记录。

            Task 2 · 旅游

            旅游收益与居民成本

            比较利弊的分量，说明为什么一方更重要

            回到原题入口
            查看题面 · 来源
            International tourism has brought enormous benefit to many places. At the same time, there is concern about its impact on local inhabitants and the environment. Do the disadvantages of international tourism outweigh the advantages?

            Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

            官方样题 · IELTS Academic Writing Sample Tasks (2023) · PDF 第 7 页

            参考置信度：高（题面与来源已核对；练习讲解为编写内容）

            回到原题入口
            阅读后写作 · 本题可用表达

            写作前置 · 文中表达

            下面的表达来自阅读材料，例句按本题语境编写。选择确实需要的表达即可。

            Why we need silence｜噪声风险与城市降噪

            noise from aircraft

            飞机产生的噪声

            可用于旅游活动对机场附近居民的影响，须说明航班增长这一具体联系；不能把所有旅游目的地的主要问题一律写成航空噪声。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Where tourism leads to more frequent flights, noise from aircraft may become an additional burden for residents near airports.

            题目明确要求考虑旅游对当地居民与环境的影响；条件句把表达限定在航空活动增长的目的地。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Mapungubwe｜贸易、器物与衰落

            placed too much stress on local resources

            给当地资源带来过大压力

            可根据句子时态改为place或places，保留place stress on的搭配。谈旅游时应具体说明水、土地或公共设施等资源，不能把古代王国衰落直接当作现代旅游的实证。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Uncontrolled growth in visitor numbers could place too much stress on local resources, especially water supplies during the dry season.

            题目讨论旅游对当地环境与居民的代价；资源压力能够具体解释游客增长可能产生的成本。

            回到这份材料的精读

            提纲首稿检查与修订可选 · 再写

            01 / 审题与提纲

            回应题目，用理由与例子支持立场，至少 250 词，建议约 40 分钟。 可直接开始首稿；提纲为可选准备。

            需要提示：看一种审题与展开方法

            两边各列两个点不等于完成 outweigh。选择一条比较尺度，例如影响持续多久、影响谁、能否缓解，并在结论中解释为何这使一方更重。承认旅游创造收入后，可进一步问：收入是否留在当地、住房压力是否持续。政策例子是论证中的假设条件，不能当作题目已给出的事实。

            Tourism can support local shops, but this benefit may be seasonal. If homes are converted into holiday rentals throughout the year, residents may face a more persistent cost than the temporary jobs can offset.

            这是自编假设情境。seasonal 与 persistent 提供同一比较尺度；if 和 may 保留条件，避免把所有旅游城市说成同一种情况。

            以上为本地教学示范，不是官方范文或评分。

            首稿 · 国际旅游：经济收益与社区成本如何比较

            40:00到时保留输入，刷新后继续计时。

            用 60–80 词写一个权衡段：承认一项收益，说明一项居民成本，再明确为何其中一项更重。

            展开参考与核对方法

            自核：有一项明确收益、一项明确成本、一条共同比较尺度，以及权衡结论。若只写 However tourism also causes pollution，再罗列另一点，还需要补上为何更重。

            Task 2 · 城市住房

            高层住宅是否是最佳方案

            辨清 best 的比较要求，补足条件与因果

            回到原题入口
            查看题面 · 来源
            The best way to provide enough homes in large cities is to build tall apartment blocks. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

            Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 31 页

            参考置信度：高（题面与来源已核对；练习讲解为编写内容）

            回到原题入口
            阅读后写作 · 本题可用表达

            写作前置 · 文中表达

            下面的表达来自阅读材料，例句按本题语境编写。选择确实需要的表达即可。

            Dar es Salaam · 城市扩张与交通方案

            on the periphery

            在城市外围

            用于讨论住房位置与服务距离，需要说明外围扩张带来的具体条件，不能据此断定所有郊区住房都不好。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Building more homes on the periphery may lengthen journeys to work if public transport does not expand at the same time.

            高层住宅题涉及如何在大城市提供足够住房；这一表达帮助比较外围扩张与紧凑建设的出行影响。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Dar es Salaam · 公交设计与实际故障

            within a short walk of

            距……很近，步行即可到达

            说明住房与公交网络的空间联系；是否足够近应由实际布局支持。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Apartment blocks within a short walk of frequent public transport can provide more homes without making every resident dependent on a car.

            直接用于比较高层住宅的条件：密度优势需要交通可达性支持。

            回到这份材料的精读

            提纲首稿检查与修订可选 · 再写

            01 / 审题与提纲

            回应题目，用理由与例子支持立场，至少 250 词，建议约 40 分钟。 可直接开始首稿；提纲为可选准备。

            需要提示：看一种审题与展开方法

            “一栋楼能容纳更多住户”支持用地效率，却不能单独证明所有城市都应建高层，也不能保证房价下降。先区分供给数量与可负担性，再比较土地、基础设施与成本等条件。选少量相关条件展开，比列出许多没有解释的城市问题更有用。

            Tall apartment blocks can accommodate more households on a limited site, which makes them useful in areas where land is scarce. However, this does not automatically make housing affordable, because construction and maintenance costs may still be high.

            自编教学例句先说明机制，再限定推论。which 指向前句的空间效率；however 转向可负担性。文章还需解释这些条件如何影响最佳方案的判断。

            以上为本地教学示范，不是官方范文或评分。

            首稿 · 高层住宅是否是城市住房的最佳方案

Others argue that theatres and cinemas are still important both economically and culturally. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

            Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 53 页

            参考置信度：高（题面与来源已核对；练习讲解为编写内容）

            回到原题入口
            阅读后写作 · 本题可用表达

            写作前置 · 文中表达

            下面的表达来自阅读材料，例句按本题语境编写。选择确实需要的表达即可。

            The Davies Sisters｜印象派转向与战时收藏

            a vibrant artists' community

            一个充满活力的艺术家社群

            适合与support、sustain、help build搭配，讨论实体文化空间如何为创作者提供交流和演出机会。这里借用表达描述一种可能作用，不把文中救助艺术家的历史直接当成剧院效果的证据。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Local theatres can help sustain a vibrant artists' community by giving performers opportunities to work together and reach an audience.

            题目要求讨论剧院和影院的经济、文化价值；此表达适合展开剧院支持当地艺术生产和创作者交流的文化作用。

            回到这份材料的精读

            The Davies Sisters｜收藏停止与文化遗产

            a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy

            持久且有意义的文化遗产

            可用于讨论文化活动对未来的贡献，但要写清通过什么机制传承，例如保留地方戏剧、作品或表演传统，不能只用抽象赞美代替解释。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Theatres that preserve local plays and performance traditions can leave a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy for future generations.

            直接服务于实体剧院的文化价值：说明现场演出空间如何承载和传递传统，而不只比较观看的便利程度。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Miles Davis：困境、跨界与创造力

            draw wider audiences

            吸引范围更广的观众

            可具体说明线上娱乐的可达性；观众范围扩大不等于线下场所失去全部文化价值。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Online screenings can draw wider audiences than a small theatre can accommodate, especially when viewers live far from major cities.

            自编例句，直接回应线上娱乐的覆盖范围优势；can和especially保留条件，也为讨论剧院独有的现场体验留下空间。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Artificial Intelligence｜公众想象与解决一切的误区

            no shortage of

            大量；不缺

            可以承认数字内容数量充足，再讨论数量之外的体验差异。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            There is no shortage of films online, but access to a large catalogue does not reproduce the shared experience of a cinema.

            自编例句，直接回应线上娱乐与影院价值：先承认线上内容丰富，再解释共同观看体验这一文化维度。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Children who are brought up in families that do not have large amounts of money are better prepared to deal with the problems of adult life than children brought up by wealthy parents. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion?

            Multilingualism · 教学语言与出人意料的结果

            essential for day-to-day survival

            Some children learn practical skills essential for day-to-day survival, but this does not mean that financial hardship prepares every child better for adulthood.

            Task 2 · 同意程度

            科研由政府控制：公共利益与研究多样性

            从自己的首稿开始，按需要检查与修订。

            回到原题入口
            查看题面 · 来源
            Scientific research should be carried out and controlled by governments, rather than by private companies. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

            Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

            官方样题 · IELTS Academic Writing — modified large print · PDF 第 10 页

            参考置信度：高（题面与来源已核对；练习讲解为编写内容）

            回到原题入口
            阅读后写作 · 本题可用表达

            写作前置 · 文中表达

            下面的表达来自阅读材料，例句按本题语境编写。选择确实需要的表达即可。

            Do animals dream?｜章鱼行为与研究边界

            shed light on

            帮助增进理解

            常见搭配是research/findings may shed light on a process or question。适合讨论基础研究的潜在贡献，同时保留may、could等程度词，不把研究方向写成已经证实的成果。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Public funding can support basic research that may shed light on how memory works, even when there is no immediate commercial return.

            科研由政府还是企业控制的题目涉及研究激励；该表达可用于说明公共资金支持无即时商业回报的基础研究这一理由。它是写作中的政策论点，不是原文对资助模式作出的结论。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Artificial Intelligence｜公众想象与解决一切的误区

            setting unrealistic expectations about

            对……设定不切实际的预期

            可在avoid等动词后保留setting形式，具体说明期待的成果或时间；不把所有期待都说成不切实际。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Governments should avoid setting unrealistic expectations about how quickly publicly funded research can produce practical benefits.

            自编例句，贴合政府科研职责，说明资助研究时如何理解成果周期；并不据此推出应排除私营研究。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Artificial Intelligence｜公共部门实施条件

            appropriate data infrastructure

            合适的数据基础设施

            适合具体说明公共科研投入的基础条件；搭配provide或develop时仍需交代研究用途。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Government funding can provide appropriate data infrastructure for long-term environmental research whose commercial returns are uncertain.

            自编例句，贴合政府资助具有公共价值、商业回报不确定的科研，具体化资金可以支持什么；不是说科研只能由政府执行。

            reap the benefits of

            实际获得……的益处

            后接能够说明来源的资源、经验或合作成果，避免只写空泛的benefits。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Public laboratories may reap the benefits of specialist knowledge held by private companies if they are allowed to collaborate.

            自编例句，直接回应政府与私企研究是否应排他：用有条件的合作说明可以利用不同主体的专业知识。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Artificial Intelligence｜部署边界、医疗与司法案例

            minimise the potential harms

            尽量减少潜在伤害

            适合与审查、监管和试验条件相连；不能声称审查可以保证消除全部风险。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Independent review can help both public and private laboratories minimise the potential harms of experimental treatments.

            自编例句，直接回应科研应如何受到控制：提出可适用于公共和私营实验室的审查安排，不把监管等同于政府独占所有研究。

            be aware of the limitations of

            认识到……的局限

            后接具体技术或方法；认识边界服务于判断用途，避免演变成空泛反科技态度。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Research regulators need to be aware of the limitations of a new technology before approving its wider use.

            自编例句，贴合政府科研监督职责，把能力边界与是否批准扩大应用联系起来。

            回到这份材料的精读

            回到原题入口

Alternative forms of transport should be encouraged and international laws introduced to control car ownership and use. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

            写作前置 · 文中表达

            下面的表达来自阅读材料，例句按本题语境编写。选择确实需要的表达即可。

            Why we need silence｜噪声风险与城市降噪

            reducing noise from roads

            减少道路噪声

            适合说明鼓励公共交通、步行或骑行可能带来的生活环境收益。需要具体写出减少何种车流或噪声源，不把交通方式改变等同于必然消除所有噪声。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Replacing some private car journeys with walking or cycling can make residential areas more pleasant by reducing noise from roads.

            题目讨论鼓励替代交通与限制车辆使用；道路噪声是与车辆使用直接相关的生活环境理由。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Dar es Salaam · 城市扩张与交通方案

            a future controlled by the private car

            由私家车主导的未来

            适合描述城市发展的整体方向，随后应解释公共交通如何提供现实替代。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Investment in reliable public transport can help cities avoid a future controlled by the private car.

            直接回应交通题鼓励替代交通方式的主张；不自动推出必须统一限制所有地区的汽车拥有量。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Dar es Salaam · 公交设计与实际故障

            accessible to people using wheelchairs

            便于轮椅使用者使用

            用于说明公共交通替代方案应照顾不同乘客；需配合无台阶入口、站台等具体设计。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Buses should be accessible to people using wheelchairs so that alternatives to cars serve passengers with different mobility needs.

            交通题中的替代方式不只是增加车辆，还包括让不同人群能实际使用。

            within a short walk of

            距……很近，步行即可到达

            说明住房与公交网络的空间联系；是否足够近应由实际布局支持。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            More residents may choose buses if their homes are within a short walk of a reliable route.

            说明公交替代汽车所需的接近性与可靠性，连接设施安排和出行选择。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Task 2 · 原因与措施

            过度捕捞：从激励与监管写到对策

            从自己的首稿开始，按需要检查与修订。

            回到原题入口
            查看题面 · 来源
            Overfishing of the world’s oceans threatens many species with extinction and is putting the livelihood of millions of people around the world at risk. What are the causes of this problem and what can be done to prevent it from happening?

            Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

            官方教辅 · British Council — Writing Task 2: Problems and solutions · PDF 第 7 页

            参考置信度：高（题面与来源已核对；练习讲解为编写内容）

            回到原题入口
            阅读后写作 · 本题可用表达

            写作前置 · 文中表达

            下面的表达来自阅读材料，例句按本题语境编写。选择确实需要的表达即可。

            The World of Sugar｜全球贸易与误解纠正

            threatening the livelihood of

            威胁……的生计

            适合用于描述资源衰退或不公平竞争怎样影响依赖某产业谋生的人。可以作为结果分词短语，但要让前面的原因具体可理解。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Overfishing can deplete local fish stocks, threatening the livelihood of small-scale fishing communities.

            现有题目明确谈过度捕捞对数百万人生计的风险；表达可直接连接鱼类资源减少与沿海家庭收入受损。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Saving the saiga · 生存适应与早期数量变化

            on an industrial scale

            以极大的、工业化的规模

            适合描述技术与设备使资源开采规模扩大；不能把所有小型经营都称为 industrial scale。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Large vessels can remove fish on an industrial scale, making effective limits on catches essential.

            过度捕捞题讨论捕捞能力与生态压力，大型船舶造成的规模效应与原文大规模猎杀直接相关。

            relieve the pressure on

            减轻……所承受的压力

            说明措施帮助哪个对象；on 后接鱼群、生态系统等，随后解释压力怎样减少。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Temporary closures can relieve the pressure on vulnerable fish stocks by allowing them time to reproduce.

            直接用于过度捕捞的措施段，把休渔与鱼群恢复相连；不套用赛加保护倡议的历史结果。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Saving the saiga · 栖息地、疾病、气候与恢复

            working in partnership with

            与……共同合作

            适合说明跨地区生态治理的合作关系，应明确谁和谁合作以及共同处理什么问题。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Coastal authorities, working in partnership with neighbouring countries, can coordinate limits on catches from shared fish stocks.

            过度捕捞涉及跨界鱼群，原文跨境物种保护中的机构协作与共享海域监管高度吻合。

            protect and restore

            保护并修复

            protect 强调避免进一步破坏，restore 强调恢复已经受损的状态；并列时应同时存在预防与修复需要。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Fishing restrictions should protect and restore marine ecosystems while allowing communities time to adapt.

            可用于说明限制捕捞的生态目标，并与题目中的渔业生计相衔接。

            回到这份材料的精读

            Task 2 · 原因与措施

            儿童肥胖：原因—措施对应而非空泛建议

            从自己的首稿开始，按需要检查与修订。

            回到原题入口
            查看题面 · 来源
            A rise in childhood obesity is a real threat to health with an increasing number of children now classified as overweight. What are the causes of the problem and what measures can be taken to solve them?

            Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

            官方教辅 · British Council — Writing Task 2: Problems and solutions · PDF 第 12 页

            参考置信度：高（题面与来源已核对；练习讲解为编写内容）

            回到原题入口
            阅读后写作 · 本题可用表达

            写作前置 · 文中表达

            下面的表达来自阅读材料，例句按本题语境编写。选择确实需要的表达即可。

            The World of Sugar｜工业化、消费与作者立场

            attempts to reduce consumption

            降低消费量的努力

            在健康话题里要补清consumption指什么，例如含糖饮料，而不是笼统主张减少所有食品消费。适合描述措施与商业激励之间的关系。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Attempts to reduce consumption of sugary drinks among children are more likely to succeed when healthier alternatives are affordable and easy to obtain.

            儿童肥胖题要求提出措施；这句话把减少含糖饮料摄入与可负担替代品联系起来，强调环境支持而非只责怪个人自控。

            a large number of processed foods

            大量加工食品

            可讨论配方、标签或食品环境，但加工食品并非全部有相同营养特征，例句应限定要比较的成分。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            When added sugar is present in a large number of processed foods, clear labels can help parents compare products more easily.

            适合儿童肥胖措施段中的食品信息环境；条件句聚焦添加糖与标签，避免把所有加工食品概括为有害。

            回到这份材料的精读

            健康观念变化：年份、十年与三大领域

            the social and environmental conditions

            社会与环境条件

            适合说明健康行为受到可获得资源与生活环境的影响；必须接具体机制，不把抽象词组当成完整原因。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Measures to reduce childhood obesity should address the social and environmental conditions that make nutritious food and safe places to play difficult to access.

            自编例句，直接对应儿童肥胖的原因与措施：把食物和活动空间的可达性作为可以改善的具体条件，不把所有责任归于儿童个人。

            maintain healthy behaviours and lifestyles

            维持有益健康的行为与生活方式

            与提供条件和持续支持搭配；不承诺一项措施可以单独消除儿童肥胖。

            本题例句 · 编写示范

            Schools can help children maintain healthy behaviours and lifestyles by providing regular opportunities for physical activity and nutritious meals.

            自编例句，用学校可采取的具体支持回应儿童肥胖题的措施部分；can表示可能贡献，不宣称所有儿童会因此获得相同结果。

            回到这份材料的精读

            01take … into account｜把条件纳入判断讨论费用、个人差异或政策效果时，说明结论考虑了哪些条件。约 8 分钟
            可选：记录或再练一次

            意义与结构

            用于表示作判断或决定时考虑某个因素。结构是 take + 名词／名词短语 + into account；也可以 take into account + 较长的名词短语或 the fact that 从句。过去式 took，过去分词 taken。

            例句

            The timetable should take students' travel time into account. 课程表应该考虑学生的通勤时间。

            We need to take into account the fact that some learners work full time. 我们需要考虑到有些学习者有全职工作。

            易混点

            account for 常用于“解释／占某比例”，不是这里的“考虑”。consider 是自然、简洁的替换，不需要为了显得高级每次都用长表达。taken into account 表示被考虑，不等于最终一定按这一因素作决定。

            留下本单元首稿

            本单元先学再用；不记为未见初测。口语可使用原章节录音器，或自行录音并记文件名。

            先读短课，再独立应用；保存后看反馈。

            先写下自己的答案。

            核对依据，再修订

            ① into。② 参考：When evaluating online courses, we need to take students' internet access into account. 也可用 the quality of students' internet connections，取决于你想表达能否联网还是连接质量。③ The plan takes students' travel time into account. account for 在不同语境可能有不同意义，这里换成明确结构能避免被读成“解释”。自己的句子应保留评估对象与需考虑的因素；不要求与参考逐字相同。

            自查只记三项：意义是否符合本意；结构是否完整；是否保留必要的范围或条件。参考答案不是唯一合法表达，不根据是否使用这个搭配给雅思分数。

            READING PASSAGE 3

            You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27-40, which are based on Passage 3 below.

            Artificial Intelligence

            In many countries in the West, hysteria about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) is everywhere. There seems to be no shortage of sensationalist news about how AI could cure diseases, accelerate human innovation and improve human creativity. Just looking at the media headlines, you might think that we are already living in a future where AI has infiltrated every aspect of society.

            While it is undeniable that AI has opened up a wealth of promising opportunities, it has also led to the emergence of a mindset that can be best described as 'AI solutionism'. This is the philosophy that, given enough data, machine learning algorithms can solve all of humanity's problems. But, in fact, instead of supporting AI progress, this mindset actually jeopardises the value of machine intelligence by disregarding important AI safety principles and setting unrealistic expectations about what AI can really do for humanity.

            In only a few years, AI solutionism has made its way from the technology evangelists' mouths in Silicon Valley in California to the minds of government officials and policymakers around the world. The pendulum has swung from the dystopian notion that AI will destroy humanity to the utopian belief that our algorithmic saviour is here.

            We are now seeing governments pledge support to national AI initiatives and compete in a technological race to dominate the burgeoning machine-learning sector. While many politicians proclaim the transformative effects of the coming 'AI revolution', they fail to realise the complexity around deploying advanced machine learning systems in the real world.

            One of the most promising varieties of AI technologies are neural networks. This form of machine learning is loosely modelled on the neuronal structure of the human brain, but on a much smaller scale. But what many politicians do not understand is that simply adding a neural network to a problem will not automatically mean that you'll find a solution. Similarly, adding a neural network to a system of government does not mean it will be instantaneously more inclusive or fair.

            AI systems need a lot of data to function, but the public sector typically does not have the appropriate data infrastructure to support advanced machine learning. Most of the data remains stored in offline archives. The few digitised sources of data that exist tend to be buried in bureaucracy. More often than not, data is spread across different government departments that each require special permissions to be accessed. Above all, the public sector typically lacks the human talent with the right technological capabilities to fully reap the benefits of machine intelligence.

            For these reasons, the sensationalism over AI has attracted many critics. Stuart Russell, a professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley, has long advocated a more sensible and realistic approach that focuses on simple everyday applications of AI instead of the

            原文 · 印刷页47

            hypothetical takeover by super-intelligent robots. Similarly, Rodney Brooks, professor of robotics at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, writes that 'almost all innovations in robotics and AI take far, far, longer to be really widely deployed than people in the field and outside the field imagine'.

            One of the many difficulties in deploying machine learning systems is that AI is extremely susceptible to adversarial attacks. This means that a malicious AI can target another AI to make it behave in a certain way, such as forcing it to make wrong predictions. Many researchers have warned against the rolling out of AI without appropriate security standards and defence mechanisms. Still, AI security remains an often overlooked topic when machine learning systems are installed.

            If we are to reap the benefits and minimise the potential harms of AI, we must start thinking about how machine learning can be meaningfully applied to specific areas of government, business and society. This means we need to have a discussion about AI ethics and the distrust that many people have towards machine learning.

            Most importantly, we need to be aware of the limitations of AI and where people still need to take the lead. Instead of painting an unrealistic picture of the power of AI, it is important to take a step back and separate the actual technological capabilities of AI from fantasy.

            The medical profession has also recognised the drawbacks to AI. The IBM Watson for Oncology programme was a piece of AI that was meant to help doctors treat cancer. Even though it was developed to deliver the best recommendations, human experts found it hard to trust the machine. As a result, the AI programme was abandoned in most hospitals where it was trialled.

            Similar difficulties arose in the legal domain when algorithms were used in courts in the US to sentence criminals. An algorithm calculated risk assessment scores and advised judges on the sentencing. The system was found to amplify structural racial discrimination and was later abandoned.

            There are some crucial lessons here for everyone aiming to boost investments in national AI programmes. These examples demonstrate that there is no AI solution for everything. Using AI simply for the sake of AI may not always be productive or useful, and not every issue is best addressed by applying machine intelligence to it. All solutions come with a cost and not everything that can be automated should be.

            02meet someone's needs｜满足具体需要评价教育、交通或公共服务时，把笼统的“好”改为满足谁的什么需要。约 8 分钟
            可选：记录或再练一次

            意义与结构

            meet someone's needs 或 meet the needs of + 人／群体，表示提供的东西符合对方需要。这里 meet 不是“见面”；过去式和过去分词都是 met。needs 通常用复数，若已明确一个具体需要也可说 meet a need。

            例句

            Evening classes can meet the needs of adults who work during the day. 晚课能满足白天工作的成年人的需要。

            A single bus route may not meet everyone's travel needs. 一条公交线路可能无法满足所有人的出行需要。

            易混点

            满足需要不等于满足每个人的所有愿望。尽量写明群体与具体需要，而不是空泛地写 meet people's needs。address a need 可表示着手回应需要，语义不必达到“已经满足”的程度。

            自查只记三项：意义是否符合本意；结构是否完整；是否保留必要的范围或条件。参考答案不是唯一合法表达，不根据是否使用这个搭配给雅思分数。

            READING PASSAGE 2

            You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14-26, which are based on Passage 2 below.

            The problems of getting around the city of

            Dar es Salaam

            Dar es Salaam in Tanzania is one of the fastest growing cities in Africa. Its population has increased eightfold since 1980 and swells by half a million people every year. United Nations projections anticipate it will become a megacity within seven years as its population passes 10 million, reaching 13.4 million by 2035. Daniel Hoornweg for the Global Cities Institute forecasts the city could be home to an incredible 73.7 million people by 2100.

            Today, four out of five of its people live in single-storey informal settlements on the spreading edges of the city, where the journey to and from the centre regularly takes over two hours. It can be longer if rain turns the dirt roads to mud.

            Even in the middle of the day, traffic frequently slows to a stop without warning. It is not unusual for cars and minibuses to queue for 20 minutes at a key intersection. A single suburban rail line serves residents in a few areas to the south but is tiny in the context of the wider city. Outside the centre many rely on boda boda (motorbike taxis) to navigate the narrow side streets and potholed mud roads that make up much of the metropolis. Their safety record is scandalous.

            Dar es Salaam's reliance on four arterial roads into the city is a legacy of the colonial government that planned the city at the start of the 20th century to cater for a population of 35,000. Most of the current growth is made up of young people arriving from the countryside to find work, and as the population has exploded, Dar es Salaam has grown around those four highways. Nearly all the expansion is happening on the periphery, and nearly all takes place informally without any agreed strategy.

            But Dar es Salaam is pinning its hopes on a solution that could offer a different model for Africa's megacities, giving them an alternative to a future controlled by the private car. Unlike many cities on the continent, Dar es Salaam isn't trying to build a metro. It has chosen a less exciting but cheaper and more achievable method: the bus.

            The DART bus rapid transit (BRT) system runs on bus lanes separated from other traffic, mostly in the middle of the road to reduce stoppages. Ticket purchase and control takes place at stations prior to boarding and the buses are step-free, which means the entire route is accessible to people using wheelchairs or who are travelling with baby buggies.

            原文 · 印刷页65

            'The new buses are much, much better,' says Paulas George, a young IT worker. He takes the bus every day and it has cut his journey time by two-thirds. He says it is not perfect, though, complaining that drivers often refuse to turn on the air conditioning to save fuel.

            That is not the only problem. A shortage of buses after a serious flood at the main depot during the rainy season means the system is carrying 200,000 people a day - half the expected capacity. Smartcards can't be used as the mechanical readers aren't working either, forcing passengers to buy individual paper tickets for every journey. Each is printed with a scannable QR code, but there are no scanners. Staff stand by the gates and tear tickets as people enter. As a result, queues are considerable at peak times.

            Morogoro Road to the north-west of the city was phase I of the BRT project. Phases II and III will install bus lanes along Nyerere Road to the south-west and Kilwa Road to the south. Construction on both routes is due to start imminently. Phase IV, towards Bagamoyo in the north, is in the preliminary design stage. 'Much of the city will have access to a world-class transport system within the space of a few years,' says Chris Kost, the Africa director of ITDP (the Institute for Transportation and Development Policy). All phases are being planned to high standards and, once complete, a third of city residents will be within a short walk of the BRT network.

            The ITDP regrets Africa's obsession with metros. 'With a metro, an international firm will often just parachute in its own system,' says Kost. 'Bus rapid transit allows existing stakeholders to get involved. That's what we did in Dar es Salaam and what we're planning in Nairobi, where the bus bodies will be built in the city and local operators will look after tickets, fare collection and IT ... Bus rapid transit has been transformational for Dar es Salaam. For millions of people in African cities, this is their best hope of ever being connected.'

            03raise awareness of …｜提高对某事的认识描述宣传或教育的作用，同时避免把“知道了”直接当成“行为已改变”。约 8 分钟
            可选：记录或再练一次

            意义与结构

            raise awareness of + 问题／风险／现象，表示帮助人们更清楚地知道、理解某事。about 也可使用；这里先熟悉 of 这一结构。awareness 通常是不可数名词，可说 public awareness。an awareness campaign 也正确，此处可数的是 campaign（一次宣传活动），不是 awareness。

            例句

            School workshops can raise awareness of online scams. 学校的专题活动可以提高大家对网络诈骗的认识。

            The campaign raised public awareness of food waste, but its effect on purchasing habits was unclear. 宣传提高了公众对食物浪费的认识，但其对购买习惯的影响还不明确。

            易混点

            raise 是及物动词，需要宾语；awareness rose 则用不及物的 rise。认知提高不自动证明行为改变，论证中应另给行为证据。

            留下本单元首稿

            READING PASSAGE 1

            You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1-13, which are based on Passage 1 below.

            Saving the saiga

            The saiga, a species of antelope native to Central Asia, once roamed the vast grasslands of this region in enormous herds, many millions strong. Regrettably, such spectacular sights are a thing of the past. Today, the saiga is largely confined to a single country: Kazakhstan. This country is estimated to be home to well over 90% of the global saiga population, with Russia, Mongolia and Uzbekistan accounting for the rest.

            The saiga is perfectly adapted to the tough conditions of the remote wilderness of the steppes of Central Asia. One such adaptation is its bizarre bulbous nose, which enables the animal to survive the extreme seasonal temperature swings of the region. The swollen nostrils of the nose serve several purposes: they filter out dust and cool the blood during hot, dry summers, and they warm the cold air before it enters the saiga's lungs in winter. Other seasonal adaptations include a heavy winter coat that the saiga sheds when the weather warms up.

            Despite these superb adaptations to harsh conditions, the saiga has no defence against the threats posed by humans. It was almost driven to extinction by hunters in the 19th century. Legal protection ensured its survival for a while, and numbers steadily recovered throughout most of the 20th century. But the respite was only temporary. In the ten years following the break-up of the former Soviet Union in 1991, over 95% of the global population was lost - one of the fastest examples of species loss ever recorded for a mammal.

            The dramatic decline during this decade was due to illegal poaching on an industrial scale. Male saiga are a particular target, because their horns are highly prized by traditional medicine practitioners. Poaching reached epidemic levels after misguided conservationists tried to relieve the pressure on threatened African rhinos by actively encouraging the use of saiga horns in traditional medicine as an alternative to those of rhinos. Male saiga were almost wiped out, leading to a population crash from which the species has been struggling to recover ever since.

            Another threat to the survival of the saiga is loss of habitat, as a result of agricultural expansion and human settlement. Physical barriers such as railways, pipelines and fences can block the seasonal migration routes of this transboundary species. In the worst cases, herds may starve to death after being trapped.

            原文 · 印刷页61

            Then there is the risk of disease. In 2015, an outbreak of haemorrhagic septicaemia, caused by the normally harmless bacterium Pasteurella multocida, killed over 75% of the global adult saiga population in just three weeks. In 2017, 60% of the Mongolian saiga population - a subspecies found nowhere else in the world - was killed by a virus that spilled over from livestock. These so-called mass mortality events represent an unpredictable and serious threat to the species.

            Climate change poses a further threat. Although well adapted to cold winters and hot summers, saiga struggle to cope with temperature extremes and unpredictable fluctuations in climate. Experts believe that unusually warm weather may have triggered the 2015 mass mortality event. The steppe region has also become increasingly arid in recent years, and many of the smaller streams that the species normally depended on have dried up and vanished.

            Recent efforts to save the saiga have been spearheaded by the Altyn Dala Conservation Initiative, a project led by the Association for the Conservation of Biodiversity of Kazakhstan, working in partnership with the Kazakh government's Committee for Forestry and Wildlife, Frankfurt Zoological Society and Fauna and Flora, an international conservation charity. Its purpose is to protect and restore Kazakhstan's steppe, semi-desert and desert ecosystems and the many species they support, including the critically endangered saiga. In 2022 the United Nations recognised the initiative as a World Restoration Flagship project, an accolade reserved for the ten best examples of large-scale ecosystem restoration around the globe.

            So, how many saiga are there now? By 2000, the global saiga population had hit an all­ time low of just 21,000 individuals. There was some recovery in the first decade of the new millennium but this was then crushed by devastating mass mortality events that saw the loss of hundreds of thousands of the species. But thanks to the intervention of the Altyn Dala Conservation Initiative, the most recent episodes in the ongoing story of the saiga have been relatively uplifting. Three years ago, the Ustyurt Plateau population in Kazakhstan experienced its largest mass birth of saiga calves in many years. An aerial census two years ago recorded an estimated 842,000 saiga across Kazakhstan as a whole, and according to an aerial survey earlier this year, the saiga population in Kazakhstan now exceeds 1.9 million. The world's strangest-looking antelope remains critically endangered, but the direction of travel is positive.

            04pose a threat to …｜对……构成威胁描述风险的来源、受影响对象及可能后果，不把风险写成已发生的损害。约 8 分钟
            可选：记录或再练一次

            意义与结构

            主语是威胁来源：X poses a threat to Y。pose 后面接 a threat，to 后面连接受威胁的人、环境或系统。也可说 pose a risk／pose a problem，但这些名词的后续结构要按具体句子处理。

            例句

            Rapid habitat loss poses a threat to local wildlife. 栖息地迅速减少对当地野生动物构成威胁。

            False health advice may pose a threat to public safety. 错误的健康建议可能威胁公共安全。

            易混点

            threat 表示危险或可能的损害，不等于某次损害已被证实。证据有限时可用 may／could，但不要堆成 may possibly perhaps。pose 还有摆姿势、提出问题等义项，不能把所有 pose 都理解成威胁。

            留下本单元首稿

            05strike a balance between … and …｜兼顾两种需求讨论工作学习、发展保护等取舍时，明确需要同时照顾的两方面。约 8 分钟

            意义与结构

            strike a balance between A and B，指在相互牵制的需求之间找到可接受的安排。A 和 B 最好在语法上平行：两个名词短语，或两个动名词短语。过去式 struck，过去分词 struck。

            例句

            Students need to strike a balance between study and rest. 学生需要兼顾学习和休息。

            The city is trying to strike a balance between attracting visitors and protecting historic buildings. 这座城市正试着兼顾吸引游客与保护历史建筑。

            易混点

            balance 不必表示各占一半，而是适合情境的比例。只写“需要平衡”还不是充分论证：继续说具体怎样安排，以及为什么。

            以下为正式样题原始材料。先按原题要求作答，再看原答案与对应解释；材料描述的是原文中的语境，不把历史数据当作当前事实。

            原材料 · 第1页

            [Note: This is an extract from a General Training Reading text on the subject of coal. The text preceding this extract catalogued the general belief that extracting and using coal is bad for the environment.]

            Greenhouse gases arise from a wide range of sources and their increasing concentration is largely related to the compound effects of increased population, improved living standards and changes in lifestyle. From a current base of 5 billion, the United Nations predicts that the global population may stabilise in the twenty-first century between 8 and 14 billion, with more than 90 per cent of the projected increase taking place in the world’s developing nations. The associated activities to support that growth, particularly to produce the required energy and food, will cause further increases in greenhouse gas emissions. The challenge, therefore, is to attain a sustainable balance between population, economic growth and the environment.

            The major greenhouse gas emissions from human activities are carbon dioxide (CO2), methane and nitrous oxide. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are the only major contributor to the greenhouse effect that does not occur naturally, coming from such sources as refrigeration, plastics and manufacture. Coal’s total contribution to greenhouse gas emissions is thought to be about 18 per cent, with about half of this coming from electricity generation.

            The worldwide coal industry allocates extensive resources to researching and developing new technologies and ways of capturing greenhouse gases. Efficiencies are likely to be improved dramatically, and hence CO2 emissions reduced, through combustion and gasification techniques which are now at pilot and demonstration stages.

            Clean coal is another avenue for improving fuel conversion efficiency. Investigations are under way into super-clean coal (35 per cent ash) and ultraclean coal (less than 1 per cent ash). Super-clean coal has the potential to enhance the combustion efficiency of conventional pulverised fuel power plants. Ultraclean coal will enable coal to be used in advanced power systems such as coal-fired gas turbines which, when operated in combined cycle, have the potential to achieve much greater efficiencies.

            Defendants of mining point out that, environmentally, coal mining has two important factors in its favour. It makes only temporary use of the land and produces no toxic chemical wastes. By carefully preplanning projects, implementing pollution control measures, monitoring the effects of mining and rehabilitating mined areas, the coal industry minimises the impact on the neighbouring community, the immediate environment and long-term land capability.

            原页文字提示：原题引文保留原页拼写：Defendants of mining。这里语义上指采矿的支持者；自己的表达请用 defenders of mining，不把原题拼写当作推荐搭配。

            原材料 · 第2页

            Dust levels are controlled by spraying roads and stockpiles, and water pollution is controlled by carefully separating clean water runoff from runoff which contains sediments or salt from mine workings. The latter is treated and reused for dust suppression. Noise is controlled by modifying equipment and by using insulation and sound enclosures around machinery.

            Since mining activities represent only a temporary use of the land, extensive rehabilitation measures are adopted to ensure that land capability after mining meets agreed and appropriate standards which, in some cases, are superior to the land’s pre-mining condition. Where the mining is underground, the surface area can be simultaneously used for forests, cattle grazing and crop raising, or even reservoirs and urban development, with little or no disruption to the existing land use. In all cases, mining is subject to stringent controls and approvals processes.

            2 The proportion of all greenhouse gases created by coal is approximately

            A 14 per cent. B 18 per cent. C 27 per cent. D 90 per cent.

            3 Current research aims to increase the energy-producing efficiency of coal by

            A burning it at a lower temperature. B developing new gasification techniques. C extracting CO2 from it. D recycling greenhouse gases.

            4 Compared with ordinary coal, new, ‘clean’ coals may generate power

            A more cleanly and more efficiently. B more cleanly but less efficiently. C more cleanly but at higher cost. D more cleanly but much more slowly.

            5 To control dust at mine sites, mining companies often use

            A chemicals which may be toxic. B topsoil taken from the site before mining. C fresh water from nearby dams. D runoff water containing sediments.
