Over the next 12 years, the sisters amassed the bulk of their Impressionist collection, including six further works by Monet, two more by Manet, and three by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne.

            原文第6段The First World War (1914-1918) played a part in the development of the sisters' collection. Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area. Later in the conflict, both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes, in northern France; Gwendoline in 1916, followed by Margaret in 1917.

            原文第7段It was tedious and distressing work, which would have a permanent effect on Gwendoline's health. Yet on one of numerous trips to nearby Paris, she visited the Bernheim-Jeune Gallery. Here she acquired two works by Cézanne - Provençal Landscape and The François Zola Dam. The paintings were shipped directly to Bath, England, where they became the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain.

            *** Impressionist: an artist with a style of painting that developed in France in the late 1800s by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne

            原页文字提示：脚注引文保留原页；其后半句涉及 Renoir 作品，属于来源编辑瑕疵，不要把整条脚注当作英语完整定义范例。这里的 Impressionist 指印象派画家。

            5. the first Impressionist paintings they bought showed places in 5 __________

            6. they worked in a 6 __________ for soldiers in France

            10. Hugh Blaker opposed the Davies sisters' decision to buy art by French Impressionists.

            11. The exhibition of Cézanne paintings at the Bath gallery was very popular with the public.

            对照答案，回到证据

            第 5 题 · Venice

            题干问画中的地点，不是买画地点；Paris是干扰信息。

            their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice

            第 6 题 · canteen

            soldiers对应troops；a后填地点canteen，不能答城市Troyes。

            both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes

            第 10 题 · FALSE

            champion与had a hand in说明支持并参与，和opposed相反，属于明确反证。

            Hugh Blaker, as a champion of contemporary French art had a hand in the decision

            第 11 题 · NOT GIVEN

            原文只确认首次公开展出，没有观众反响或人数。全文也未提供其受欢迎程度；first与popular不可互换。

            the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain

            核对原答案页

            材料精读 · 内容与词句

            姐妹的收藏逐渐转向法国印象派。文章承认影响因素存在，却没有把转向归结为一个已确定的原因；随后把战争中的救助、志愿服务和购画经历交织起来，展示私人行动如何最终进入公共文化生活。

            原文第5段

            However, it was only a few years before their collecting took a new direction and they turned to the work of the French Impressionists***. We know that Hugh Blaker, as a champion of contemporary French art had a hand in the decision, and we know also that they would have seen examples on their various trips to Paris. Whatever the precise reason for this change, their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice by the French artist Claude Monet. Over the next 12 years, the sisters amassed the bulk of their Impressionist collection, including six further works by Monet, two more by Manet, and three by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne.

            收藏方向改变后，姐妹开始购入法国印象派作品。支持当代法国艺术的Hugh Blaker参与了这个决定，她们在巴黎旅行时也应当接触过相关作品，但作者没有断言某一个因素就是决定性原因。1912年她们购入莫奈的威尼斯风景，之后12年形成了印象派收藏的主体。the bulk强调大部分藏品在这一时期积累。

            原文第6段

            The First World War (1914-1918) played a part in the development of the sisters' collection. Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area. Later in the conflict, both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes, in northern France; Gwendoline in 1916, followed by Margaret in 1917.

            第一次世界大战也影响了她们的收藏经历。她们起初出钱帮助被占领比利时的艺术家安全来到威尔士，这既出于人道关怀，也带有发展当地艺术家社群的愿望。后来两人先后到法国为部队食堂做志愿服务。本段把文化理想放在战争救助的现实行动中，而不是只讲艺术市场。

            原文第7段

            It was tedious and distressing work, which would have a permanent effect on Gwendoline's health. Yet on one of numerous trips to nearby Paris, she visited the Bernheim-Jeune Gallery. Here she acquired two works by Cézanne - Provençal Landscape and The François Zola Dam. The paintings were shipped directly to Bath, England, where they became the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain.

            食堂工作单调又令人痛苦，并对格温多琳的健康产生了持久影响。即使如此，她仍在赴巴黎期间参观画廊并购买塞尚的两幅画。这些作品被直接运往英国巴斯，成为英国公共画廊首次展出的塞尚作品。最后一句将个人购藏的故事转向公众能够接触艺术的变化。

            词语与搭配

            took a new direction

            转向新的方向

            主语可以是事业、研究或活动的发展；这里的collecting指持续的收藏实践发生变化。

            had a hand in the decision

            参与或影响了这个决定

            have a hand in不表示独自决定；文中同时承认旅行见闻等可能影响。

            a vibrant artists' community

            一个充满活力的艺术家社群

            vibrant强调活跃、有创造力；artists'是复数所有格，community指艺术家相互联系形成的群体，不只是建筑或展馆。

            go on display in a public gallery

            开始在公共画廊展出

            go on display强调从未展出到展出的状态变化，public gallery使私人收藏与公共接触联系起来。

            句子精读

            Whatever the precise reason for this change, their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice by the French artist Claude Monet.

            无论这一变化的确切原因是什么，她们于1912年10月首次购入的印象派作品，都是法国画家克洛德·莫奈描绘威尼斯的风景画。

            Whatever the precise reason是省略了may have been一类成分的让步结构，表示不论原因如何。主干是their first purchases were scenes of Venice；made in October 1912是过去分词短语，补充购入时间；by...说明作者。this change指收藏转向印象派，日期、描绘对象与作者属于不同层面的信息。

            Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area.

            她们最初对战时行动的回应，是资助艺术家从被占领的比利时安全前往威尔士；这是一项人道行动，同时也寄托着在当地建立活跃艺术家社群的希望。

            主干是Their initial response was to finance...，不定式说明具体行动。from...to...标明迁移起止地。as a humanitarian act与with the hope of...并列说明两层动机，but also在这里补充文化愿景而非否定人道目的。the area指威尔士当地；hope表明愿望，不能直接当成已经实现的结果。

            这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

            a vibrant artists' community

            一个充满活力的艺术家社群

            适合与support、sustain、help build搭配，讨论实体文化空间如何为创作者提供交流和演出机会。这里借用表达描述一种可能作用，不把文中救助艺术家的历史直接当成剧院效果的证据。

            用于写作：题目要求讨论剧院和影院的经济、文化价值；此表达适合展开剧院支持当地艺术生产和创作者交流的文化作用。

            读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

            The Davies Sisters｜收藏停止与文化遗产未作答笔记填空 / 事实判断 TFNG · 3 段 · 238 词 · 3 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 18 页

            Q7：Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage. Q12–13：TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN。

            原文第8段Commentators have often described the sisters as unlikely pioneer collectors. Much is made of their isolation in rural Wales and the fact that they didn't make friends with artists or gallery owners. Yet they didn't feel obliged to follow fashionable tastes and were free to pursue their own preferences. Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.

            原文第9段By the early 1920s, Gwendoline felt increasingly uncomfortable buying art works when faced with the poverty and social upheaval created by the First World War. Her philanthropic pursuits then became focused almost exclusively on social causes and the development of the sisters' home at Gregynog Hall into a conference center and venue for the Gregynog Festival of Music and Poetry. Gwendoline made her final art purchase in March 1926. Margaret also stopped collecting around this time, but started again in the 1930s acquiring, on a relatively small scale, work by contemporary British artists.

            原文第10段The sisters collected French Impressionist paintings at a time when such art was routinely ignored by individuals and institutions alike. The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists. In collecting paintings that they loved, the sisters created a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy for the people of Wales and beyond.

            7. were not considered typical collectors – they lived in isolation in the countryside and did not have any 7 __________ who were artists

            12. The impact of the First World War encouraged Gwendoline to reconsider her interest in collecting art.

            13. The Davies sisters bought French Impressionist art during a period when very few people were doing so.

            对照答案，回到证据

            第 7 题 · friends

            题干把make friends改为have friends；any后用复数friends，不是advisers。

            they didn't make friends with artists or gallery owners

            第 12 题 · TRUE

            战后贫困与动荡使她不安，随后慈善转向社会事业并停止购买，是reconsider的具体证据链。

            Gwendoline felt increasingly uncomfortable buying art works when faced with the poverty and social upheaval created by the First World War

            第 13 题 · TRUE

            ignored by individuals and institutions同时覆盖个人与机构，与very few people were doing so同义。

            at a time when such art was routinely ignored by individuals and institutions alike

            核对原答案页

            材料精读 · 内容与词句

            这部分先重新解释姐妹看似偏离艺术圈的生活方式，再说明战争造成的社会问题如何改变她们的支出重点，最后评价收藏留下的公共文化遗产。独立品味、社会责任与文化贡献在结尾汇合。

            原文第8段

            Commentators have often described the sisters as unlikely pioneer collectors. Much is made of their isolation in rural Wales and the fact that they didn't make friends with artists or gallery owners. Yet they didn't feel obliged to follow fashionable tastes and were free to pursue their own preferences. Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.

            评论者常把姐妹描述为出人意料的收藏先驱，因为她们住在威尔士乡间，也不与艺术家或画廊主人交朋友。作者随后补充另一面：远离潮流压力使她们能够追随自己的品味。她们仍依赖可信顾问，经常到伦敦和巴黎，也让人把画送到家里考虑，因此地理上的偏远不等于缺少接触作品的机会。

            原文第9段

            By the early 1920s, Gwendoline felt increasingly uncomfortable buying art works when faced with the poverty and social upheaval created by the First World War. Her philanthropic pursuits then became focused almost exclusively on social causes and the development of the sisters' home at Gregynog Hall into a conference center and venue for the Gregynog Festival of Music and Poetry. Gwendoline made her final art purchase in March 1926. Margaret also stopped collecting around this time, but started again in the 1930s acquiring, on a relatively small scale, work by contemporary British artists.

            到1920年代初，战争遗留的贫困和社会动荡使格温多琳对继续购画越来越不安。她把精力几乎完全转向社会事业，并将家宅发展为会议及音乐诗歌节场所，1926年作了最后一次购画。玛格丽特也在大致同期停止收藏，却在1930年代恢复小规模购买当代英国作品。两人的后续选择有关联，但不能合并为完全相同的人生轨迹。

            原文第10段

            The sisters collected French Impressionist paintings at a time when such art was routinely ignored by individuals and institutions alike. The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists. In collecting paintings that they loved, the sisters created a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy for the people of Wales and beyond.

            文章把个人经历放回当时的艺术接受环境：姐妹收藏印象派时，个人和机构普遍忽视这类作品。她们的藏品后来分别于1951年和1963年捐给威尔士国家博物馆，包含重要画家的代表作。最后一句评价她们追随个人喜爱的行为产生了超出私人范围的长期文化价值。

            词语与搭配

            free to pursue their own preferences

            能够自由追随自己的喜好

            be free to强调不受外部义务或压力束缚；这里与不必追随流行趣味相连，不表示完全不接受建议。

            when faced with the poverty and social upheaval

            面对贫困和社会动荡时

            when faced with是省略主语和be动词的结构，后接所面对的局面；说明价值判断发生变化的社会背景。

            on a relatively small scale

            以相对较小的规模

            scale描述活动的规模，relatively保留比较意味；这里限定玛格丽特后来恢复收藏的程度。

            a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy

            持久且有意义的文化遗产

            legacy是前人行动留给后来者的影响或成果；这里不是遗产金额，而是可被公众持续接触的艺术收藏。

            句子精读

            Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.

            虽然她们依靠一群信赖的顾问，但仍经常前往伦敦和巴黎，也常让人把画送到家中供她们考虑。

            Although引出依靠顾问的事实，主句突出她们自己的主动参与。made frequent trips和had paintings sent并列；have something done表示安排别人完成某事，sent是过去分词。for consideration说明送画是为了供她们考察是否购买，而非已经购入。

            The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists.

            格温多琳和玛格丽特·戴维斯的收藏分别于1951年和1963年捐给威尔士国家博物馆，其中包括法国重要印象派画家的代表作品。

            主干是collection contains major examples。donated...是插入的过去分词短语，补充藏品的捐赠去向和时间；respectively将两位姐妹按姓名顺序与两个年份对应。by leading French Impressionists修饰work，leading在这里指具有重要地位，并非位置靠前。

            这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

            a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy

            持久且有意义的文化遗产

            可用于讨论文化活动对未来的贡献，但要写清通过什么机制传承，例如保留地方戏剧、作品或表演传统，不能只用抽象赞美代替解释。

            用于写作：直接服务于实体剧院的文化价值：说明现场演出空间如何承载和传递传统，而不只比较观看的便利程度。

            读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

            Why we need silence｜噪声风险与城市降噪未作答段落信息匹配 / 人物／特征匹配 · 3 段 · 341 词 · 4 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 21 页

            Q14–16：Which section contains the following information? 原选项A–G保留，本片段含A–C。Q23：Match the statement with the correct person, A–D. You may use any letter more than once.

            AHumans are finely attuned to noise, and for good reason. From an evolutionary perspective, sounds give us vital information, helping us navigate the world and avoid danger. To help ensure loud or unexpected noises get the attention they deserve, our internal chemistry alters in response to them. Our blood pressure goes up, muscles tense and glands release hormones that prepare us for fight or flight. In the short term, this is a good thing. When we are exposed to too much noise over the long term, however, those responses can lead to a multitude of health issues, from sleep disturbance to even cardiovascular disease.

            BThe World Health Organization has recently designated excessive noise as an 'underestimated threat' to public health, and has said that people living in cities such as Mumbai, Tokyo and Buenos Aires are being exposed to far more than the recommended 40 decibels of noise at night. A report from the European Environment Agency concluded that noise was an ongoing and widespread issue in Europe, with at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health. 'There are no "earlids" that can protect your brain from noise,' says Nick Antonio, an acoustic consultant who has contributed to the British and international standards for noise.

            CThe good news is that several cities have been working to turn the volume down. One of the first to do so was London. 'By providing recommendations for quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft, they were able to make the city quieter,' says Antonio. Other cities have introduced noise-reducing road coatings, for instance, alongside greenery that muffles sound. Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier. 'People are seeing the benefits of these more quiet environments in their cities,' Antonio says. 'I expect we will see much more of this in the future.'

            共用选项 · 原题 14、15、16

            • A
            • B
            • C
            • D
            • E
            • F
            • G

            14. examples of strategies to decrease the noise that the public are exposed to

            15. data indicating the extent of the problem of excessive noise

            16. a description of physiological changes in our bodies when we hear sudden noises

            23. The trend towards creating quieter urban locations is likely to increase in the coming years.

            • A Nick Antonio
            • B Justin Feinstein
            • C Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan
            • D Eric Pfeifer

            对照答案，回到证据

            第 14 题 · C

            C列举公交、道路、飞机以及禁令等多项策略；不是只说噪声有害的B。

            quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft

            第 15 题 · B

            extent看覆盖范围；1 in 5与城市夜间分贝限制构成具体数据证据。

            at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health

            第 16 题 · A

            blood pressure、muscles、glands是身体变化，不是社会影响。

            Our blood pressure goes up, muscles tense and glands release hormones

            第 23 题 · A

            这句话属于Antonio的直接引语，预测降噪趋势继续增加。

            I expect we will see much more of this in the future.

            核对原答案页

            材料精读 · 内容与词句

            文章先解释人为什么对声音敏感，再区分短暂警觉的适应价值与长期噪声暴露的健康代价，最后转入城市治理。身体机制、公共健康风险和具体降噪行动形成连续关系。

            A

            A Humans are finely attuned to noise, and for good reason. From an evolutionary perspective, sounds give us vital information, helping us navigate the world and avoid danger. To help ensure loud or unexpected noises get the attention they deserve, our internal chemistry alters in response to them. Our blood pressure goes up, muscles tense and glands release hormones that prepare us for fight or flight. In the short term, this is a good thing. When we are exposed to too much noise over the long term, however, those responses can lead to a multitude of health issues, from sleep disturbance to even cardiovascular disease.

            声音在进化中帮助人辨认环境和躲避危险，因此突然而响亮的声音会引起血压升高、肌肉紧张和激素释放，为战斗或逃跑做准备。短期内这种反应有保护作用；长期反复承受过量噪声，却可能与睡眠和心血管等健康问题相连。however标出评价变化，变化的关键在暴露的强度和持续时间，而不是所有声音都有害。

            B

            B The World Health Organization has recently designated excessive noise as an 'underestimated threat' to public health, and has said that people living in cities such as Mumbai, Tokyo and Buenos Aires are being exposed to far more than the recommended 40 decibels of noise at night. A report from the European Environment Agency concluded that noise was an ongoing and widespread issue in Europe, with at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health. 'There are no "earlids" that can protect your brain from noise,' says Nick Antonio, an acoustic consultant who has contributed to the British and international standards for noise.

            文中引用世界卫生组织和欧洲环境署的说法，将上一段的个体反应扩大为公共健康议题：一些城市的夜间噪声高于文中提到的建议值，欧洲也有相当数量的人持续处于有害噪声水平。声学顾问用没有earlids这一比喻说明，人不像闭眼那样能简单关闭听觉。这些数值与recently都是原文写作时期的描述，不代表实时更新的统计。

            C

            C The good news is that several cities have been working to turn the volume down. One of the first to do so was London. 'By providing recommendations for quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft, they were able to make the city quieter,' says Antonio. Other cities have introduced noise-reducing road coatings, for instance, alongside greenery that muffles sound. Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier. 'People are seeing the benefits of these more quiet environments in their cities,' Antonio says. 'I expect we will see much more of this in the future.'

            作者转向城市已经采取的改善措施：伦敦从公交、道路和飞机噪声入手，其他城市采用低噪声路面与绿化，还有城市针对吹叶机或人为改响车辆立法。段落从综合政策写到具体噪声来源，说明公共环境可以通过设计和管理改变。最后关于未来会有更多行动的说法是Antonio的期待，不是已经发生的事实。

            词语与搭配

            finely attuned to noise

            对噪声非常敏感

            be attuned to表示敏锐察觉或适应某种信号；finely加强感知的精细程度。

            in response to them

            作为对它们的反应

            in response to引出反应的触发因素；them回指响亮或出乎意料的声音。

            an ongoing and widespread issue

            一个持续存在且影响广泛的问题

            ongoing说明时间上的持续，widespread说明涉及范围大，两者从不同维度描述问题。

            reducing noise from roads

            减少来自道路的噪声

            from说明噪声来源；这里属于城市治理措施之一，表达的是降低噪声，而非把所有道路移除。

            greenery that muffles sound

            能够减弱声音的绿化植被

            muffle是使声音变低、变闷，不能理解为完全隔绝；that从句说明这里提到绿化的功能。

            句子精读

            When we are exposed to too much noise over the long term, however, those responses can lead to a multitude of health issues, from sleep disturbance to even cardiovascular disease.

            然而，当我们长期暴露于过量噪声时，这些反应可能引发多种健康问题，从睡眠受扰，甚至到心血管疾病。

            When从句同时限定过量噪声与长期暴露。those responses回指前文血压、肌肉和激素的变化；can lead to表示可能的后果，不是每次暴露都会产生疾病。from...to...列出不同程度的健康问题，however把短期保护作用与长期风险连接起来。

            Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier.

            一些措施更加具体：华盛顿特区对汽油动力吹叶机的禁令近期开始生效，而纽约市则已批准立法，对改装车辆使其更吵的人处以罚款。

            冒号后给出两座城市的实例，while在此并列对照两项政策，并非说明同时发生。to fine交代立法的目的；who修饰people，to make them noisier说明改装造成的变化，them指车辆。recently以原文叙述时间为参照。

            这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

            reducing noise from roads

            减少道路噪声

            适合说明鼓励公共交通、步行或骑行可能带来的生活环境收益。需要具体写出减少何种车流或噪声源，不把交通方式改变等同于必然消除所有噪声。

            用于写作：题目讨论鼓励替代交通与限制车辆使用；道路噪声是与车辆使用直接相关的生活环境理由。

            noise from aircraft

            飞机产生的噪声

            可用于旅游活动对机场附近居民的影响，须说明航班增长这一具体联系；不能把所有旅游目的地的主要问题一律写成航空噪声。

            用于写作：题目明确要求考虑旅游对当地居民与环境的影响；条件句把表达限定在航空活动增长的目的地。

            读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

            Why we need silence｜漂浮舱的两项实验未作答摘要填空 / 人物／特征匹配 · 3 段 · 311 词 · 5 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 21 页

            Q18–21：Complete the summary. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Q24：Match the statement with the correct person A–D.

            DResearchers are also seeking to understand what aspects of silent experiences are most beneficial to our health. One of the best-researched is the flotation tank: a lightproof, soundproof tank of salt water in which a person floats as a form of deep relaxation. While some people experience altered perception in the tanks, involving subtle humming sounds and visual effects, these effects are benign and do not detract from the benefits of the experience, says Justin Feinstein, a clinical neuropsychologist. 'When you don't have external sensory stimuli coming in, the brain tries to fill the void to make sense of this dark and silent world,' he explains. 'In these tanks, some people can even hear the sound of their eyes blinking,' says Feinstein. 'But it is the ability to focus on the breath that helps people reach a relaxed or meditative state.'

            E（第一段）E To further explore flotation tanks as a therapeutic tool, Feinstein and his colleagues recruited 50 people with a variety of conditions related to stress and had them answer a questionnaire prior to and following a flotation session. Participants reported decreases in muscle tension, pain and symptoms of their conditions after a single, 1-hour float, alongside an increase in feelings of relaxation and overall wellbeing.

            E（第二段）Less is known about what effects sensory deprivation can have on the brain. To investigate, Feinstein's team had 48 people participate in either three 90-minute float sessions or three 90-minute periods of relaxing on a chair which reclined. Participants had their brains scanned using functional magnetic resonance imaging at the beginning and end of the trial. Float sessions uniquely decreased activity in the default mode network (DMN), a collection of brain regions commonly linked with depression. Feinstein says it is an exciting finding, because flotation tanks seem to offer a way of 'resetting' our nervous system to prevent it from getting out of balance.

            18. According to Justin Feinstein, flotation tanks allow people to concentrate on their own 18 __________, which helps them relax and enables them to meditate.

            19. Feinstein and his colleagues conducted an experiment in which 50 people, who were all suffering from stress and related issues, were given a 19 __________ to complete before and after using a flotation tank.

            20. Participants reported a reduction in their symptoms after an hour in the tank, together with signs of relaxation and improved general 20 __________.

            21. In another experiment, the researchers had 48 people spend periods of 90 minutes either lying back in a chair or floating in a tank. Brain scans then revealed that those people who had been in a tank had decreased activity in parts of the brain associated with 21 __________.

            24. When our body's senses are completely deprived of input, our minds compensate for this by creating the illusion of images and sounds.

            • A Nick Antonio
            • B Justin Feinstein
            • C Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan
            • D Eric Pfeifer

            对照答案，回到证据

            第 18 题 · breath

            concentrate on与focus on同义；不是描述感官幻觉的humming sounds。

            the ability to focus on the breath

            第 19 题 · questionnaire

            50 people唯一锁定第一项实验，before and after对应prior to and following。

            answer a questionnaire prior to and following a flotation session

            第 20 题 · wellbeing

            general对应overall；答案是整体状态wellbeing，不是症状pain。

            an increase in feelings of relaxation and overall wellbeing

            第 21 题 · depression

            associated with对应linked with；48人/90分钟与上一项50人/一小时必须分开。

            a collection of brain regions commonly linked with depression

            第 24 题 · B

            D引语来自Feinstein；visual effects与humming sounds对应images and sounds。

            the brain tries to fill the void to make sense of this dark and silent world

            核对原答案页

            材料精读 · 内容与词句

            这一部分围绕漂浮舱提出两个层次的问题：人主观上有什么感受，脑活动发生了什么变化。文章分别介绍问卷与脑扫描研究，并保留科学解释中的不确定性；参与者报告的轻松感不能直接扩大成对所有疾病或所有人的疗效结论。

            D

            D Researchers are also seeking to understand what aspects of silent experiences are most beneficial to our health. One of the best-researched is the flotation tank: a lightproof, soundproof tank of salt water in which a person floats as a form of deep relaxation. While some people experience altered perception in the tanks, involving subtle humming sounds and visual effects, these effects are benign and do not detract from the benefits of the experience, says Justin Feinstein, a clinical neuropsychologist. 'When you don't have external sensory stimuli coming in, the brain tries to fill the void to make sense of this dark and silent world,' he explains. 'In these tanks, some people can even hear the sound of their eyes blinking,' says Feinstein. 'But it is the ability to focus on the breath that helps people reach a relaxed or meditative state.'

            漂浮舱通过遮光、隔音和盐水漂浮减少外界感觉输入。有人会听见轻微嗡鸣或出现视觉感受，Feinstein认为这可能是大脑在缺少外界刺激时尝试填补空白。这些现象在他的描述中是良性的；真正帮助进入放松状态的，是把注意力放在呼吸上的能力。本段是在介绍一种体验及专家解释，并非要求读者自行进行治疗。

            E（第一段）

            E To further explore flotation tanks as a therapeutic tool, Feinstein and his colleagues recruited 50 people with a variety of conditions related to stress and had them answer a questionnaire prior to and following a flotation session. Participants reported decreases in muscle tension, pain and symptoms of their conditions after a single, 1-hour float, alongside an increase in feelings of relaxation and overall wellbeing.

            研究团队招募50名有不同压力相关状况的人，在一次漂浮前后填写问卷。参与者报告一小时后肌肉紧张、疼痛和相关症状减少，放松感与整体舒适感提高。这里的信息来自参与者的前后自报；本段没有交代对照条件或长期追踪，因而只宜理解为此次研究中观察到的短时体验变化。

            E（第二段）

            Less is known about what effects sensory deprivation can have on the brain. To investigate, Feinstein's team had 48 people participate in either three 90-minute float sessions or three 90-minute periods of relaxing on a chair which reclined. Participants had their brains scanned using functional magnetic resonance imaging at the beginning and end of the trial. Float sessions uniquely decreased activity in the default mode network (DMN), a collection of brain regions commonly linked with depression. Feinstein says it is an exciting finding, because flotation tanks seem to offer a way of 'resetting' our nervous system to prevent it from getting out of balance.

            第二项研究改为考察大脑：48人分别接受三次90分钟漂浮或在躺椅上放松，并在研究开始和结束时做功能磁共振扫描。原文报告只有漂浮组出现默认模式网络活动降低，该网络常与抑郁有关。Feinstein把这解释为可能帮助神经系统重获平衡的线索；seem和resetting上的引号提醒读者，这是一种试探性、形象化解释，不等于已经证明能治疗抑郁。

            词语与搭配

            external sensory stimuli

            外界感觉刺激

            stimuli是stimulus的复数，指来自声音、光线等的感觉输入；这里解释漂浮舱改变了什么环境条件。

            do not detract from the benefits

            不会削弱其益处

            detract from后接价值、效果或吸引力，表示使其减少；文中是专家对特定体验的评价。

            as a therapeutic tool

            作为一种治疗或辅助治疗手段

            as标明研究考察的用途，therapeutic不意味着已经获得对所有疾病的有效性证明。

            prior to and following a flotation session

            在一次漂浮体验之前和之后

            prior to与following平行标明两个测量时点；它们本身并不说明因果或效果能维持多久。

            句子精读

            To further explore flotation tanks as a therapeutic tool, Feinstein and his colleagues recruited 50 people with a variety of conditions related to stress and had them answer a questionnaire prior to and following a flotation session.

            为进一步探索漂浮舱作为治疗手段的作用，Feinstein及其同事招募了50名有多种压力相关状况的人，让他们在一次漂浮体验前后填写问卷。

            开头To further explore说明研究目的。主干包含recruited和had两个并列动作；with...修饰people，related to stress修饰conditions。have somebody do something表示让某人做某事，所以answer保持动词原形；prior to and following共同修饰填写问卷的时间。

            Feinstein says it is an exciting finding, because flotation tanks seem to offer a way of 'resetting' our nervous system to prevent it from getting out of balance.

            Feinstein表示，这是一项令人兴奋的发现，因为漂浮舱似乎提供了一种让神经系统“重置”的方式，以防其失去平衡。

            says标出评价来自Feinstein；第一个it指前文默认模式网络活动降低的发现。seem to保留推测色彩，'resetting'是引号中的比喻。to prevent说明可能目的，prevent it from doing中的it指神经系统；句子不把这一解释写成已经确定的临床疗效。

            读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

            Why we need silence｜主动安静与短时收益未作答段落信息匹配 / 人物／特征匹配 · 3 段 · 304 词 · 4 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 22 页

            Q17：Which section A–G contains the information? Q22/25/26：Match statements with people A–D. You may use any letter more than once.

            F（第一段）F Neurobiologist Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan is also an advocate of silence as a therapy. 'When we find ways to be quiet, we are not only quiet in our environment, but quiet in our inner selves,' she explains. 'This allows us to be more aware of what is happening around us and what the situation may require from us so we can provide [a more] adequate response.'

            F（第二段）Not everyone will benefit from silence to the same extent, but Ben-Soussan says one characteristic is key: the person must need to want to engage in the experience. 'We see from animal models and human studies that volition and intentionality is important,' she says. 'When people do not want silence, it can be very distressing.'

            GEric Pfeifer, a psychotherapy researcher, also concedes that some people may not benefit from silence, particularly those who are in a heightened state of stress. 'People in these states may not be able to relax or calm down in a silent condition,' he says. Professional guidance can be useful, he adds, allowing people to approach silence slowly so that they can gradually enjoy the benefits. And Pfeifer is convinced that silence is more attainable in everyday life than people think. First, complete silence isn't necessary. In a recent study, he found that participants reported more relaxation and less boredom when they sat quietly in an outdoor garden compared with a completely silent room. Second, Pfeifer believes we don't need a lot of silence to gain benefits. 'You don't need to spend hours in silence,' he says. 'It is likely better to have more frequency of silence for a few minutes at a time than a longer period of silence only once a week. Just finding those places in your daily life where you can find some silence ... can make a big difference.'

            共用选项 · 原题 22、25、26

            • A Nick Antonio
            • B Justin Feinstein
            • C Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan
            • D Eric Pfeifer

            17. evidence that a relatively quiet environment can be more beneficial than a totally silent one

            • A
            • B
            • C
            • D
            • E
            • F
            • G

            22. It is unpleasant and upsetting for people to be placed in a silent environment against their will.

            25. Even a short amount of silent time can have a positive impact.

            26. External and internal quietness makes us more conscious of events occurring in our surroundings and helps us react appropriately to these events.

            对照答案，回到证据

            第 17 题 · G

            必须有两种环境的比较；G中花园与完全静音房间的结果符合题干。

            more relaxation and less boredom when they sat quietly in an outdoor garden compared with a completely silent room

            第 22 题 · C

            F第二段Ben-Soussan把自愿性列为前提，against their will对应do not want。

            When people do not want silence, it can be very distressing.

            第 25 题 · D

            G的Pfeifer明确说几分钟、高频也有益，不要求一次持续数小时。

            Just finding those places in your daily life where you can find some silence ... can make a big difference.

            第 26 题 · C

            F第一段Ben-Soussan提到外部与内在安静，进而更好回应环境。

            more aware of what is happening around us and what the situation may require from us

            核对原答案页

            材料精读 · 内容与词句

            安静在这里不是越彻底、越久就越好。文章强调个人意愿、当前心理状态和适应过程，再把理想化的绝对无声，转化为日常中较容易获得的短暂安静。

            F（第一段）

            F Neurobiologist Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan is also an advocate of silence as a therapy. 'When we find ways to be quiet, we are not only quiet in our environment, but quiet in our inner selves,' she explains. 'This allows us to be more aware of what is happening around us and what the situation may require from us so we can provide [a more] adequate response.'

            Ben-Soussan把安静区分为外部环境的安静与内在状态的安静。她认为后者可以帮助人更清楚地觉察周围情况，并作出合宜反应。This承接这种内外安静的状态，而不是单指没有任何声音；本段呈现的是她对安静作用的解释。

            F（第二段）

            Not everyone will benefit from silence to the same extent, but Ben-Soussan says one characteristic is key: the person must need to want to engage in the experience. 'We see from animal models and human studies that volition and intentionality is important,' she says. 'When people do not want silence, it can be very distressing.'

            文章马上加入限制：不同人的获益程度不一样，而且主动愿意参与体验很重要。volition与intentionality指个人的意愿和有意识的参与。如果一个人并不想处于安静之中，这种情境反而可能令人痛苦。因此，安静不能被当成不顾意愿、对所有人都适用的要求。

            G

            G Eric Pfeifer, a psychotherapy researcher, also concedes that some people may not benefit from silence, particularly those who are in a heightened state of stress. 'People in these states may not be able to relax or calm down in a silent condition,' he says. Professional guidance can be useful, he adds, allowing people to approach silence slowly so that they can gradually enjoy the benefits. And Pfeifer is convinced that silence is more attainable in everyday life than people think. First, complete silence isn't necessary. In a recent study, he found that participants reported more relaxation and less boredom when they sat quietly in an outdoor garden compared with a completely silent room. Second, Pfeifer believes we don't need a lot of silence to gain benefits. 'You don't need to spend hours in silence,' he says. 'It is likely better to have more frequency of silence for a few minutes at a time than a longer period of silence only once a week. Just finding those places in your daily life where you can find some silence ... can make a big difference.'

            Pfeifer进一步指出，高度紧张的人有时无法在安静环境中放松，专业指导可以帮助其逐渐适应。他随后提出两个让安静更可获得的想法：不必绝对无声，研究参与者在安静花园中比完全无声的房间更放松、较少无聊；也不必每次持续很久。他倾向于频繁短时的安静，但原文用likely表达判断，并未给出对所有人有效的固定时长处方。

            词语与搭配

            to the same extent

            达到相同程度

            用于比较程度；Not everyone...to the same extent表示人与人之间有差异，不是所有人完全没有益处。

            engage in the experience

            参与并投入这种体验

            engage in后接活动或过程；此处强调主动愿意参与，而不只是身体置于安静房间。

            a heightened state of stress

            一种压力升高、紧张加剧的状态

            heightened修饰state所指的程度，描述当时状态，不能直接给某人贴上永久性标签。

            a few minutes at a time

            每次几分钟

            at a time说明单次持续长度，与一周只进行一次但时间很长相对照。

            句子精读

            Professional guidance can be useful, he adds, allowing people to approach silence slowly so that they can gradually enjoy the benefits.

            他补充说，专业指导可能有所帮助，让人慢慢接近和适应安静，从而逐渐享受到其中的益处。

            he adds是插入的转述语，he指Pfeifer。allowing...补充说明专业指导如何起作用；so that连接渐进适应与预期收益。can be useful表示可能有帮助，slowly与gradually共同强调过程，而非立即强迫人进入完全无声的状态。

            In a recent study, he found that participants reported more relaxation and less boredom when they sat quietly in an outdoor garden compared with a completely silent room.

            在近期的一项研究中，他发现参与者报告说，相比待在完全无声的房间里，安静地坐在室外花园中会让他们更放松，也更少感到无聊。

            found后的that从句说明研究发现，reported提醒这是参与者报告的体验。when从句描述花园条件，compared with引出对比的房间条件。more relaxation与less boredom是两个并列变化；recent以原文写作时点为参照，句子没有宣称花园对每个人或每种健康状况都更有效。

            读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

            The World of Sugar｜全球贸易与误解纠正未作答选择题 · 3 段 · 248 词 · 3 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 26 页

            Choose the correct letter A, B, C or D. 原题Q27–29。

            原文第1段Ulbe Bosma's The World of Sugar is a genuinely global history. Bosma discusses all the sugar growing places of the world, beginning with Cuba and Java, the largest exporters of the early 20th century. But this is a history not just of cane sugar but also of beet sugar, an equally important form of traded sugar over the last hundred years. Beet sugar is grown mainly in Europe and the United States. It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

            原文第2段Bosma's discussion of the sugar market in Britain gives a sense of the book's range. The sweet-toothed British first bought cane sugar from their own slavery-dependent colonial plantations. Following the abolition of slavery in the British Empire, cane sugar was imported to Britain from places which retained the practice, such as Cuba and Brazil. Towards the end of the 19th century, the British started to import beet sugar from continental Europe. Only in the 20th century was there a move to develop a national beet sugar industry.

            原文第3段The book provides a global labour history, investigating the wide range of labour regimes associated with growing sugar. Contrary to popular belief, cane sugar production was never just restricted to large, dedicated plantations owned by rich men. For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.

            27. What does the reviewer suggest about the cultivation and trading of sugar in the first paragraph?

            • A Sugar has played a major role in international relations.
            • B Beet sugar has been made more internationally competitive.
            • C Cane sugar is thought to be of superior quality to beet sugar.
            • D New locations for cultivating sugar have increased production.

            28. In the second paragraph, when discussing the sugar market in Britain, the reviewer stresses

            • A how the sources used changed over time.
            • B how developments in agriculture affected trade.
            • C the increased demand for sugar over the years.
            • D the growing support for ethical methods of cultivation.

            29. What is the reviewer doing in the third paragraph?

            • A describing an efficient approach to sugar cultivation
            • B explaining why the use of sugar plantations declined
            • C addressing a misconception about the growing of sugar cane
            • D evaluating different approaches to the cultivation of sugar cane

            对照答案，回到证据

            第 27 题 · B

            补贴让甜菜糖以人为低价竞争，支持B。文中并未比较甘蔗糖品质。

            massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets

            第 28 题 · A

            first→Following→Towards the end→Only in the 20th century构成来源随时间变动的序列。

            first bought cane sugar from their own slavery-dependent colonial plantations

            第 29 题 · C

            首句提出劳动力历史，Contrary to popular belief明确纠正普遍误解，小农Java例子服务于该功能。

            Contrary to popular belief, cane sugar production was never just restricted to large, dedicated plantations

            核对原答案页

            材料精读 · 内容与词句

            这是一篇书评的开头：作者介绍Bosma如何把糖写成一部全球贸易史和劳动史。甘蔗糖与甜菜糖、进口来源的变化、大种植园与小农生产相互补充，使糖的历史不再只剩单一地区或单一劳动制度。

            原文第1段

            Ulbe Bosma's The World of Sugar is a genuinely global history. Bosma discusses all the sugar growing places of the world, beginning with Cuba and Java, the largest exporters of the early 20th century. But this is a history not just of cane sugar but also of beet sugar, an equally important form of traded sugar over the last hundred years. Beet sugar is grown mainly in Europe and the United States. It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

            书评首先评价这是一部真正具有全球范围的糖史，既讨论古巴和爪哇等甘蔗糖出口地，也把欧洲、美国的甜菜糖纳入。随后指出补贴与人为压低的价格会影响世界市场，威胁甘蔗糖生产者的生计。It指甜菜糖这一行业和产品，不能理解为世界上所有糖生产都采用同一制度。

            原文第2段

            Bosma's discussion of the sugar market in Britain gives a sense of the book's range. The sweet-toothed British first bought cane sugar from their own slavery-dependent colonial plantations. Following the abolition of slavery in the British Empire, cane sugar was imported to Britain from places which retained the practice, such as Cuba and Brazil. Towards the end of the 19th century, the British started to import beet sugar from continental Europe. Only in the 20th century was there a move to develop a national beet sugar industry.

            英国市场的进口变化展示了全书的跨度：先从依赖奴役劳动的本国殖民种植园购买甘蔗糖，废奴后仍从保留奴隶制的古巴、巴西等地进口，19世纪末开始进口欧洲甜菜糖，20世纪才发展本国甜菜糖业。这段揭示，某国法律改变与商品供应链中的劳动制度变化并不一定同步。

            原文第3段

            The book provides a global labour history, investigating the wide range of labour regimes associated with growing sugar. Contrary to popular belief, cane sugar production was never just restricted to large, dedicated plantations owned by rich men. For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.

            作者转向劳动组织的多样性，纠正甘蔗糖始终只由富人拥有的大型专门种植园生产这一单一想象。爪哇的小农曾以高度劳动密集的方式同时种甘蔗和水稻，是这种多样性的一个实例。not just restricted强调不只存在大种植园，并没有否认大种植园的重要历史。

            词语与搭配

            sold at artificially low prices

            以人为压低的价格出售

            artificially在这里指价格受到补贴等外部干预，不是说产品是假货；at引出出售价格。

            threatening the livelihood of

            威胁……的生计

            livelihood指赖以谋生的方式和收入基础；此处现在分词说明低价竞争带来的影响。

            Following the abolition of slavery

            在奴隶制废除之后

            following相当于after，标记时间关系；它本身不保证其他国家或供应链也同时发生同样变化。

            Contrary to popular belief

            与普遍看法相反

            用于引入与常见理解不一致的事实，后面需要具体内容或例证支持，不能只把自己的意见写成事实纠正。

            an extraordinarily labour-intensive way

            一种极为依赖大量劳动投入的方式

            labour-intensive描述生产对劳动投入的依赖程度，与单纯技术先进或落后不是同一个概念。

            句子精读

            It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

            甜菜糖还获得了巨额补贴，并在世界市场上以人为压低的价格出售，威胁着甘蔗糖生产者的生计。

            It承接上句的beet sugar；has been统领subsidised和sold两个被动分词。at引出价格，on world markets说明交易范围。末尾threatening...是补充结果的现在分词短语，说明受影响的是甘蔗糖生产者，而非把两种糖当成同一种生产群体。

            For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.

            例如，在20世纪初的重要食糖出口地爪哇，小农以极其劳动密集的方式，把甘蔗与水稻一起种植。

            主干是sugar cane was grown...by small farmers。a huge exporter...是Java的同位语，交代地区背景；together with rice说明共同种植的作物，in...way说明生产方式。句子把出口规模大与生产者是小农放在一起，说明两者可以同时成立。

            这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

            threatening the livelihood of

            威胁……的生计

            适合用于描述资源衰退或不公平竞争怎样影响依赖某产业谋生的人。可以作为结果分词短语，但要让前面的原因具体可理解。

            用于写作：现有题目明确谈过度捕捞对数百万人生计的风险；表达可直接连接鱼类资源减少与沿海家庭收入受损。

            读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

            The World of Sugar｜劳动组织与行业权力未作答选词摘要填空 · 2 段 · 203 词 · 6 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 26 页

            Complete the summary using the list of words A–I. Write the correct letter A–I. 原选项完整保留；Q31–36。

            原文第4段The World of Sugar is also a story of similarity and continuity in sugar cultivation. For example, imported labour has been used for much large-scale production. German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production. Cane cutting, Bosma shows, remains a poorly paid and brutal business to this day in many places in the world. But as well as this, the book is about the continuity of the use of traditional methods on small farms. In the mid 20th-century, this type of sugar production dominated in South Asia and Latin America.

            原文第5段This is also a history of capitalists and sugar dynasties, as well as corporations that in some cases have remained influential over very long periods. Great firms and great interests have had profound influence on the policies of states. In many places - not just the British Caribbean but Cuba and the Philippines too - a powerful sugar bourgeoisie played a major role in politics and their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies. In the battle for control of the industry, it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse. All this is explored by Bosma with wonderful subtlety and control.

            共用选项 · 原题 31、32、33、34、35、36

            • A national governments
            • B agricultural developments
            • C less wealthy nations
            • D untrained workers
            • E small-scale cultivation
            • F outdated methods
            • G financial controls
            • H migrant workers
            • I powerful individuals and businesses

            31. In the big industries in both Germany and the US, sugar farming depended on 31 __________.

            32. However, in other parts of the world such as South Asia and Latin America, 32 __________ continued.

            33. Sugar production has also involved 33 __________ who were eager to protect their markets.

            34. In countries such as Cuba the sugar industry therefore had a major influence on 34 __________.

            35. To support the interests of sugar producers, 35 __________ were established.

            36. As a result of this, 36 __________ were penalised.

            对照答案，回到证据

            第 31 题 · H

            波兰人赴德、墨西哥人等赴美均是跨地迁移劳工，概括为migrant workers。

            German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production

            第 32 题 · E

            small farms与small-scale cultivation对应；F outdated带有落后评价，原文只说traditional。

            traditional methods on small farms

            第 33 题 · I

            资本家、糖业家族与公司合并概括为powerful individuals and businesses。

            a history of capitalists and sugar dynasties, as well as corporations

            第 34 题 · A

            policies of states和politics对应national governments，不是农业技术。

            Great firms and great interests have had profound influence on the policies of states

            第 35 题 · G

            贸易壁垒与补贴是financial controls的实例，不能只靠相同词选项。

            their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies

            第 36 题 · C

            poor countries对应less wealthy nations，came off worse对应were penalised。

            it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse

            核对原答案页

            材料精读 · 内容与词句

            这部分将糖业的连续性放在两个层面观察：劳动者的处境和传统生产方式延续，资本、企业与国家政策的关系也长期存在。书评由田间劳动转向政治经济，解释谁能够保护自己的利益，谁更容易承担代价。

            原文第4段

            The World of Sugar is also a story of similarity and continuity in sugar cultivation. For example, imported labour has been used for much large-scale production. German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production. Cane cutting, Bosma shows, remains a poorly paid and brutal business to this day in many places in the world. But as well as this, the book is about the continuity of the use of traditional methods on small farms. In the mid 20th-century, this type of sugar production dominated in South Asia and Latin America.

            德国甜菜业、美国糖业都使用跨境劳工，说明不同地区的规模生产有相似的劳动力来源。作者继而指出，在文中所说的许多地方，砍甘蔗仍是报酬低、劳动艰苦的工作。另一种连续性是小农传统方法的延续，20世纪中叶在南亚和拉丁美洲占重要地位。连续性既指劳动处境，也指生产形式，不能把两者缩成同一个现象。

            原文第5段

            This is also a history of capitalists and sugar dynasties, as well as corporations that in some cases have remained influential over very long periods. Great firms and great interests have had profound influence on the policies of states. In many places - not just the British Caribbean but Cuba and the Philippines too - a powerful sugar bourgeoisie played a major role in politics and their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies. In the battle for control of the industry, it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse. All this is explored by Bosma with wonderful subtlety and control.

            镜头从工人和农户转到资本家、糖业家族与长期有影响力的公司。书评认为，强大的糖业利益集团参与政治，并通过贸易壁垒和补贴保护自身利益；争夺行业控制权时，较穷国家更容易处于不利地位。最后一句是书评作者对Bosma叙述细致程度的赞赏，与前面概括的经济历史内容属于不同层次。

            词语与搭配

            similarity and continuity

            相似性与延续性

            similarity比较不同地方或群体，continuity关注跨时间的持续；两词并列组织本段的观察角度。

            a poorly paid and brutal business

            一种报酬低且极为艰苦的营生

            business在这里指谋生活动，brutal强调劳动处境严酷；不是泛指某家公司。

            remained influential over very long periods

            在很长时期内持续具有影响力

            remain后接形容词，说明状态持续；over very long periods突出跨越时间的力量。

            trade barriers and subsidies

            贸易壁垒与补贴

            两者都是影响市场的政策工具，但机制不同：前者限制外部竞争，后者提供支持；其具体后果需要结合行业和政策设计讨论。

            came off worse

            在竞争或冲突中处于更不利的结果

            come off是表示结果的短语动词，worse说明相对劣势；这里指贫穷国家在行业权力争夺中的处境。

            句子精读

            In many places - not just the British Caribbean but Cuba and the Philippines too - a powerful sugar bourgeoisie played a major role in politics and their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies.

            在许多地方——不只是英属加勒比地区，也包括古巴和菲律宾——强大的糖业资产阶级在政治中发挥重要作用，因此其利益受到贸易壁垒和补贴的保护。

            两处短横线夹出地区范围的补充说明。主干用and连接played...与their interests were protected...；their指糖业资产阶级，consequently明确表现书评所概括的因果关系。not just...but...too扩大适用地区，并不意味着世界所有地区都完全一样。

            In the battle for control of the industry, it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse.

            在争夺行业控制权的斗争中，最终遭遇更不利处境的，必然是那些贫穷国家。

            In the battle...交代竞争情境；it was...which...是强调结构，突出承受不利结果的poor countries。came off worse描述结果，inevitably带有书评作者强烈的判断色彩，精读时应将这种概括与中性的统计描述区分。

            读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

            The World of Sugar｜工业化、消费与作者立场未作答观点判断 YNNG / 选择题 · 3 段 · 444 词 · 5 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 27 页

            Q30：Choose A–D. Q37–40：Do the statements agree with the views of the writer? YES / NO / NOT GIVEN。

            原文第6段But sugar production was never just a matter of agriculture. It also involved the extraction, close to the place of harvest, of sucrose from the sugar plant, a process which required machinery powered by humans, animals, wind or steam. Further processes involved boiling (from the 19th century, this often involved vacuum systems) and the separation of sugar from other materials in a process known as refinement. From very early on, sugar production was an energy-intensive industrial process, mostly taking place in the countryside and in refineries in centres of consumption, both small and large. The growth of the industry entailed a very rapid diffusion of ideas and techniques from one country to another. Cuba, for example, developed an extraordinarily dense system of railways to transport workers and cane, as well as steam-powered sugar factories. Particular varieties of cane sugar and beet sugar spread very rapidly across the world, in accordance with local needs and demands.

            原文第7段Where once only tiny quantities of sugar could be produced, now new techniques, varieties, fertilisers, irrigation systems and much more have turned gleaming white sugar into a ubiquitous chemical. Over the same time, there has been a massive increase in consumption. Once regarded as a luxury, sugar came to be promoted as a valuable source of energy. But as the consumption of sugar has increased, so has the harm it does, whether to people's teeth or weight. In the face of appalling obstruction from the sugar industry to attempts to reduce consumption, some countries have been forced to tax sugar in order to bring that about. The sugar industry has a history of attacking its critics and, when it comes to obesity, of trying to blame fats, and lack of exercise and self-control. And the recent past has seen worrying new developments in mass sweetening. High-fructose corn syrup made from maize using an enzymatic process invented in Japan in the 1960s has a similar number of calories to table sugar but is far cheaper to produce. It is now widely consumed, having been adopted in the making of soft drinks and a large number of processed foods, and is regarded as a leading cause of obesity.

            原文第8段This is a wonderfully rich book, a model of global history, the history of production and the history of capitalism. Bosma avoids outbursts of emotion, celebratory or critical, even if they might have made his analysis of the multiple tragedies involving sugar all the more powerful. He shows that we could always have done without sugar and that today we have many alternative sources of sweetness. Yet many of the poorest people in the world still depend on it to make a living.

            30. In the final paragraph, what does the reviewer suggest is the overall message of Bosma's book?

            • A Sugar is a harmful and unnecessary product.
            • B Economic pressure is needed to control sugar production.
            • C Conditions for workers in sugar production should be improved.
            • D Intensive marketing of sugar has had disastrous consequences.

            37. Sugar has now become available in large quantities due to a range of agricultural developments.

            38. Advertisers initially marketed sugar as a luxury product.

            39. The invention of high-fructose corn syrup was a positive development.

            40. High-fructose corn syrup is an ingredient in many processed foods.

            对照答案，回到证据

            第 30 题 · A

            前文解释危害，末段强调可不依赖糖与替代来源，A概括全书结论。末句贫困者生计不等于作者主张继续扩大糖业。

            we could always have done without sugar and that today we have many alternative sources of sweetness

            第 37 题 · YES

            new techniques等列举支持农业变化让糖大量普及；ubiquitous为无处不在。

            new techniques, varieties, fertilisers, irrigation systems and much more have turned gleaming white sugar into a ubiquitous chemical

            第 38 题 · NOT GIVEN

            过去被视为奢侈品，不等于广告商当时把它作为奢侈品营销；全文无该营销主体与初始策略信息。

            Once regarded as a luxury, sugar came to be promoted as a valuable source of energy.

            第 39 题 · NO

            作者用worrying并关联肥胖，明确与positive相反；便宜只是事实，不代表作者支持。

            the recent past has seen worrying new developments in mass sweetening

            第 40 题 · YES

            adopted in the making对应is an ingredient；many对应a large number。

            having been adopted in the making of soft drinks and a large number of processed foods

            核对原答案页

            材料精读 · 内容与词句

            书评从糖的种植转向提炼、能源和技术传播，再追踪大规模生产如何与消费增长及健康争议相连。结尾保留一个现实张力：人们可以减少对糖的依赖，但许多贫困生产者仍依靠糖业谋生。

            原文第6段

            But sugar production was never just a matter of agriculture. It also involved the extraction, close to the place of harvest, of sucrose from the sugar plant, a process which required machinery powered by humans, animals, wind or steam. Further processes involved boiling (from the 19th century, this often involved vacuum systems) and the separation of sugar from other materials in a process known as refinement. From very early on, sugar production was an energy-intensive industrial process, mostly taking place in the countryside and in refineries in centres of consumption, both small and large. The growth of the industry entailed a very rapid diffusion of ideas and techniques from one country to another. Cuba, for example, developed an extraordinarily dense system of railways to transport workers and cane, as well as steam-powered sugar factories. Particular varieties of cane sugar and beet sugar spread very rapidly across the world, in accordance with local needs and demands.

            糖不仅是农作物，还需要提取蔗糖、煮制和精炼，这些环节很早就依赖机械与能源。生产既在乡村进行，也在消费中心的精炼厂进行。行业扩张还推动技术、品种和运输设施跨国传播，古巴的密集铁路与蒸汽糖厂是例子。作者借此打破农业与工业截然分开的想象，同时强调不同地方会按照自身需要采用技术。

            原文第7段

            Where once only tiny quantities of sugar could be produced, now new techniques, varieties, fertilisers, irrigation systems and much more have turned gleaming white sugar into a ubiquitous chemical. Over the same time, there has been a massive increase in consumption. Once regarded as a luxury, sugar came to be promoted as a valuable source of energy. But as the consumption of sugar has increased, so has the harm it does, whether to people's teeth or weight. In the face of appalling obstruction from the sugar industry to attempts to reduce consumption, some countries have been forced to tax sugar in order to bring that about. The sugar industry has a history of attacking its critics and, when it comes to obesity, of trying to blame fats, and lack of exercise and self-control. And the recent past has seen worrying new developments in mass sweetening. High-fructose corn syrup made from maize using an enzymatic process invented in Japan in the 1960s has a similar number of calories to table sugar but is far cheaper to produce. It is now widely consumed, having been adopted in the making of soft drinks and a large number of processed foods, and is regarded as a leading cause of obesity.

            新的技术、品种、肥料和灌溉使糖从少量奢侈品变成普遍消费品，也被宣传为能量来源。书评随后转向消费增加带来的牙齿和体重问题，以及糖业阻挠减糖、转移责任的争议。末尾介绍高果糖玉米糖浆：热量与食糖相近，生产成本却低得多，因此被广泛用于饮料和加工食品；作者也转述了其与肥胖有关的评价。这是书评中的论述，不能把所有体重问题归于单一成分，也不能把文中now和recent past当成今日实时信息。

            原文第8段

            This is a wonderfully rich book, a model of global history, the history of production and the history of capitalism. Bosma avoids outbursts of emotion, celebratory or critical, even if they might have made his analysis of the multiple tragedies involving sugar all the more powerful. He shows that we could always have done without sugar and that today we have many alternative sources of sweetness. Yet many of the poorest people in the world still depend on it to make a living.

            结尾高度评价全书的全球史、生产史和资本主义史视角，同时指出Bosma克制了赞颂或批判的情绪表达。作者认为更强烈的情绪可能增强悲剧分析的冲击力，这是一种书评判断。最后的Yet重新引入生产者：即使消费者有其他甜味来源，许多穷人仍靠糖业生活，因此减少消费与保障生计需要一起被看见。

            词语与搭配

            an energy-intensive industrial process

            一种耗能密集的工业过程

            energy-intensive说明单位活动需要较多能源，industrial process指多环节加工；不能仅因原料来自农田就忽略加工环节。

            in accordance with local needs and demands

            依照当地需要与需求

            in accordance with表示与某种要求一致；这里说明技术和品种的传播并非各地完全相同。

            a massive increase in consumption

            消费的大幅增加

            increase in后接发生增长的指标；massive是强程度词，实际写作中应与有依据的规模判断相配。

            a valuable source of energy

            一种有价值的能量来源

            在本文中位于was promoted as之后，属于曾经的宣传定位，不等同于作者无条件推荐增加糖摄入。

            depend on it to make a living

            依靠它谋生

            depend on说明经济依赖，to make a living解释依赖的目的；it指糖及糖业相关生产。

            句子精读

            It also involved the extraction, close to the place of harvest, of sucrose from the sugar plant, a process which required machinery powered by humans, animals, wind or steam.

            糖的生产还包括在收获地点附近从糖料作物中提取蔗糖，这个过程需要由人力、畜力、风力或蒸汽驱动的机械。

            It指糖的生产。extraction of sucrose from the sugar plant是一个完整名词结构，中间插入close to the place of harvest补充地点；a process是对提取活动的同位说明。which修饰process，powered by...是过去分词短语修饰machinery，列出动力来源而非四个必须依次经过的阶段。

            In the face of appalling obstruction from the sugar industry to attempts to reduce consumption, some countries have been forced to tax sugar in order to bring that about.

            面对糖业对降低消费努力的严重阻挠，一些国家不得不对糖征税，以促成消费的减少。

            In the face of引出阻力背景；from the sugar industry说明阻挠来自谁，to attempts...说明受到阻挠的是哪类尝试。主干是some countries have been forced to tax sugar。that回指reduce consumption，in order to表达政策目的，不能单凭这个目的就判断政策效果已经实现。appalling保留了书评的批评态度。

            这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

            attempts to reduce consumption

            降低消费量的努力

            在健康话题里要补清consumption指什么，例如含糖饮料，而不是笼统主张减少所有食品消费。适合描述措施与商业激励之间的关系。

            用于写作：儿童肥胖题要求提出措施；这句话把减少含糖饮料摄入与可负担替代品联系起来，强调环境支持而非只责怪个人自控。

            a large number of processed foods

            大量加工食品

            可讨论配方、标签或食品环境，但加工食品并非全部有相同营养特征，例句应限定要比较的成分。

            用于写作：适合儿童肥胖措施段中的食品信息环境；条件句聚焦添加糖与标签，避免把所有加工食品概括为有害。

            读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

            Do animals dream?｜跨物种睡眠研究未作答表格填空 · 4 段 · 355 词 · 5 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 39 页

            Complete the table below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. 各行研究结果与评论合并为可输入题面，物种及原空号保留。

            原文第1段Studies using electrodes attached to the heads of sleepers have shown that when we sleep, we do so in two ways that alternate throughout the night. The first is rapid eye movement (REM) or active sleep. During this stage our eyes move, even though our eyelids are closed. Our muscles also twitch slightly, though they are largely paralysed so we don't hurt ourselves. In contrast, we also engage in non-REM sleep, during which we barely move at all. Most dream states, and certainly those with the most vivid dreams, happen during REM sleep.

            原文第2段There's some evidence that other mammals may also dream. For example, researchers compared the brain patterns of rats running through a maze when awake with their brain patterns during REM sleep. They found the patterns were very similar and concluded that the sleeping rats were dreaming about going through the maze.

            原文第3段But finding evidence of dreaming in non-mammals has proved more difficult. Their brains are very different from those of humans, and it can often be difficult to record their activity while they are sleeping. Recently, however, researchers succeeded in recording brain activity in sleeping pigeons. As in mammals, the recordings revealed both REM and non-REM sleep. Intriguingly, REM sleep activity was high in brain regions involved in processing visual information, especially images related to physical activities such as flying, which suggests that this may possibly be what the pigeons were dreaming about.

            原文第4段That said, dreaming and REM sleep are unlikely to be universal in the animal kingdom. For example, sponges don't have brains, so they lack the machinery for dreaming. There are also some animals with unusual sleep patterns. These include whales and dolphins, which do not shut down their entire brain when they sleep, but only half of it, keeping the rest awake. They also show no sign of REM sleep, suggesting that they may only experience non-REM dreams, which are less vivid. This is surprising because we tend to think of whales and dolphins as having complex inner lives. It's thought that they don't experience REM sleep because during REM sleep animals are more vulnerable to extremes of temperature.

            1. Research into sleep and dreaming — 1 __________: similar brain patterns were observed when active and sleeping; indicative of dreaming

            2. Pigeons: when sleeping, pigeons displayed activity in parts of the brain that deal with 2 __________ input; may have been dreaming of flying

            3. Whales and dolphins: still have 3 __________ their brain awake when they sleep

            4. Whales and dolphins: don't experience REM sleep, as this could affect their sensitivity to 4 __________

            5. Whales and dolphins: their dreams are probably not very 5 __________

            对照答案，回到证据

            第 1 题 · rats

            表格此行要求动物类别；清醒走迷宫与REM睡眠对比的是rats。

            the brain patterns of rats running through a maze when awake with their brain patterns during REM sleep

            第 2 题 · visual

            input对应information；空前deal with与processing相对应，所需形容词为visual。

            brain regions involved in processing visual information

            第 3 题 · half

            只关闭一半，所以另一半保持清醒。句子逻辑转换但数值不变。

            only half of it, keeping the rest awake

            第 4 题 · temperature

            原因落在末句；temperature而不是前文machinery或lives。

            during REM sleep animals are more vulnerable to extremes of temperature

            第 5 题 · vivid

            less vivid改写为not very vivid；保持形容词词性。

            non-REM dreams, which are less vivid

            核对原答案页

            材料精读 · 内容与词句

            作者从人类的两种睡眠状态出发，逐步追问其他动物是否也做梦。脑活动记录提供了跨物种比较的线索，但动物无法直接报告梦境，所以观察到的睡眠特征与对主观体验的推测始终需要区分。

            原文第1段

            Studies using electrodes attached to the heads of sleepers have shown that when we sleep, we do so in two ways that alternate throughout the night. The first is rapid eye movement (REM) or active sleep. During this stage our eyes move, even though our eyelids are closed. Our muscles also twitch slightly, though they are largely paralysed so we don't hurt ourselves. In contrast, we also engage in non-REM sleep, during which we barely move at all. Most dream states, and certainly those with the most vivid dreams, happen during REM sleep.

            电极研究表明，人的睡眠在快速眼动与非快速眼动状态之间交替。快速眼动时眼球活动、肌肉可能轻微抽动，但大部分肌肉受到抑制；非快速眼动时身体几乎不动。多数梦境，尤其生动的梦，与快速眼动睡眠相连。本段提供后文比较动物的基础，但most没有把全部梦境都限定在一种状态。

            原文第2段

            There's some evidence that other mammals may also dream. For example, researchers compared the brain patterns of rats running through a maze when awake with their brain patterns during REM sleep. They found the patterns were very similar and concluded that the sleeping rats were dreaming about going through the maze.

            研究者比较老鼠清醒走迷宫时和快速眼动睡眠中的脑活动，发现两者相似，因此推测老鼠可能在梦中重现走迷宫的经历。这里先有脑活动模式的观察，再有对梦内容的解释；开头some evidence和may保留了动物内在体验无法直接验证的限制。

            原文第3段

            But finding evidence of dreaming in non-mammals has proved more difficult. Their brains are very different from those of humans, and it can often be difficult to record their activity while they are sleeping. Recently, however, researchers succeeded in recording brain activity in sleeping pigeons. As in mammals, the recordings revealed both REM and non-REM sleep. Intriguingly, REM sleep activity was high in brain regions involved in processing visual information, especially images related to physical activities such as flying, which suggests that this may possibly be what the pigeons were dreaming about.

            研究非哺乳动物更困难，因为脑结构不同，睡眠中的脑活动也更难记录。鸽子的记录显示两类睡眠状态，并且快速眼动时视觉信息处理区域较活跃，特别涉及飞行等身体活动的影像。作者因此提出可能与相应梦境有关，但suggests、may和possibly层层保留推测，不能直接写成研究人员看到了鸽子的梦。

            原文第4段

            That said, dreaming and REM sleep are unlikely to be universal in the animal kingdom. For example, sponges don't have brains, so they lack the machinery for dreaming. There are also some animals with unusual sleep patterns. These include whales and dolphins, which do not shut down their entire brain when they sleep, but only half of it, keeping the rest awake. They also show no sign of REM sleep, suggesting that they may only experience non-REM dreams, which are less vivid. This is surprising because we tend to think of whales and dolphins as having complex inner lives. It's thought that they don't experience REM sleep because during REM sleep animals are more vulnerable to extremes of temperature.

            That said转向适用范围：梦和快速眼动不太可能遍布所有动物。海绵没有大脑；鲸与海豚只让半侧大脑进入睡眠，文中说它们没有快速眼动睡眠迹象，进而推测可能只有较不生动的非快速眼动梦。末句以It's thought提出一种温度脆弱性的解释，属于学术推测，不是确定且唯一的原因。

            词语与搭配

            alternate throughout the night

            整夜交替出现

            alternate表示两种状态轮流变化，throughout覆盖整个夜间；不意味着只切换一次。

            the most vivid dreams

            最鲜明生动的梦境

            vivid描述体验或画面鲜明，不等于这些梦更真实地反映外部世界。

            recording brain activity

            记录脑活动

            指获取神经活动数据，不能等同于直接读取一段完整主观体验。

            complex inner lives

            复杂的内在精神生活

            inner lives涉及感受、记忆等内在体验；文中是人类对鲸与海豚的通常认识，而非本文逐一证实的内容。

            more vulnerable to extremes of temperature

            更容易受到极端温度影响

            vulnerable to后接潜在威胁；more比较的是不同睡眠状态中的脆弱程度。

            句子精读

            Intriguingly, REM sleep activity was high in brain regions involved in processing visual information, especially images related to physical activities such as flying, which suggests that this may possibly be what the pigeons were dreaming about.

            有趣的是，快速眼动睡眠期间，与处理视觉信息有关的脑区活动较强，尤其涉及飞行等身体活动的影像；这提示，鸽子当时可能梦到的正是这些内容。

            involved in...是过去分词短语修饰brain regions；related to...修饰images；such as flying给出身体活动的例子。which承接前面整个观察，this指相关视觉和身体活动内容。suggests、may possibly都说明从脑活动到梦内容是推断，what...是表语从句，表示鸽子梦到的内容。

            These include whales and dolphins, which do not shut down their entire brain when they sleep, but only half of it, keeping the rest awake.

            这类动物包括鲸和海豚，它们睡觉时并不会让整个大脑都停止清醒活动，而是只让其中一半进入睡眠，让剩下的一半保持清醒。

            These指上文具有特殊睡眠模式的动物。which引导补充说明鲸和海豚的从句；not...but...纠正范围，从整个大脑缩小到半个。it指brain，the rest指另一半；keeping...说明与此同时保持的状态。shut down在这里是通俗叙述，不能机械理解为生理活动完全归零。

            读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

            Do animals dream?｜章鱼行为与研究边界未作答事实判断 TFNG · 6 段 · 400 词 · 8 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

            本材料也用于本册教学。已看过原文、示范或答案时，这次作答用于练习与复习，不作为未见题测试。

            真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 40 页

            Do the following statements agree with the information? TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN。原题Q6–13；NG对照完整原篇后确认，未用裁切缺失信息制造答案。

            原文第5段Nevertheless, in many cases REM sleep does seem to have benefits. Growing evidence from birds and mammals suggests that REM sleep and dreaming are important for forming memories and learning. It is believed that when events are replayed in dreams, this helps to integrate memories into longer-term storage. As soon as animals evolved moderately complex lifestyles, they would have needed to dream in order to manage these lifestyles.

            原文第6段However, we still don't understand how this outward behaviour relates to internal experience. It seems impossible to know what it is like to be a rat or a pigeon, let alone imagine their dreamscapes. We are quick to interpret the twitching limbs and quiet barks of sleeping dogs, but the truth is that we don't know if there is an internal experience of chasing rabbits that comes along with that.

            原文第7段Another non-human dreamer offers insight here. In 2019, while making a documentary, David Scheel of Alaska Pacific University in the USA housed an octopus named Heidi in a tank in his living room. At one point, in the middle of the night, Heidi seemed to dream: her limbs and head moved, and her skin rapidly changed colour, as though she was pursuing a crab.

            原文第8段Similarly, a report recently emerged of a sleeping octopus apparently having a nightmare. Costello, as the octopus was called, thrashed around, extended his mantle as if trying to make himself look bigger, and squirted ink as though he were being attacked by a predator. The nightmare study is intriguing, says Scheel, but is only based on one animal. He argues that as well as outward behaviour, brain imaging is needed to show that the octopuses are replaying sequences of activities from their waking lives in dreams.

            原文第9段The trouble is that we will never be able to experience any animal's dreams. That goes for other humans' dreams too. But we can try to imagine what these dreamscapes are like by meeting animals on their own terms. For example, vision is the dominant sense for many humans, and so our dreams are heavily visual too. Dogs primarily navigate the world using smell while spiders rely much more on vibrations.

            原文第10段It is likely that dreaming has served multiple purposes since the first complex animals evolved. And if this is the case, it is possible that better understanding of these purposes might shed light on the true purpose of our own dreams.

            6. Dreaming about past experiences helps us to create lasting memories of them.

            7. It is now possible to tell what type of dream a dog is having.

            8. David Scheel's documentary was influential on other research into the sleeping patterns of octopuses.

            9. While it was asleep, the octopus called Costello reacted as if it was hunting.

            10. Scheel believes more research into octopuses' dreams should be carried out.

            11. We may soon be able to share the dreams of other human beings.

            12. Hearing may be an important part of the dreams of some animals.

            13. Interest in the reasons why humans dream has increased greatly in recent times.

            对照答案，回到证据

            第 6 题 · TRUE

            replayed events是过去经历，longer-term storage对应lasting memories。

            when events are replayed in dreams, this helps to integrate memories into longer-term storage

            第 7 题 · FALSE

            行为可以被观察，但不知道狗的内部体验，直接否定“现在可以判断梦类型”。

            the truth is that we don't know if there is an internal experience of chasing rabbits

            第 8 题 · NOT GIVEN

            只说明拍摄纪录片时的观察；后续另一报告不等于受其影响，全文没有研究之间的影响关系。

            In 2019, while making a documentary, David Scheel of Alaska Pacific University in the USA housed an octopus named Heidi in a tank in his living room.

            第 9 题 · FALSE

            Costello表现为被捕食者攻击，题干hunting把角色反转；前一只Heidi才像追逐螃蟹。

            as though he were being attacked by a predator

            第 10 题 · TRUE

            需要脑成像来核验行为解释，说明更多研究仍有必要。

            as well as outward behaviour, brain imaging is needed

            第 11 题 · FALSE

            never与soon be able相反，后句明确将结论扩展到其他人类。

            we will never be able to experience any animal's dreams. That goes for other humans' dreams too.

            第 12 题 · NOT GIVEN

            该段举视觉、嗅觉、振动，但没有讨论hearing在梦中的地位；不能自行把振动等同听觉。

            Dogs primarily navigate the world using smell while spiders rely much more on vibrations.

            第 13 题 · NOT GIVEN

            全文谈研究前景，没有比较近期与过去关注度，故不存在increased greatly的依据。

            better understanding of these purposes might shed light on the true purpose of our own dreams

            核对原答案页

            材料精读 · 内容与词句

            文章先提出梦可能帮助记忆与学习，再用章鱼睡眠行为展示观察的吸引力与局限。结尾提醒我们从动物自身的感官世界理解梦，并把跨物种研究作为理解人类梦境的一条可能路径。

            原文第5段

            Nevertheless, in many cases REM sleep does seem to have benefits. Growing evidence from birds and mammals suggests that REM sleep and dreaming are important for forming memories and learning. It is believed that when events are replayed in dreams, this helps to integrate memories into longer-term storage. As soon as animals evolved moderately complex lifestyles, they would have needed to dream in order to manage these lifestyles.

            鸟类和哺乳动物的证据逐渐支持快速眼动与梦对记忆、学习有重要作用。一种解释认为，梦中重现事件有助于把记忆整合到较长期储存中。关于复杂生活方式促使动物需要梦的说法仍带有推断性；it is believed和would have needed都不是对进化过程的直接录像式描述。

            原文第6段

            However, we still don't understand how this outward behaviour relates to internal experience. It seems impossible to know what it is like to be a rat or a pigeon, let alone imagine their dreamscapes. We are quick to interpret the twitching limbs and quiet barks of sleeping dogs, but the truth is that we don't know if there is an internal experience of chasing rabbits that comes along with that.

            However明确区分外在行为与内在体验：我们容易把睡着的狗抽动和轻吠想象成追逐兔子，但其实不知道它是否真的有这种梦境。人甚至难以知道作为老鼠或鸽子的体验是什么样，更不用说具体的梦世界。这段不是否认动物会做梦，而是限制人类解释行为时可以声称知道多少。

            原文第7段

            Another non-human dreamer offers insight here. In 2019, while making a documentary, David Scheel of Alaska Pacific University in the USA housed an octopus named Heidi in a tank in his living room. At one point, in the middle of the night, Heidi seemed to dream: her limbs and head moved, and her skin rapidly changed colour, as though she was pursuing a crab.

            作者引入2019年章鱼Heidi的观察。它睡眠时肢体、头部活动，皮肤迅速变色，看起来像在追螃蟹。seemed和as though表明这是依据行为作出的类比，而不是已确认章鱼确实梦到了某只螃蟹。

            原文第8段

            Similarly, a report recently emerged of a sleeping octopus apparently having a nightmare. Costello, as the octopus was called, thrashed around, extended his mantle as if trying to make himself look bigger, and squirted ink as though he were being attacked by a predator. The nightmare study is intriguing, says Scheel, but is only based on one animal. He argues that as well as outward behaviour, brain imaging is needed to show that the octopuses are replaying sequences of activities from their waking lives in dreams.

            另一只章鱼Costello出现剧烈扭动、伸展外套膜和喷墨，看起来像应对捕食者，因此被描述为可能做噩梦。Scheel认为这很有趣，却指出观察只涉及一只动物，还需要脑成像来支持梦中重演清醒活动的解释。本段将令人印象深刻的个例，与形成更稳固认识所需的证据区分。

            原文第9段

            The trouble is that we will never be able to experience any animal's dreams. That goes for other humans' dreams too. But we can try to imagine what these dreamscapes are like by meeting animals on their own terms. For example, vision is the dominant sense for many humans, and so our dreams are heavily visual too. Dogs primarily navigate the world using smell while spiders rely much more on vibrations.

            作者承认，人无法直接进入其他动物甚至其他人的梦，但可以从物种自己的感官特点出发想象其体验。人类多依赖视觉，狗依赖嗅觉，蜘蛛较依赖振动，因此不能把所有动物的梦都想成一段人类式视觉电影。on their own terms要求尊重不同物种的生活方式。

            原文第10段

            It is likely that dreaming has served multiple purposes since the first complex animals evolved. And if this is the case, it is possible that better understanding of these purposes might shed light on the true purpose of our own dreams.

            结尾提出，梦自复杂动物演化以来可能承担了多种功能；如果如此，更好地理解这些功能也许能帮助理解人类的梦。likely、if、possible和might层层保留条件，作者以开放的研究方向收尾，而没有给出唯一且最终的梦的用途。

            词语与搭配

            forming memories and learning

            形成记忆与学习

            两个动名词并列，说明研究讨论的功能；本段说证据逐渐支持相关作用，并未给出适用于所有物种的统一机制。

            integrate memories into longer-term storage

            把记忆整合进较长期的储存

            integrate...into...表示并入某个系统或结构，longer-term是相对较长期，并非永不遗忘。

            as well as outward behaviour

            除了外在行为以外

            as well as在此补充另一类所需证据，后面提出脑成像；不是说行为观察毫无价值。

            on their own terms

            从它们自身的条件和生活方式出发

            their指动物，强调不要只套用人类的感官经验；此处不是交易或谈判中的条款。
